US Navy aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln has steamed into Thailand's Laem Chabang on Wednesday ⁠with roughly 5,000 sailors and Marines who have spent 286 days at sea.

They arrive amid reports of mental health concerns and deteriorating conditions on board.

The Lincoln was deployed in November last year and was involved in the US naval blockade and combat operations in the war with Iran. It set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea, according to Democratic lawmakers.

Typically naval deployments are for between six and nine months, but ⁠during times of conflict that can be extended.

There's no getting around the fact that Thailand's seaside resort of Pattaya has a lingering reputation for sex tourism, even though that's only part of the story for the city that's an expected shore leave destination of crew members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

open image in gallery Thailand Pattaya Portrait ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

The 5,000 or so sailors and Marines will be following in the wake of millions of other tourists, including a significant number of US military personnel who take part every year in major land and sea exercises nearby with their Thai counterparts.

Social media ahead of the Lincoln's visit has been awash with jibes about lusty sailors, but recent visitors say the development of more family-friendly attractions makes the new Pattaya overshadow its former seedy self.

open image in gallery A tugboat guides US nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) towards Laem Chabang Port, near the city of Pattaya on September 2, 2026 ( AFP/Getty )

Many US Navy ships dock at nearby deep-water facilities such as Laem Chabang Port and the Sattahip Royal Thai Navy Base, both less than an hour away by road.

Shore leave spending boosts the local economy, and mission duties often include community outreach in and around the city, such as specialized medical care for villagers or putting in volunteer time at orphanages.

But when hundreds or thousands of sailors have a chance to enjoy some onshore liberty, the navy deploys members of its Shore Patrol to work side by side with Thai police to defuse any trouble.

Navy personnel are likely to have been reminded that, though rarely enforced, the law in Thailand technically bans prostitution, and paying for sex is a punishable offense under Article 134 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice, the legal framework for the U.S. armed forces.

The military connection goes back at least to the Vietnam War era, when at its height, 40,000-50,000 U.S. service personnel were stationed in Thailand, largely in support of that conflict's air operations. Bases used by U.S. forces dotted Thailand, and all attracted their share of nightlife activities.

Pattaya was close to both the Sattahip naval base and the Thai Navy's U-Tapao airfield, which hosted U.S. Air Force B-52 bombers.

open image in gallery Tourists stroll down Walking Street in Pattaya, Thailand, on Aug. 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Elizabeth Becker, author of "Overbooked: The Exploding Business of Travel and Tourism," wrote that American GIs during the Vietnam War flocked to Pattaya, a once-quiet fishing village, "and it turned into a raunchy seaside playground."

The military facilities brought a continuous stream of personnel through Pattaya, while the 1966 Entertainment Places Act created a legal gray area allowing the sex trade to operate semiopenly in bars and massage parlors — as something of a private arrangement between customer and employee — despite a 1960 law criminalizing prostitution.

Pattaya also had a beach that could be reached relatively easily from Bangkok, which positioned it well for a transition to civilian visitors after the withdrawal of U.S. military forces in 1976.

Pattaya's infrastructure of go-go clubs and other entertainment venues was then marketed to travelers arriving in greater numbers due to cheaper air travel and a boom in package tours. Sex tourism became entrenched.

open image in gallery The USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) aircraft carrier arrives at Laem Chabang Port on September 02, 2026 in Si Racha, Thailand ( Getty )

Severe economic disparities brought many young women and men from Thailand's poor northeastern Isan region to earn wages far exceeding rural agricultural incomes by working in Pattaya's lucrative nightlife sector, allowing them to send money home to their families.

Prostitution is culturally taboo, but sex work has quietly flourished in Thai society for centuries, with the domestic market dwarfing the more glitzy one for foreigners.

open image in gallery Tourists ride a jet ski on Pattaya Beach in Pattaya, Thailand, on Aug. 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Sakchai Lalit) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

Pattaya underwent another evolution in the 1990s, with a new wave of tourists coming from what had been the Soviet Union, after communism there collapsed in late 1991.

Embracing modern globalized tourism, the newcomers came on direct charter flights, even from provincial cities, to the civilian airport at U-Tapao, benefiting from a 30-day visa-free agreement. Signs in Cyrillic sprouted around Pattaya as businesses catered to this new clientele.

Russians were not the only people calling Pattaya their home away from home.

The agreeable climate and allegedly laissez-faire attitude of local law enforcement attracted fugitives from justice and criminals from all over the world, including Russian, Eastern European, and Western European gangsters as well as drug-dealing motorcycle gangs from Australia.

open image in gallery People wait at a bar along a street lined with bars and entertainment venues, in Pattaya City, Thailand, September 1, 2026. REUTERS/Chalinee Thirasupa ( Reuters )

Pattaya has tried with some success this century to rebrand itself as a family destination, with parks, malls and luxury resorts largely in surrounding areas that attract large numbers of Thais and visitors from other Asian nations.

A popular water park is themed around Cartoon Network shows. The Nong Nooch Tropical Botanical Garden displays vast stretches of flora and hosts cultural shows. The Sanctuary of Truth Museum is an ornate all-wood structure over 100 meters (yards) tall.

There are also golf courses, running events and day trips to nearby islands.

Travelers can still get a taste of old Pattaya with a nocturnal stroll down "Walking Street," at the heart of the city's racy nightlife district.

News.title: Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer
News.content:
It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

Julian Alvarez to Barcelona… or Arsenal

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Lamine Camara to Chelsea

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

Ismaila Sarr to Liverpool

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

News.title: Borrowing cost surge leaves Healey with £10bn headache
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs have surged at one of the fastest paces in the world in a move that threatens to blow a near £10bn hole in Chancellor John Healey’s fiscal plans.

Interest rates on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for Treasury borrowing costs, rose to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday amid a global bond market rout.

Britain’s cost to borrow over 20 years rose to its highest level since 1998, signalling growing stress in the market.

Government borrowing costs around the world have climbed sharply in recent weeks, amid concerns about unsustainable debts and persistent inflation.

However, Britain suffered the biggest increase in bond yields in the G7 on Tuesday as economists warned that investors were particularly nervous ahead of Mr Healey’s first Budget.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

Sports.title: Sunderland finally sign Lyon’s Malick Fofana after Crystal Palace tug-of-war with TWO private jets waiting for winger
Sports.content:
SUNDERLAND were the eventual winners of the dramatic deadline day tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

He penned a five-year contract with Regis Le Bris’ side after a deal worth £25.7m plus a potential £5.3m in add-ons, a new club-record, was finally agreed following the transfer rollercoaster.



The Black Cats pounced after Arsenal opted against moving for the winger over the weekend – only for the Eagles to swoop before the star flew to Wearside today.

The North East club had agreed to sign the Belgian international, 21, before Palace also had a similar offer accepted.



That left Fofana with TWO private jets – one bound for Sunderland and the other to London – waiting at Lyon airport to fly him to England but instead he failed to board either.

Palace manager Pierre Sage, who previously coached him at Lyon, was desperate for a reunion with the ace at Selhurst Park.

Fofana evaluated both offers as he instead underwent a medical at a private hospital in France before finally agreeing to move to the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland lodged a deal sheet, giving them an additional two hours to get the deal done, as owner Kyril Louise Dreyfus remained with the player and his representatives in Lyon to ensure there were no further hiccups.

He is now finally due to fly to Sunderland on Wednesday to start life in the Premier League.

Sunderland director of football Florent Ghisolfi said: “Malick has all the attributes to thrive in the Premier League.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“He is a player with huge potential and Sunderland AFC will provide him with the right environment to continue to develop and prosper. He operates off the left and will complement the versatility of the other wide men we have at the club, who can play across both flanks.

“We are delighted to welcome Malick to the club and look forward to supporting him as he takes the next steps in his career.”

Meanwhile, Sunderland also signed Tottenham star Kevin Danso on loan with an obligation to buy the star.

The Black Cats will pay an initial £2,5m loan fee for the Austrian.



That move will become permanent for an additional £22.25m should they avoid relegation this term after the ace, 27, agreed a four-year contract with the option for an additional 12 months.

Danso, who will wear the number 4 shirt and previously worked with Sunderland director of football Florent Ghisolfi at Lens, said: “I’m really happy to be here and I can’t wait to get started.

“Sunderland is a big club with huge ambition, and I’m excited to be part of what we’re building this season.

“I know Florent well from our time together at Lens, so that was an important factor in my decision.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m looking forward to working with him again, meeting my new team-mates and experiencing the atmosphere at the Stadium of Light.”

The Black Cats also snapped up Ecuadorian starlet Juan Riquelme Angulo Caicedo, 18, from Independiente del Valle.

Sports.title: Leeds sign fastest player in Bundesliga history as £25.7m Jean-Matteo Bahoya seals deadline line day transfer
Sports.content:
LEEDS have snapped up the fastest player in Bundesliga history to bolster Daniel Farke’s squad.

Jean-Matteo Bahoya, 21, arrived at Elland Road from Eintracht Frankfurt on an initial season long loan with an obligation to buy for £25.7m.



The signing of the electric French U21 winger paved the way for Italian flanker Willy Gnonto to return to his homeland and join Fiorentina on a season-long loan with an option to buy.

Bahoya is the only player to surpass 37km/h since Bundesliga records began.



For context on Bahoya, Usain Bolt’s average speed when setting the 100m world record in 2009 was 37.58km/h.

Leeds are paying a £1.7m loan fee and will be obliged to pay a further £19.7m, plus £4.3m in potential add-ons, if he triggers a clause in the deal to make it permanent.

Leeds also added versatile French left back Melvin Bard, 25, on a season-long loan from Nice with an option to buy.

Meanwhile, fellow winger Largie Ramazani also departed Leeds.

The 25-year-old Belgian moved to Championship outfit Burnley on an initial season-long loan.

That will become permanent next summer, depending on appearances, for a fee of £6.5m with a potential further £2m in add-ons.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Ramazani, who spent last term on loan at Valencia, said: “It feels amazing. I’m well aware of Burnley as a club from the competition we had a couple of years ago and it’s a great club.

“I know a few of the players here already too, so it’s a really exciting move for me and I’m ready to show what I can do and help Burnley get back to the Premier League.

“I have experience from playing in this league and creating that winning environment, so I’m hoping I can bring something to the team on and off the pitch.”

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho ‘agrees shock free transfer to BRAZIL as ex-Man Utd and Chelsea winger links up with former Prem stars’
Sports.content:
JADON SANCHO has reportedly agreed a shock move to Brazil.

The former England international is currently a free agent following the expiration of his contract with Manchester United.



The winger was linked with moves to Fiorentina and Roma throughout the summer.

The moves to Florence and Rome, however, are said to have fallen through due to his financial demands.



But according to a stunning report, the 26-year-old is on the verge of a surprise move to South America.

That’s according to Marca, who claim the former Aston Villa and Chelsea loanee has agreed to join Serie A side Palmeiras.



Reporter Alfonso Partidor claims the forward has inked a two-year deal with the Verdao.

The agreement is said to include the option of an additional year at the Nubank Parque.

Should Sancho join Palmeiras, they’ll be his FOURTH club in the last three years.

He spent the second half of the 2023/24 season back on loan with Borussia Dortmund.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Manchester United sent him back out on loan with Chelsea for the duration of the following season.

And he spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan with Aston Villa.

His respective stints at Stamford Bridge and Villa Park were successful as he lifted the Conference and Europa League trophies.

A move to Palmeiras will see Sancho link up with former United team-mate Andreas Pereira, who joined the outfit last August following a three-year stint with Fulham.



He’ll also be joined by former West Ham star Felipe Anderson.

Sports.title: Premier League’s most expensive summer transfer XI revealed as English clubs set new record by splurging over £3BILLION
Sports.content:
THE summer transfer window is officially CLOSED.

And Tuesday’s 11pm deadline closed the book on an incredible spending spree from Premier League clubs.



The 20 clubs in England‘s top flight spent over a jaw-dropping £3BILLION bolstering their squads for the season ahead.

The biggest spenders of the window were Manchester City.



New City boss Enzo Maresca dropped a whopping £427MILLION on reinforcements to stop Arsenal from winning a second successive Prem crown.

City’s spending was rivalled by Chelsea and Tottenham, who both spent upwards of £300M.



Some fantastic signings and some questionable ones were made during the window, which opened on June 15.

And SunSport is here to reflect on the biggest deals of a bonkers summer that got heated in more ways than one.

Goalkeepers

One of the biggest stopper signings of the summer was Aston Villa‘s acquisition of Zion Suzuki

The 24-year-old seemed destined to join Italian giants Juventus before Villa swooped in and signed the Japan international, who has inked a five-year contract with the Brummie club, from Parma for a fee of £30m.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Suzuki arrived at Villa Park to replace Argentina international Emi Martinez, who joined Chelsea in a £7.5m deal following a shaky start to the season from Robert Sanchez – who has been shipped off to Como.

Liverpool also splashed the cash on a new keeper, dropping £30m on highly-rated 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans.

Arsenal made a surprise addition to their goalkeeping options, signing former Leeds goalkeeper Ilan Meslier.



The Gunners, however, didn’t have to pay a transfer fee for the Frenchman as he was a free agent following the expiration of his contract at Elland Road.

The biggest stopper signing of the summer, however, was James Trafford‘s move to Leeds, who stumped up a club-record £40m to sign the England international from City.

Defenders

The biggest defensive deal of the summer was undoubtedly done by Liverpool.

The Reds pipped Chelsea to the signature of the highly-rated Jeremy Jacquet in July.



And they paid a premium for his services, agreeing to part with £60m to sign the France Under-21 international from Rennes.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta also broke the bank for a defensive reinforcement.

Eager to bolster his defensive options following injury to William Saliba during the World Cup, he raided Aston Villa for the services of Ezri Konsa.

The defending Prem champions forked out £55m to sign the England international.



Arsenal’s London rivals Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur also spent big in the defensive department.

New Blues boss Xabi Alonso forked out £52m to sign centre-back Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace.

Spurs spent the same sum signing Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton.

Nottingham Forest also spent a pretty penny signing Ousmane Diomande from Sporting Lisbon, with it being understood that the east Midlands club spent £34m to bring the Ivory Coast international to the City Ground.



Midfielders

Manchester City ran away with the spending in the midfield department in their bid to fill the void left by Rodri, who joined Barcelona last month.

Maresca spent a whopping £116m to sign England international Elliot Anderson from Forest.

But they gazumped that figure on deadline day with a staggering £125MILLION deal to sign Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea.

Anderson and Fernandez, 23 and 25 respectively, have inked lucrative five and six-year contracts at the Etihad.



Arsenal also spent big, adding yet more steel to their already stacked midfield, with Arteta dropping £75m on former Newcastle United skipper Bruno Guimaraes.

The Gunners’ raiding of Newcastle’s midfield, however, paled into comparison to that of their bitter rivals Spurs, who spent £100M luring Sandro Tonali away from St James’ Park.

Tottenham, desperate to improve on back-to-back 17th placed finishes, went wild in the midfield department by also signing Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85m.

Manchester United forked out £105m bolstering their midfield with the signings of Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans from Brighton and Aston Villa, respectively.



Forwards

Just as they did last summer, Liverpool were the biggest spenders in the attacking department.

The Reds, who broke the British record transfer fee last summer to sign Alexander Isak, dropped a staggering £123m to sign wantaway winger Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

Chelsea made British transfer history with their £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, which made the winger the most expensive English player in history.

Spurs also spent big in the attacking department with an £85m swoop for Savinho, or Savio as he wants to be referred to since his move to north London, from Manchester City.



They also picked up Omar Marmoush from the Citizens, but won’t pay up for him until next summer when they will have to fork out £60m. On top of those, they also took a punt on Mykhailo Mudryk from Chelsea on loan.

Villa also spent a pretty penny replacing the recently departed Ollie Watkins, dropping £65m to sign Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea.

City spent that figure with a perplexing deadline-day swoop for Iliman Ndiaye from Everton.

Another shock and pricey move was Liam Delap‘s £50m move to Forest just a year after his £30m transfer to Chelsea – where he scored one Premier League goal.

Arsenal, meanwhile, added to their attacking options with their £34m signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge.



Money team

The summer window will go down as one of the craziest of all time.

Tottenham breaking the £100m barrier, Chelsea making a profit on Delap after he managed just one goal last season, Man City paying £116m for Anderson – but the Englishman ending up only their second most expensive midfield signing…

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As football fans know, spending big is no guarantee of success. The only certainty is some teams have signed some big money flops.



Who they are we’ll have to wait and see – but for now we’ve compiled a team of the most expensive summer signings that cost £925MILLION to assemble…

Sports.title: Man City complete British record £125million Enzo Fernandez transfer as he finally leaves Chelsea on deadline day
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has sealed a deadline day move to Manchester City after a mega-money £125million deal was agreed with Chelsea.

City chiefs finally opened club-to-club talks with their Premier League rivals over a swoop for the midfielder, 25, on Monday.



And Fernandez has now reunited with his former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the Etihad Stadium dugout in the summer.

The Cityzens had to race against time to complete the Argentine’s switch before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline – eventually announcing it shortly after the cut-off time.



The clubs reached an agreement to transfer Fernandez for a package which matches the £125M Premier League transfer record that Liverpool paid to sign Alexander Isak.

And the World Cup winner, who has pushed to quit Stamford Bridge since March, has passed a medical and penned a long-term contract at the Etihad Stadium.

Maresca identified Fernandez as a key addition following a number of midfield exits this summer.

Chelsea had expected him to stay after a self-imposed August 14 deadline for bids of £120m came and went without an approach from Manchester.

However, talks accelerated in the final days of the window and he was finally allowed to complete his move.

Fernandez also wrote an emotional goodbye to the Chelsea fanbase, admitting that he had not been in a good place in the build up to his Stamford Bridge exit.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He wrote on social media: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it. This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

“You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best. Always Blue. Thank you, Chelsea.”

Chelsea supremo Xabi Alonso remained tight-lipped when he was quizzed over Fernandez’s future after being left out of the squad to face Brighton on Sunday.



The Spaniard, after being asked if the former Benfica man had made his final appearance for the West Londoners, said: “We’ll see.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we made the decision against Luton and today and anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.

“We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Fernandez sensationally slammed the Chelsea board when Maresca was sacked in January.



He told Mexican broadcaster TUDN: “I don’t understand it. Sometimes there are things that we as players don’t understand, how and in what way they try to manage things.

“Obviously, it was a departure that hurt us a lot especially in the middle of the season, it cuts everything short.

“We had an identity. He gave us an order, even though, as is the way of football, sometimes it’s good and bad.

“But he always had a very clear identity when it came to training and playing.”

Chelsea have put together a five-man shortlist of potential Fernandez replacements, but an approach for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi has already been knocked back.



The Blues thought they had found their man when they agreed a deal for Monaco star Lamine Camara, and already had a medical booked in.

The star had been off the market as Monaco prepared for the departure of his team-mate Folarin Balogun, but the USA international failed his medical and appeared set to stay in France – allowing Chelsea to swoop back in for their target.

But the French side reneged on their agreement after Everton proceeded with a deal for Balogun despite his medical woes under altered terms.



Deals for Bournemouth talisman Alex Scott and Roma’s Manu Kone have also been explored.

Fernandez joined Chelsea for a then-British record £106m in January 2023 and has won the Conference League and Club World Cup at Stamford Bridge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He and his agent, former Argentina international Javier Pastore, made his desire to move public this summer, testing the patience of senior figures at Stamford Bridge.

Real Madrid, who looked into a deal, eventually took the step of publishing a statement to make it clear they would not be pursuing a deal.

Sports.title: ‘Haven’t been in good place’ – Enzo Fernandez bids emotional farewell to Chelsea as he joins Man City in £125m transfer
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has released an emotional farewell statement to Chelsea fans as he sealed his switch to Man City.

The midfielder agreed a move to the Cityzen’s for a joint-record British fee of £125million on deadline day.



And he released a lengthy statement thanking fans for their support and explaining some of the situation that made his final months at the club so tense.

He admitted in the emotional post that the run in to his exit had been a difficult period, and that he hasn’t “been in a good place.”



He wrote: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.



“Life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions.

“I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it. This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

“You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best. Always Blue. Thank you, Chelsea.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Enzo Fernandez statement in full Dear Chelsea, I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place. Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club. Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones. I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart. But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart. But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way. I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution. To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future. Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it. This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that. You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best. Always Blue. Thank you, Chelsea.

The statement was accompanied by a video showing some of Fernandez’s highlights from his time at Stamford Bridge.

The farewell came moments before it was revealed that his apparent replacement, Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, would not be joining the Blues after all.

A deal was agreed and a medical scheduled for the Senegal international, with Monaco sanctioning his departure after Folarin Balogun’s move to Everton appeared to fall through on medical grounds.

But Everton revisited the negotiating table and hammered out a deal for the stricken star, causing Monaco to renege on their agreement with Chelsea and decide to hold on to Camara.

It was a rocky exit for Fernandez, who drew ire from the fans when he appeared to hint that he would be interested in a move to Real Madrid earlier this summer.



That transfer never materialised, but his former boss Enzo Maresca did swoop in to add him to his City squad.

The monster fee equals the record-breaking £125m that Liverpool paid for Alexander Isak last summer.

Sports.title: Arsenal owners buy new sport team for £3BILLION but Gunners fans rage at timing of deal on transfer deadline day
Sports.content:
ARSENAL owners Kroenke Sports Entertainment have purchased Major League Baseball franchise the Los Angeles Angels.

The company, fronted by businessman Stan Kroenke, reportedly agreed a deal in the region of £3BILLION to purchase the Angels, who are currently struggling at the bottom of the American League West.



But Arsenal fans are fuming at the timing of the new announcement, which arrived on a quiet Premier League transfer deadline day for the Gunners.

Founder Kroenke and his son Josh have financed some big deals this summer, including the £75million addition of Bruno Guimaraes and the £55m arrival of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.



But fans in North London are still unhappy with a perceived lack of action from their billionaire owners.

Kroenke, 79, has a hand in a number of sporting enterprises.

As well as Arsenal and the Angels, his company has stakes in the NFL‘s Los Angeles Rams, NHL outfit the Colorado Avalanche and MLS side Colorado Rapids.

But Arsenal fans were seemingly not delighted to see him add another organisation to his list of assets.

One fan responded to the news: “Kroenke buying a new team before an attacking signing.”

Another complained: “Is this what they are doing with all our transfer money?”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

A third fan quipped: “Well they did something on transfer deadline day I guess.”

And a fourth added: “That’s what we did on deadline day folks.”

Fans at the Emirates had hoped to see Atletico Madrid superstar Julian Alvarez sign after a drawn out battle with Barcelona.



The Argentine star dreamed of a move to the Catalan side, but his team refused to sanction an agreement with their fierce rivals.

However Arsenal were not able to capitalise on the opportunity, and were left with Christos Tzolis as their only major attacking signing of the summer window.

Chelsea star Malo Gusto was reportedly wanted by Liverpool on transfer deadline day, but a deal never seemingly got close to being completed. Gusto’s future has been the subject of speculation throughout the summer transfer window, with fresh reports emerging hours before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline.

‌



Reports in recent weeks have been suggesting that some members of the Chelsea squad could head for the exit door at Stamford Bridge, notably Enzo Fernandez, who is closing in on a £125million switch to Manchester City.

‌

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus makes honest Julian Alvarez admission after leaving Arsenal for Barcelona

Gabriel Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barcelona, where he's become their alternative to Julian Alvarez, after leaving Arsenal in a deal worth £12.85million

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus spoke honestly at his unveiling by Barcelona (Image: Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has admitted he isn't bothered about being Barcelona's second choice after Julian Alvarez following his transfer from Arsenal.

‌



Jesus has signed a three-year contract with Barca, who agreed to pay the Gunners a fee which could reach £12.85million. The Brazilian entered the final year of his deal in north London and Mikel Arteta made it clear that he didn't feature in his plans for the 2026/27 season.

‌



He was frozen out of the first-team set-up along with Gabriel Martinelli and has now landed on his feet in Barcelona. The Catalan giants had wanted to sign Alvarez instead, but Atletico Madrid released a statement to publicly state they wouldn't do business with their La Liga rivals after growing irritated by their interest.

‌



Jesus rejected a move to Napoli and his decision ended up paying dividends, with a dream transfer to Barca the result. "A week ago I received a message that it could happen," he said at his unveiling. "When I started to think it was a real possibility, I was so excited. Now I can't wait to start training and playing.

"It doesn't annoy me [being Plan B to Alvarez], it doesn't bother me. What annoys me is if people say I'm a bad guy, which has never happened in my life - or if I am not playing football, that bothers me.

‌



"I have the chance to play for Barcelona, a chance I had 10 years ago and now life has offered me that opportunity again."

Jesus joined Arsenal from Manchester City in 2022 for £45million, but his time in Arteta's side never really worked out. He slipped behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres in the pecking order and leaves having scored 32 goals in 123 appearances for the Gunners.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez looks set to stay at Atletico Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images)

‌



"I took a significant salary drop, but it's a dream to be here," Jesus added. "But it wasn't just me who had to make an effort to get the transfer over line, Barca also played their part.

"If you had asked me one month ago, I would have said it was unlikely this would happen. At 29, I didn't think I would have the chance to come to Barca."

He made 27 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal last season after recovering from a cruciate ligament knee injury. But after a summer of training he feels ready to hit the ground running for Hansi Flick's side, who needed a replacement for Robert Lewandowski.

Article continues below

"The last two years have been really complicated after the knee injury," Jesus said. "I was out of the game for almost one year, but it's in the past. I feel good physically now. I recovered well, returned to action for Arsenal and I am 100 per cent ready to play and give my all."

Sports.title: Man Utd in talks to sign ANOTHER midfielder before the transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Man Utd in talks to sign ANOTHER midfielder before the transfer deadline

Manchester United appeared set for a quiet transfer deadline day, but they are now working on a deal to bring in their fourth midfielder of the window before 11pm

View 2 Images Louis Page could leave Leicester for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are in talks with Leicester City over the signing of midfielder Louis Page. United have already signed three central midfielders in the summer transfer window, but could make it four before Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

‌



Michael Carrick's side have spent a combined £155million this summer to bring in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba. Remodelling the midfield was the priority for the club, who may forgo the left-back Carrick also wanted.

‌



It has appeared as though landing competition for Luke Shaw was the only possible incoming deal on deadline day. But United are now in pole position to sign Page from Leicester, having overtaken Arsenal.

‌



The 18-year-old midfielder has progressed from the Foxes' under-21s side to the senior team and has made four appearances for Russell Martin's team this season. He is understood to be keen on a move to Old Trafford, but there is no agreement in place yet, with Leicester demanding more than £8million for his signature.

Leicester hosting Plymouth at the King Power Stadium on Tuesday night is another potential barrier to the deal being completed in time.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

As our sister title Manchester Evening News reports, it is possible that Page could be loaned straight back to Leicester if the deal goes ahead. Leicester are playing in League One this season following relegation and United may be happy to see Page getting regular game time, rather than in their under-21s squad.

United have been interested in Page since early August and Leicester boss Martin has already addressed his potential exit. “Louis is a really fantastic young player," he told Sky Sports.

‌



"Obviously, I know the director of football [Jason Wilcox] at Manchester United very well after spending some time with Southampton. We haven't actually spoke on Louis because he probably knows what I'd say to him and tell him to go away!

View 2 Images Louis Page has attracted interest from Arsenal and Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

"Until something comes in that is really brilliant for the club and player and everyone is happy, then Louis stays and he's in the squad. I’m really enjoying working with him, he's a fantastic young player.”

‌



United manager Carrick tried to downplay the possibility of movement on deadline day following the 5-2 thrashing of Ipswich on the weekend.

"It's always difficult to say to be honest, when there's so little time left," Carrick said. "I think the business we've managed to do, I'm pleased with - we're a better group, a better squad and potentially a better team. Adding Marcus [Rashford] into that feels like a new signing.

"In that respect, we're quite happy but we're always hoping that if there's something else to add, I wouldn't shut that down. As it stands, we'll have to wait and see."

Sports.title: Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list
Sports.content:
Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list

Chelsea are still in the hunt for a replacement as Manchester City attempt to sign Enzo Fernandez from the Blues and have identified five options

View 2 Images Chelsea are on the outlook for an Enzo Fernandez replacement (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Chelsea have a five-man shortlist to replace Enzo Fernandez on transfer deadline day that includes players from Arsenal and Tottenham. The Blues are working at finding a midfield signing who can arrive should the Argentina star leave Stamford Bridge in the coming hours.

‌



Fernandez could complete a momentous deadline day transfer to Manchester City before Tuesday's 11pm deadline, and become the first player to have commanded more than £100million twice.

‌



Chelsea's efforts so far have focused on landing Monaco ace Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Kone. They have so far been able to reach an agreement, with a £38.5m bid for Camara rejected, while Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini does not want Kone sold.

‌



Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Xabo Alonso has three more players on the club's shortlist, however, and all are closer to home. talkSPORT reports that Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi, Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall and Morgan Gibbs-White of Nottingham Forest are also under consideration.

Despite the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes to the Emirates this summer, Mikel Arteta suggested that Zubimendi was not available for sale. "No, he’s a really important player. He’s a really important player for us," Arteta said recently.

‌



"Zubi without a doubt was one of the best players for Arsenal last season. Without him we would never get into the position that we got in the last few weeks and he deserves massive credit.

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi is on Chelsea's shortlist (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

"We spoke a lot in pre-season. He's a top player, a top potential player. I like he stays, but I think now he wants to stay and we have no problem."

Sports.title: Man Utd’s private Lewis Hall transfer plan as Newcastle confirm price tag
Sports.content:
Man Utd’s private Lewis Hall transfer plan as Newcastle confirm price tag

Manchester United have put a new left-back at the top of their shopping list on deadline day with Newcastle’s Lewis Hall having emerged as a standout option for the Red Devils

View 2 Images Lewis Hall looks unlikely to be moving to Old Trafford for the time being (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United could be forced to delay their move for Lewis Hall after learning of Newcastle's eye-watering £75m price tag. The Red Devils are keen to add a new left-back to their squad this summer.

‌



Luke Shaw is currently Michael Carrick’s only senior option in the position, with academy graduate Harry Amass available as back-up. But the youngster could potentially be available on deadline day, with Burnley ready should United allow him to leave.

‌



Hall, 21, has emerged as a standout option for United chiefs, albeit a deal is not expected to be cheap. According to Mail Online, Newcastle want to receive around £75m for the four-time England defender, a price tag that has proven prohibitive so far.

‌



That has led to United chiefs having to be creative with their pursuit. It is suggested that they will now delay a big-money swoop for Hall and will instead look to sign him next summer instead.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



It is not the first time that the Red Devils have had to put a deal on the back-burner. They were also pursuing a move for Carlos Baleba last season, albeit felt his price was too high so delayed for 12 months and eventually managed to secure his signature at a more reasonable price.

United’s decision comes after legendary former midfielder Paul Scholes urged the club to re-evaluate their interest in Hall. Asked if boss Michael Carrick would be keen on defensive additions, he replied: “100 per cent. That will have been going on for months, you’re not just talking the last couple of days.

“Do you know one thing that might help Michael? Luke Shaw getting done yesterday [against Ipswich] like he did. So he might go, ‘Look, we need him’, and you think Lewis Hall might be the most doable who is out there and available.

‌



“You would have thought some work on that has been done. The amount of rumours there have been, you would have thought some work on that has been done.

View 2 Images Man United had previously looked at Alejandro Balde (Image: Getty Images)

“It doesn’t feel like they’re going to do anything does it? Lewis Hall was floated about for a bit.

‌



“I don’t think it’s going to happen and this is why United are going to be United again: we’re probably not much different from last year and not much different from the last five years.

“They can look devastating at times but at times they’ll look like they did in the first half [against Ipswich] where they concede goals.

“Look, it’s no surprise, who is shocked? You’ve got the same back-four you’ve had for five years. What’s going to change?”

Article continues below

The Red Devils had a number of alternatives to Hall during the window including Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and Racing Santander’s Jorge Salinas.

Sports.title: Portsmouth legend Alan Knight dies aged 65 as tributes pour in for club icon
Sports.content:
Portsmouth legend Alan Knight dies aged 65 as tributes pour in for club icon

Portsmouth have paid tribute to club legend Alan Knight, who played for Pompey in all four professional divisions across four different decades before later returning as a coach

View 2 Images Alan Knight, who was a legendary goalkeeper for Portsmouth, has passed away (Image: Getty Images)

Portsmouth have confirmed the death of Alan Knight at the age of 65. The club legend died this morning, surrounded by his close family, after a battle with prostate cancer.

‌



Knight made his diagnosis public in October 2024, encouraging others to get tested should they notice any symptoms and raising awareness of the disease. The club helped raise £40,000 for prostate cancer charities last May with an Alan Knight XI drawing 8-8 with a Pompey Legends side at Fratton Park.

‌



He played 801 times for Portsmouth. Knight made more appearances for one club than any other goalkeeper in football history.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Pompey's statement says: "The word legend is often overused in football, but the fact that Alan was still known as 'The Legend' at Pompey more than 20 years after hanging up his gloves speaks volumes. He will be sadly missed by the Fratton faithful, teammates and all of us at the club who knew and loved him.

"Our thoughts are with Alan's wife Heather, his daughters Jade and Rebekah, and all his family and friends at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, The Legend."

‌



The club also say they are setting up a book of condolence at Fratton Park.

View 2 Images Alan Knight, played 801 times for Portsmouth, has passed away

Born in the Balham area of south-east London, Knight joined Portsmouth aged 14 as an apprentice. He debuted two years later on the final day of the 1977/78 season and kept a clean sheet against Rotherham United as Pompey finished bottom of the Third Division.

‌



Knight played from them in all four professional divisions, winning promotion three times, including to the top flight in 1986/87. The goalkeeper also helped Portsmouth reach the FA Cup semi-finals in 1992.

They took the eventual champions Liverpool to a replay and only bowed out on penalties. Knight made his final appearance aged 38 in January 2000.

Knight went on to play three times for for Havant & Waterlooville before becoming Portsmouth's goalkeeping coach. He also worked in the same capacity for Aldershot Town, Bournemouth, the Major League Soccer side Dallas, Dorchester Town, Havant & Waterlooville and Horndean.

A short-term return to Portsmouth followed in 2013 under Guy Whittingham after leaving Dorchester. Later that same year he was appointed a club ambassador.

Sports.title: 'I know what I have to work on' - Fery ready to take on best despite US Open exit
Sports.content:
Britain's Arthur Fery said he now knows what he has to work on after his US Open debut was cut short on Tuesday.

His hopes of making a splash in New York were ended in the first round after a straight-sets defeat by Lorenzo Musetti.

The 24-year-old had been riding the crest of a wave since his historic run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wildcard earlier this summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fery hit this tweener in a superb rally against Musetti

He reached his first ATP final at the Winston-Salem Open last week and arrived at Flushing Meadows with high hopes of another deep run at the Grand Slam.

But he ran aground against Italian 13th seed Musetti in a straight-sets loss on Grandstand Stadium.

It was a comprehensive defeat, but a useful gauge for Fery who has risen from outside the top 200 a year ago to No 33 in the world.

"I know what I have to work on," he said. "I got a lot of ideas coming straight off the court of what I have to work on to do better.

"My serve really let me down today, which is not usually the case, but I've been struggling a little bit to find my rhythm on the serve.

"Today was particularly a struggle, but definitely playing guys at that level, it's tough and the margins are small."

Fery, now the British No 1, was close to being seeded at Flushing Meadows, meaning he would have avoided a player of Musetti's class in the early stages.

He admitted he was under-prepared due to his run in North Carolina last week, but said he would not have done things differently.

"The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments and everyone has their eye on them." he added. "At the same time, would I sign for these past two weeks? Probably, to be honest.

"It's a lot of ranking points, it's a first ATP final, so it's good. Even though it meant that my preparation for the US Open was not great."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Harrison believes more players will now know how to play against Fery since his recent success but believes being exposed could also be a blessing in disguise

'Learning curve for Fery'

Image: Fery sees areas of his game which he wants to improve

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman said Fery will take "an enormous amount" from his defeat and will gain vital experience.

The former British No 1 said: "What he lacks right now is experience at the highest level. He's 33 in the world and hasn't played a great deal of tennis outside the UK at this level.

"To come up against Musetti, who is a world-class player, has been five in the world and reached semi-finals of Grand Slams, provides clear evidence of what he needs to work on."

Asked where Fery can improve his game, Henman said: "He's got to continue to give himself opportunities to finish points at the net.

"His forehand side, in these types of [hot] conditions, he can perhaps take the ball a bit earlier and get more penetration through the court.

"He can work on that first serve to get a bit more pace, which is not easy because he's not the tallest of players, but then he's got to improve that accuracy."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Harrison analysed Fery's game ahead of his US Open debut

Robson: Musetti too good for Fery

Laura Robson said: "Musetti was too good. He had that extra gear to go to with his pace off the racquet and his ability to open up the lines made such a big difference.

"Fery will be a little disappointed that he wasn't able to hang in that first set. That could have changed the course of the match.

"But he came up against such a good opponent."

Sports.title: Balogun walks away from Everton deal
Sports.content:
Everton's move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has fallen through after a change of heart from the player - after the deal scuppered Chelsea's chances of signing Lamine Camara.

Balogun arrived on Merseyside at lunchtime to complete the £40m Deadline Day transfer, but doubts then started to emerge about the deal being completed during the afternoon as the medical threw up an issue.

As a result of this issue, Monaco then proceeded with a move to sell midfielder Camara. But in another twist, Everton renegotiated the terms of the deal for Balogun - which forced a dramatic move from Monaco.

With a full agreement to sell Camara to Chelsea in place, Monaco withdrew from the deal as the 11pm transfer deadline passed, which left the Blues furious.

Chelsea also had the chance to withdraw from the £125m move to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City, but chose not to out of good faith.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to rivals Manchester City despite the last-minute collapse of their deal to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco.

But just after midnight on Wednesday, it was revealed Balogun had a change of heart about moving to Everton and walked away from the deal - which will only infuriate Monaco and Chelsea even more.

It also means Balogun's dramatic 2026 continues - after the American international was at the centre of the World Cup red card storm involving Donald Trump.

It leaves Everton with just one recognised senior striker until January in Thierno Barry, after Beto left for Fiorentina and Manchester United rejected a loan offer for Joshua Zirkzee.

Everton's attacking options were further diminished by the departure of Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City, but they did sign Jack Grealish on another loan deal.

The Balogun drama in chronological order

Everton agree fee with Monaco for Folarin Balogun.

Balogun arrives on Merseyside for medical and to complete formalities of the move.

Chelsea have multiple bids rejected by Monaco for Lamine Camara. They consider other targets.

Chelsea agree deal to sell Enzo Fernandez to Man City for £125m. Comfortable with the options in their squad if no one comes in.

Doubts emerge around Everton's deal for Balogun.

Everton make an offer to sign Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United on loan with an option to buy.

Chelsea agree deal with Monaco for Lamine Camara, due to the doubts about the Balogun deal.

Manchester United reject Everton's loan offer for Zirkzee.

Everton grow in confidence that they can get Balogun over the line after renegotiating with Monaco.

Chelsea's deal to sign Camara collapses after Monaco withdraw from the deal. The Balogun deal being back on satisfied their need for a sale.

Balogun had a change of heart and walked away from the deal after a deal sheet was submitted.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

'Chelsea are really unhappy'

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol on Chelsea's Lamine Camara's Chelsea move breaking down:

"Chelsea have not been able to sign a replacement for Enzo Fernandez. Chelsea are really unhappy with the way Monaco behaved.

"My information is everything was done - written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London [on Wednesday].

"At the same time, Monaco have been negotiating with Everton to sell Folarin Balogun. Once they have agreed a deal with Everton, they have come back to Chelsea and gone back on their agreement.

"Chelsea don't believe this is the way clubs should conduct business. I suppose this is one of the risks you take when you leave things so late."

Sports.title: Deal off! Monaco pull out of selling Fernandez replacement Camara to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Monaco have pulled out of the deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea - who feel the French club have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way.

Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was to sign a six-year deal pending a medical.

Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

The reason for Monaco pulling out was that they had successfully renegotiated the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton, but the striker sensationally backed out of the move at the very last minute.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett explains why the collapse of the Folarin Balogun deal leaves Everton short of strikers for the season.

Monaco only wanted to sell one player, and once they thought they had a deal agreed to sell Balogun to Everton, they pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal despite a full written club-to-club agreement with the Blues.

Monaco refused to sign a Camara deal sheet before the 11pm deadline, and there is no chance of Chelsea resurrecting a deal for the Senegal international.

The feeling at Chelsea towards Monaco now is likely to be "what goes around comes around".

Chelsea had been looking for a new midfielder with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City in a joint-British-record £125m deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Ransom reports that finally Enzo Fernandez has completed his £125m move from Chelsea to Man City on a five-year deal.

Chelsea had the option of pulling the plug on Fernandez's move to Man City after the Camara deal had collapsed, but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal.

Roma's Manu Kone was also shortlisted as a potential option, while Chelsea were also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

'Chelsea are really unhappy'

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"Enzo Fernandez is going to be a Manchester City player. Lamine Camara to Chelsea collapsing is totally separate.

"Chelsea have not been able to sign a replacement. Chelsea are really unhappy with the way Monaco behaved.

"My information is everything was done - written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London [on Wednesday].

"At the same time, Monaco have been negotiating with Everton to sell Folarin Balogun. Once they have agreed a deal with Everton, they have come back to Chelsea and gone back on their agreement.

"Chelsea don't believe this is the way clubs should conduct business. I suppose this is one of the risks you take when you leave things so late."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

Who has left Chelsea on Deadline Day?

Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como.

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa.

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg. Essugo was of interest to Hull in this window.

Striker Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to Strasbourg. He signed from Santos for £17.1m three years ago but made only three appearances.

Forward Dujuan Richards has also joined Wimbledon on a season-long loan.

Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow ahead of his loan move to Celtic, who are also working to finalise a deal for Chelsea left-back Landon Emenalo.

Sports.title: Sunderland complete Fofana signing after dramatic saga
Sports.content:
Sunderland have finally completed the signing of Lyon winger Malick Fofana after a dramatic Deadline Day transfer saga involving two private jets and the player changing his mind multiple times.

Sunderland agreed a deal to sign Fofana on Deadline Day morning but Crystal Palace - whose manager Pierre Sage worked with him before at Lyon - tried to hijack the deal.

With both Premier League clubs agreeing a deal with Lyon for the winger, Fofana was then sat at Lyon airport, with two private jets waiting on him to make a decision. One plane was set for Sunderland, the other was set for London.

Fofana also took one medical in Lyon on Deadline Day that both teams had access to.

But just over an hour to go until the deadline, Fofana eventually chose Sunderland with Black Cats owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus travelling to Lyon to convince the player to join.

Fofana's move to Sunderland consists of an initial £25.7m with £5.14m in add-ons.

Arsenal were also considering a move for Fofana over the weekend but did not make a move for the player.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

How a dramatic Deadline Day panned out

10:47am: After Arsenal did not take up the chance to sign Fofana, Sunderland agreed a deal with Lyon for the winger worth up to £30m.

1:01pm: Crystal Palace try to hijack Sunderland's five-year deal for Fofana by entering in direct communication with the player in an attempt to convince him to join them.

3:18pm: Crystal Palace agree a deal with Lyon for Fofana. Sunderland begin talks with fellow Belgium winger Dodi Lukebakio on top of the Fofana deal.

3.42pm: Fofana is at Lyon airport with two private jets waiting on him to make a decision - one bound for Sunderland and another for London.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Keith Downie explains how Lyon winger Malick Fofana had the choice of TWO private jets to the UK to seal a move to a Premier League club!!

8:24pm: Sunderland owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus visits Lyon to try and persuade Fofana to choose Sunderland over Palace. The player effectively undergoes one medical for both teams.

9:38pm: Sunderland's attempts to sign Benfica's Lukebakio end as a decision is made for him to remain with the Portuguese club.

9:50pm: Fofana gives Sunderland the green light after changing his mind multiple times throughout the day. The price of the deal rises to £30.8m.

10:54pm: Sunderland submit a deal sheet to get the Fofana deal over the line.

12:15am: Sunderland announce the Fofana deal

Sports.title: Koivun handed shock Team USA debut as Presidents Cup picks revealed
Sports.content:
Jackson Koivun has been handed a Team USA debut for this month's Presidents Cup, just months after turning professional, as former world No 1 Jason Day missed out on a spot in the International Team.

Koivun enjoyed a glittering amateur career before turning professional after the US Open in June, with the 21-year-old winning the PGA Tour's 3M Open three starts later and qualifying for the season-ending FedExCup Playoffs.

He will become the youngest American to feature at the Presidents Cup since Jordan Spieth in 2015 after being named among Brandt Snedeker's six captain's picks for this year's edition at Medinah Country Club, where Team USA chase a record-extending 11th consecutive victory in the biennial contest.

Koivun was one of three debutants named among Snedeker's selections, revealed in a live TV show on Tuesday, with Chris Gotterup - a three-time PGA Tour winner this season - and Genesis Invitational champion Jacob Bridgeman also included.

"It's rare to see a player this young demonstrate the level of poise and confidence that Jackson has, even before turning professional," Snedeker said. "His maturity and work ethic have always stood out. He's already proven he can win on the biggest stage in golf on the PGA Tour, and I'm excited to watch him perform in his first team event."

Image: Jackson Koivun has been handed a Presidents Cup debut for Team USA

Snedeker elected to pick experience to complete the rest of his 12-man line-up, with stalwarts Xander Schauffele, Justin Thomas and Patrick Cantlay all recalled for fourth Presidents Cup appearances.

Ben Griffin and last year's US Open winner JJ Spaun were among the high-profile players to miss out for Team USA, while Gary Woodland will remain a captain's assistant despite winning the Texas Children's Houston Open in March and adding five top-10s since on the PGA Tour.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of the Texas Children's Houston Open, where Gary Woodland won for the first time since the 2019 US Open

Day was the highest-ranked player in the International Team qualification rankings not to earn a captain's spot from Geoff Ogilvy, with the Australian struggling for form and fitness during a season where he failed to qualify for the FedExCup Playoffs for the first time since 2007.

Sungjae Im returns for a fourth appearance for the International Team, while Corey Conners will feature for a third time after narrowly missing out on an automatic pick.

Sports.title: Man City sign Fernandez in British-record-equalling deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City have signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-British-record fee of £125m.

The size of the fee matches the amount Liverpool paid Newcastle for Alexander Isak on Deadline Day a year ago. The Argentine midfielder has signed a five-year deal at the Etihad Stadium.

The Fernandez deal comes amid Chelsea fury that Monaco pulled out of selling Lamine Camara - who was deemed as the Argentine's replacement - in the final minutes of the window.

Chelsea had the option of pulling the plug on Fernandez to Man City after the Camara deal collapsed - but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol explains why Chelsea sold Enzo Fernandez to rivals Manchester City despite the last-minute collapse of their deal to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco.

Fernandez's Deadline Day move comes more than three months after the Argentina international first told Chelsea he wanted to leave, and more than two weeks after the club imposed a deadline for bids.
