Chelsea will make a £18m profit on the midfielder they signed for £107m three-and-a-half years ago, and Fernandez is now reunited with his former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca.

"Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times," said Fernandez after making the move.

"Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes the signing of Enzo Fernandez will make Man City Arsenal's biggest title challenger

"I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

"If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

"I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who's worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I'm here."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Re-live all the thrills and spills from Transfer Deadline Day on Sky Sports News.

Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was going to sign a six-year deal pending a medical.

Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

The reason for Monaco pulling out was due to the French club successfully renegotiating the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton only for the USA international to sensationally walk away from the deal.

There was a full written club-to-club agreement with Chelsea to complete the Camara deal and the Premier League club feels Monaco have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way.

Fernandez sends farewell message to Chelsea

Enzo Fernandez in his Chelsea farewell Instagram message:

Dear Chelsea,

I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven't been in a good place.

Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I've said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

Always Blue.

Thank you, Chelsea. 💙

Enzo.

Sports.title: Fernández completes record-equalling £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City
Sports.content:
Manchester City have equalled the British transfer record with a £125m deal to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea, who were left raging after their attempts to replace the Argentina midfielder were dashed by Monaco reneging on an agreement to sell Lamine Camara last night.

On a day of twists and turns, City emerged in a strong position after they bolstered their attack by signing Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for up to £65m and landed one of Enzo Maresca’s biggest targets on a five-year deal. Chelsea held out for a huge fee for Fernández and it seemed they were going to find a replacement for him as the transfer window drew to a close.

The club moved to agree a £47m fee with Monaco for Camara, who was set to sign a six-year contract with the option of an extra year. Chelsea swooped when Everton’s attempts to sign the USA striker Folarin Balogun ran into difficulties. It left Monaco needing to raise funds from elsewhere, prompting Chelsea to revive their move for Camara after having a £38.1m offer for the 22-year-old Senegal midfielder rejected earlier in the day.

Chelsea had a written agreement with Monaco but were stunned by the Ligue 1 club pulling out of the deal as the deadline approached. Sources called Monaco’s conduct “deeply unprofessional”. As an extraordinary situation developed it emerged that Everton, who have also loaned Jack Grealish from City, had refused to give up on Balogun, renegotiating the fee for the former Arsenal forward only for that deal to also fall down just after midnight.

The collapse of Camara’s move did not lead to Chelsea cancelling the sale of Fernández to City. The deal means City have spent £327m on midfielders this summer following the arrivals of Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £86m.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success,” said Fernández, who becomes this country’s most expensive player alongside Alexander Isak, who joined Liverpool from Newcastle for £125m a year ago. “I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who’s worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I’m here.”

View image in fullscreen Iliman Ndiaye also completed his move to Manchester City on a busy deadline day for sporting director Hugo Viana. Photograph: Manchester City FC

Maresca has a good relationship with Fernández after coaching him at Chelsea and a reunion has been on the cards for a while. City opened talks with Chelsea on Monday night and will feel they have successfully rebuilt their midfield after selling Rodri to Barcelona and losing Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid, while also selling Nico González to Newcastle. They were also not put off even after Chelsea’s unofficial deadline for clubs to lodge bids of £120m for Fernández passed last month.

Fernández has been angling for a way out of Chelsea since March and his departure was announced in a short statement on the club’s website. The 25-year-old, who scored 31 goals after joining from Benfica for £106.7m in January 2023, initially had his sights set on joining Real Madrid. He grew disillusioned following Maresca’s acrimonious split with Chelsea earlier this year. Fernández, the unofficial vice-captain, spoke out after Chelsea were knocked out of the Champions League by Paris Saint-Germain in March. Chelsea responded by banning him for two games.

Fernández reported back to training after the World Cup and was booed by Chelsea fans during a pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge. He featured in the club’s opening first game of the season, coming off the bench to help Xabi Alonso’s side beat Fulham, but was left out of Chelsea’s next two fixtures.

Chelsea came round to the view a sale was in their interests. There is a feeling within the club that Fernández, who won the Conference League and Club World Cup during his time in west London, had not shown himself to be vice-captain material.

Chelsea have made in the region of £500m in loans and sales this summer. They finished the window by selling Marc Guiu to RB Leipzig for £16m and loaning Dário Essugo to Strasbourg, Robert Sánchez to Como and Mykhailo Mudryk to Tottenham. Tosin Adarabioyo joined Spurs on a permanent deal.

Sports.title: Everton left with only one striker after Balogun deal collapses late on deadline day
Sports.content:
Everton’s £40m move for US international Folarin Balogun collapsed late on deadline day to leave manager David Moyes with only one striker for the first half of the season.

Everton had agreed a £40m deal for Balogun only for issues with the striker’s medical to place the transfer in doubt after the Merseyside club had sold Beto to Fiorentina and Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City. Enquiries were made to Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee and Aston Villa for Tammy Abraham but proposed loans for both forwards were rejected.

The structure of the deal was renegotiated late on – Monaco agreed to accept a lower payment up front and more in add-ons – and Everton submitted a deal sheet to complete the transfer in time. But the 25-year-old is said to have changed his mind over the move and walked away at the final moment. The collapse of the deal leaves Thierno Barry as Everton’s one recognised striker and completed a shambolic end to the window by the club’s hierarchy, who were already under pressure having tried to sell Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.

Everton also hit problems in their attempts to sign right-back Kenny Tete from Fulham. A £9m deal had been agreed for the defender only for Fulham to fail to land their preferred replacement, Andrei Ratiu of Rayo Vallecano. Everton finally concluded their long-running search for a right-back by signing former Arsenal player Ainsley Maitland-Niles from Lyon for a fee of around £4.2m. The 29-year-old has agreed a three year contract.

Funds were raised by the sales of Ndiaye to City, for £60m plus £5m in add-ons, Beto to Fiorentina for £15.5m, Tim Iroegbunam to Hull for an initial £15m and Nathan Patterson to Torino for an undisclosed fee.

Grealish returns to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on another season loan from City. The 30-year-old enjoyed a productive spell on loan in 2025-26 before sustaining a fractured foot that ended his campaign in February.

Grealish, who will be out of contract at City when this latest deal ends next summer, could make his second Everton debut against Manchester United on Sunday. He said: “I’m so happy. I think I’m at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That’s what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me. Every time I see an Everton fan, it’s just pure love.

“It means a lot to me and hopefully I’ve made a few Everton fans happy. I had a perfect time here for the first six months, then I stayed around after I got injured. I’ve been watching all the Everton games in pre-season and since the season started. Now I feel ready to go.”

Sports.title: Sunderland pip Crystal Palace in battle of the private jets to land Malick Fofana
Sports.content:
Sunderland and Crystal Palace were involved in an extraordinary deadline-day tug of war that concluded with Malick Fofana agreeing to swap Lyon for the Stadium of Light in a club-record £31m move.

On Tuesday morning it had seemed that the 21-year-old Belgium winger was heading for Sunderland on a five-year contract, but then Pierre Sage led an attempt to hijack the deal. Palace’s manager coached Fofana at Lyon and forged a strong bond with a player he was keen to bring to Selhurst Park. After speaking to Sage on the phone, Fofana seemed to have changed his mind and decided he wanted to reunite with his old boss in south London. Sunderland, though, refused to surrender.

That meant Lyon had a bidding war on their hands and responded by agreeing improved deals with both clubs. Agents’ fees and Fofana’s personal terms were also understood to have risen accordingly. Meanwhile, two private jets, one dispatched by Sunderland and the other by Palace, sat on the tarmac at Lyon airport.

At one point Fofana was said to have been seen boarding the former aircraft before a flight to Newcastle airport but, in reality, he was headed to a private hospital in France for a medical commissioned jointly by Palace and Sunderland. With time running out, both clubs accepted this unusual arrangement was the only way a player targeted by Arsenal throughout much of the window would be heading to England.

In an attempt to remind Fofana, who scored 11 goals in 59 appearances for Lyon since arriving from Gent in 2024, why he had originally been so excited about playing for Régis Le Bris on Wearside, Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, Sunderland’s owner, flew to Lyon – presumably on a third jet – and spoke to him privately. It appears to have proved an inspired intervention as, shortly after 9pm, Fofana announced that he had made his choice and would be travelling to the Stadium of Light after all.

Although the initial fee agreed is £26m, add-ons dictate it should eventually rise to £31m. That leaves a forward capped five times by Belgium set to become Sunderland’s record signing, eclipsing the £30m paid to Strasbourg for midfielder Habib Diarra last summer. Sunderland have submitted a deal sheet and expect it to be concluded shortly.

Sports.title: ‘A great feeling’: Mykhailo Mudryk seals loan move from Chelsea to Tottenham
Sports.content:
Tottenham have thrown a Premier League lifeline to the forgotten Chelsea winger, Mykhailo Mudryk, signing him on loan just before the transfer deadline and challenging him to revive his career.

Mudryk became a €100m (£89m) player when Chelsea took him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023; the deal comprised an initial €70m and €30m in add-ons. Chelsea beat Arsenal to his signature at a point when the Ukrainian was among the most in-demand players in Europe.

The move to Chelsea did not work out and Mudryk hit rock bottom when he was banned for returning an adverse reading for the banned substance, meldonium, which can increase respiratory capacity and stamina. His last competitive game for Chelsea was on 28 November 2024.

Mudryk was suspended before being given a four-year ban by the Football Association. But after an appeal to the court of arbitration for sport, he was able to resolve his case with the FA at the end of July, being cleared for an immediate return to playing. He accepted breaking anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension that was equal to the time he had already served. The FA noted that changes have been made to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s rules on meldonium and had Mudryk’s test been conducted today then “the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported” and no adverse finding would have been recorded.

Spurs have taken a punt on Mudryk on the recommendation of their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, who worked productively with the 25-year-old at Shakhtar, overseeing his breakthrough season in 2021-22. De Zerbi was in the market for a left winger to complete a new-look front line with the right-sided attacker Sávio and the central striker Omar Marmoush; both have joined from Manchester City.

Spurs failed with moves for Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. The former was retained by Liverpool; the latter went from Everton to City. And so De Zerbi, who has started the season with Mathys Tel on the left, pivoted to Mudryk. The deal for him has a £75m purchase option.

“It’s a great feeling. I can’t wait to start training and playing for the club, and I’m so excited to be reunited with Roberto De Zerbi,” said Mudryk. “He’s my football father. I believe in him. I trust him. I know what he wants from me and with him I always feel I’m improving.”

Speaking during Spurs’s pre-season tour of Australia when Mudryk’s ban ended, De Zerbi said: “He’s my son. I’m very happy. He deserves to play. He’s a cool guy, a top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years in this next season.”

Spurs have not done business with Chelsea since 2009 when the goalkeeper, Carlo Cudicini, was allowed to join them from Stamford Bridge on a free transfer. Yet they added another Chelsea player on deadline day with the centre-half Tosin Adarabioyo signing for £7m.

Adarabioyo replaces Kevin Danso, who went to Sunderland on an initial season-long loan which will be followed by a mandatory £25m purchase. Spurs also moved the midfielder, Pape Sarr, to Juventus on an initial loan with a buy option. The deal is valued at €30m.

Sports.title: West Ham fight off Wolves as Divine Mukasa double eases pressure on Nuno
Sports.content:
It was a match between two disjointed sides, two teams trying to carve out new identities following the drop into the Championship. In the end West Ham won thanks to a bit of luck, a degree of resolve and, crucially, a sharpness in front of goal that took them away from Wolves and reduced the pressure on Nuno Espírito Santo, for a few days at least.

First-half goals from Divine Mukasa and Jarrod Bowen, the latter from the penalty spot, were complemented by two more in the second; Mukasa secured his brace alongside a goal for Konstantinos Mavropanos. The defender doubled up himself too, albeit by scoring at his own end, as Wolves tried to claw their way back into contention. The visitors also added a decent goal from the midfielder Marshall Munetsi to their tally. For all their obvious technical ability, however, César Peixoto’s side lacked the hosts’ sang-froid at the crucial moments and that proved the decisive factor.

Nuno’s mantra after the match was “I think we can do better”, but he was clearly grateful for the win. “We all know that it was much needed,” he said. “Looking back even on today, we have mistakes again but we’ve been much more effective in our attacking actions.”

With West Ham’s uncertainty extending beyond the field of play, there was much interest taken from the appearance of Amanda Staveley in the stands here. The former Newcastle shareholder remains in the running to acquire a stake in West Ham and could be seen punching the air at Mukasa’s first-half banger. The Manchester City loanee was not the only new recruit to impress, with Arne Engels excellent alongside him in midfield.

What gave off the vibes of being an uninspiring opening half ended up being blessed by three goals. West Ham were on the back foot for much of the opening half-hour but established a two-goal lead by the 40th minute after a short spell of improved play. The opening goal was a memorable one, hit by Mukasa from 25 yards and cannoning into the net off the underside of the bar. It was a memorable way for the teenager to open his account, and it came after a piece of smart attacking play that got Kyle Walker-Peters behind Wolves’ defensive line. Seven minutes later, Bowen converted a penalty after swift feet from Joel Piroe confused André into an untimely tackle.

View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen doubles West Ham’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Saud Ahmed/PPAUK/Shutterstock

Before Nuno could get his troops into the dressing room and preach the importance of a clean sheet, Wolves hit back. With West Ham’s defence pushing up, a fortunate deflection off the previously bewildered André opened up the opportunity for Munetsi to run into space, check inside Mavropanos and finish coolly inside Mads Hermansen’s left-hand post.

With nascent enthusiasm tempered by the late concession, the atmosphere among the home support quietened as the second half began, perhaps in anticipation of further trials for West Ham. Instead they extended their lead in short order and it was Mukasa who struck again. This was a lovely move, starting with a cute through ball from Bowen that Pablo dummied to take four Wolves players out of the equation. Receiving on the edge of the box, Mukasa stood up Toti Gomes, shifted to his left and hit a shot that deflected off the Wolves skipper and beyond the despairing José Sá.

“I’m delighted by the way he played,” Nuno said of Mukasa. “All the young lads, not just those who joined this summer, have brought us energy and talent. There’s a lot of things to improve but I’m delighted to have him.”

Wolves responded to the third goal by grabbing hold of possession once more, but the sprightly Fer López spurned two chances. Up the other end, however, and an Engels corner was deep and dangerous and, after Mavropanos saw a towering header crash off the bar, the Greek defender smashed the rebound home on the volley. Six minutes after celebrating, Mavropanos got the final touch to a cross from Jackson Tchatchoua to turn the ball into his own net.

Wolves created no further chances, but could take solace from the performance of the full-back Tchatchoua, who looked impactful at both ends, while Mateus Mané was dominant on the left. “We created a lot of chances to score, they scored more goals,” said Peixoto. “West Ham took their chances and that’s the difference.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa sign Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis as Newcastle get Fernandez-Pardo
Sports.content:
Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.



The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started May’s Europa League triumph in Istanbul; Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.

Watkins’s £50m exit to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.



After Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” said Villa’s manager. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”



Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages. “In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.



“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that, I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”

Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window that has also seen Eddie Howe replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” said Wilson. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo is seen as having the ability and verstatilty to be an ideal fit for Matthias Jaissle’s Newcastle. Photograph: Jean-François Badias/AP

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” acknowledged Wilson. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

“I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club,” said the Belgian. “I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”

Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high-intensity gameplans explains why Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two different clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.

Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool, while across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.

Kevin Danso has joined Sunderland on a year-long loan from Tottenham that should lead to a formal £25m transfer for the Austria centre-half next summer.

Fulham have completed the signing of Manuel Ángel from Real Madrid, having already signed César Palacios and Gonzalo García from the Spanish giants.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 12: Manchester United
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 7th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 4th

Prospects

It was all-change at Manchester United during pre-season, with the departure of their head coach Marc Skinner after five years followed swiftly by the appointment of Eva Olid as a new era begins. There have been significant outgoings from the playing group, including the senior squad members Melvine Malard, Gabby George, Millie Turner and Lisa Naalsund, as well as the end-of-contracts exits of Leah Galton and Hannah Blundell, but the signings of the Spain youth international defender Andrea Medina, the former Germany youth international goalkeeper Janina Leitzig and the Sweden forward Monica Jusu Bah will give the squad a fresh feel.

Missing out on the Women’s Champions League places by nine points last season was disappointing and after a summer in which other clubs have spent big, it feels more likely United will be looking over their shoulder at challengers coming up from fifth and sixth than mounting a title challenge.

Tottenham’s and London City’s ambitious recruitment mean they could threaten United’s position but United have not turned into a bad team overnight. European quarter-finalists last season, their squad retains a strong level of quality international players, despite the sale of Malard to Chelsea in particular. The England internationals Maya Le Tissier and Ella Toone are the senior leaders in a squad that also retains a world-class goalkeeper in Phallon Tullis-Joyce, the dynamic England midfielder Jess Park and the talented Sweden wing-back Anna Sandberg. A top-half finish feels realistic and the club will hope for strong runs in the domestic cups. There is also understood to be a desire at the club to make the playing style more entertaining for supporters.

Off-field picture

As with the men’s club, the Glazer family own a majority stake and Ineos – led by Sir Jim Ratcliffe – has a minority stake but has control of football operations. The women’s team’s financial history divides opinion in the sport; some argue United are an example of how to run a professional women’s team sustainably, having recorded a profit of £397,000 in their most recent accounts and a profit of £1.34m since reforming their senior women’s team in 2018, while others lament a lack of investment from the ownership compared with the budgets of their rivals such as Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester City.

The manager

Olid was appointed on 5 August on a two-year deal with the option of a further year. The Spanish coach, who turned 41 in late August, arrives after an impressive spell at Hearts, where she led the club to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title in May. That made her the SWPL’s manager of the season. It is understood she was chosen by United’s hierarchy because they feel her CV demonstrates a strong track record of developing and improving young players.

Star signing

Bah, who has 11 caps, looks to be an important signing for United from BK Häcken for a fee reportedly of about £400,000. The 23-year-old helped the Swedish club win last term’s inaugural Women’s Europa Cup – European club-level women’s football’s second competition – and she said the opportunity to work with Olid was “perfect” because she wants to improve. She provided seven assists and scored 16 goals for her club last season and United will hope she can settle into the WSL quickly.

View image in fullscreen Monica Jusu Bah arrives in Manchester from Swedish club BK Häcken. Photograph: Poppy Townson/Manchester United/Getty Images

Stat attack

United made a mockery of underlying data last season. Only Arsenal overachieved against their attacking expected goals by more and only City conceded fewer compared with their xG at the back. They were ranked fourth for expected goal metrics at both ends but the combined variance of +9.86 against those numbers makes them hard to predict this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Set for a breakthrough

Layla Drury, an academy graduate, became United’s youngest player and goalscorer when given her debut in the Women’s FA Cup in January at 16, and this summer the 17-year-old became the youngest player to sign a professional contract with the club. She has been added to England’s Under-20 squad for September’s World Cup in Poland and last Saturday scored for the Young Lionesses in their 11-0 warm-up victory against New Caledonia. The forward had previously played for Wales’ youth teams.

What they say

“I always say: ‘My life is football.’ I don’t have other things. I spend probably 24 hours every day on football. It’s my life, my lifestyle and I give everything for the team and for the players. They always have me. Doubts, questions, [it] doesn’t matter the time of the day, I’m going to be there for them. I want to make them better, and that is how I’m going to feel good as a coach, seeing the improvement, seeing that they are better, and of course, winning matches” – Olid to MUTV.

Where are they playing their home games?

United play at Leigh Sports Village, a 12,000-capacity venue which is also the home of the rugby league club Leigh Leopards and United’s men’s Under-21s. It has been their home ground since 2018. The stadium hosted a quarter-final at 2022’s Euros. United’s final home WSL fixture, against Arsenal in May, has been scheduled for Old Trafford, although that match may have to be rearranged if Arsenal reach the semi-finals of the Women’s Champions League because the second legs are that weekend.

Sports.title: ‘I was scared to tell my old teammates’: Victoria Pelova on making leap from Arsenal to Spurs
Sports.content:
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women’s teams as there is between their men’s counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.

Victoria Pelova’s move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well wishes and love.

“I was really scared to tell my old teammates that I was going here,” Pelova says. “My close friends knew about it, obviously, but everyone responded so well. Everyone tells me that it reflects on the person I am. So, I’m actually really glad about that.”

Pelova has been an Arsenal fan favourite despite limited minutes in her three years at the club, during which she was hampered by an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained on international duty in June 2024. Why is she so liked? She comes across as fun and is loved by her teammates, with a wicked and dry sense of humour.

Pelova was not worried what people would make of her move to Spurs, but the Netherlands midfielder did think about it. Ultimately, it was “an easy decision” to join Martin Ho’s squad.

“The way Martin approached me, what he said about how he sees me as a player, the videos he showed me and how he wants me to be, I’ve actually never had a coach talking like that about me. So, for me, it was a good decision. I talked a lot with my mum about it and she immediately said yes. That was actually the most important thing for me, what my mum thought.”

At the start of June, Pelova shared online that her mum had died. A carousel of moving photos of the pair through the years was captioned: “Your biggest fear was leaving me behind. My biggest fear was losing you. Rest now, Mum.”

Pelova is not ready to talk about the loss, but it sits in the background of the interview. Not having to move home as a result of her leaving Arsenal was important. “It does really help me that I have friends and family around me that take care of me,” she says.

View image in fullscreen Pelova slides in on Chelsea’s Alyssa Thompson during Arsenal’s 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge in January. Photograph: Alex Broadway/WSL Football/Getty Images

Reflecting on her spell at Arsenal, with her ACL injury coming at a time when it was believed she would start to get more playing time, she says: “There was a private situation going on, my mum was ill, and I didn’t get minutes. So, it was a really tough time and people didn’t know what I was going through.”

The goal now? “To be happy again, in football and outside football, and just day by day see how it goes.

“It sounds like I have not been happy, but I have been happy in the last year and in being with my friends. But when you’re not playing as regularly as you want to it’s inevitable that you’re not going to be totally happy, and when I’m the happiest person, I will be the best footballer I can be.”

The fresh start at Tottenham has been rejuvenating. “It’s nice to have no one know you. For me, that’s the way to go. I don’t know if I can explain it, but I feel like when everyone knows you, they focus on the things they know.”

Ho made an instant impression on Pelova. “All the coaches I’ve met are always like: ‘Oh, you can play there and there and there.’ Martin was like: ‘You’re this for me.’ He knew exactly where he wanted me and what he wanted from me. That, right away, set the tone for me and it was where and how I see myself as well. What I’ve seen so far is that he’s so detailed. He just wants to make you better. He’s very strict, but he wants to make you a better player and that’s why I’m here.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ho has “a lot” of confidence in her, and that is hugely freeing. “That’s the part I don’t have to worry about … and I can focus on other things.”

Pelova’s experience of Tottenham had been playing against them, and the more difficult that got, the more it contributed to her decision to join. “Defending was so hard,” she says of facing Spurs last season. “So, I already liked the style Martin had the team playing. I also already know Caitlin Dijkstra; I’ve known her for eight years and we lived together in Amsterdam so we know each other so well. She’s like my sister. I know Lize Kop, they’re also one of my closest friends. So, that has made the transition easy because I can always rely on them.

“I’m quite social so I’ve been trying to get to know everyone, the youngsters. It’s quite a hard job in the beginning, it’s intense, but I like it. On the pitch, you’re building relationships, pre-season is always heavy, you just need to grind, but it has been good.”

Pelova has belief in herself and her body, too. “We train really hard. That’s different to what I’m used to. So, obviously it goes up and down, but I’m confident that in a few weeks everything as a team will have progressed so much. Always with new players, it needs time. I’ve been in football a really long time so I know how it goes.”

Asked about Tottenham’s chances of disrupting things at the top, she flips the question, then says she relishes being outsiders. “You need to put us on as underdogs. The underdog position is the place to be.”

Now, Pelova is ready for the intensity of pre-season to end and for the games to begin at home against West Ham on Sunday. One, in particular, stands out, and it comes on 25 October at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. “Please, stop pre-season,” she says with a laugh. “I just want to start. I can’t wait to play against all the teams. I can’t wait to play against Arsenal.”

Sports.title: Bill Simmons probed over alleged proxy bets after admittedly enlisting daughter's boyfriend to place wagers
Sports.content:
Bill Simmons probed over alleged proxy bets after admittedly enlisting daughter's boyfriend to place wagers

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The Massachusetts Gaming Commission is looking into comments made by podcaster and sports media titan Bill Simmons after the Bay State native seemingly admitted to placing proxy bets in the Commonwealth through his daughter's boyfriend.

'The Commission is aware of the comments made on the Bill Simmons Podcast and staff are currently reviewing the matter,' MGC spokesman Thomas Mills told The Daily Mail.

The bets were placed on FanDuel, which has since voided the wagers and sanctioned Simmons' account, as first reported by Front Office Sports.

A former ESPN The Magazine columnist and network star who later moved on to found the sports and culture website, The Ringer, Simmons may have gotten himself into trouble with Monday's episode of his FanDuel-sponsored podcast.

The 56-year-old currently lives in California, where sports gambling remains predominantly illegal. So, when he wanted to place a variety of wagers on FanDuel, he asked his daughter's 21-year-old boyfriend to log into his FanDuel account back in Massachusetts, where such wagering has been legalized.

But despite his effort to gamble legally, Simmons may have violated Massachusetts laws strictly prohibiting proxy bets.

Nobody actually cares that Bill Simmons had someone place his bets for him.



But it’s a very stupid thing for him to admit on a podcast that is sponsored by FanDuel.



Here’s the video: https://t.co/CTFiwv8MhA pic.twitter.com/AY2V1C8LZO — Mick (@BeyondAvgMick) September 1, 2026

The Massachusetts Gaming Commission is looking into comments made by podcaster and sports media titan Bill Simmons after he seemingly admitted to placing proxy bets

'There was a couple bets I really wanted to get in,' Simmons said on his eponymous podcast. 'I wanted… UCLA overs, but Houston, the market had not shifted appropriately yet.

'I can't have my daughter do it,' he continued. 'My dad would have no idea how to do it. But [my daughter's boyfriend] Hank, I really trust Hank.

'I let Hank log into my FanDuel as me. I get the code to make sure it's me to my phone. I give him the code, he logs in, and I have all this money that I had from last year because I actually hit a bunch of futures last year. And he's putting in bets for me, and honestly, it was the closest I've ever felt to Hank. It's a real bonding moment for us.'

Simmons wasn't done there.

'A week later, called him up, ran it back,' he added. 'We did some more.'

Simmons plan may have violated more than Massachusetts gaming laws.

FanDuel's terms and conditions prohibit anyone from wagering on someone else's behalf.

The Daily Mail sought comment from Simmons and spokespeople at The Ringer.

Simmons did poke fun at his situation on X, while plugging his latest podcast episode: 'New BS Podcast! (hosted by me and not a proxy).'

He also admitted to be unaware about the law.

'Did not know about the proxy rules,' he said. 'Yeah, there's some real rules with this stuff… and I learned my lesson. Proxy betting, not allowed. I actually thought it was, but that's fine… but I did learn, not allowed to do that.'

Sports.title: Manchester City are laughing in the face of the 115 charges as they hoover up rivals' star players - thanks to the new clues that the Premier League's case against them is slipping away, writes IAN HERBERT
Sports.content:
On and on Manchester City went, spending to the bitter end of the transfer window with such monumental resource at their disposal that there have been times when many of the rest have wondered why they even bothered.

There was a time, under Txiki Begiristain’s oversight of their transfer business, when they would sail serenely above this madness, though it’s a naked cash-fest now. Having blown the rest of Europe out of the water by tabling £85million for Ayyoub Bouaddi – not far off double what his market price was back in June – and laying out that cool £116million on Elliot Anderson, any other club in this land would have been done in central midfield.

City took on Chelsea’s £120million early asking price for Enzo Fernandez without blinking. They paid £125million. A further £65million for Everton's Iliman Ndiaye took it to £190million on deadline day alone.

Out there in the rest of the football eco-system, other clubs have become minnows in City’s vast pool of spends. Barcelona paid out £12million to Arsenal for Gabriel Jesus, whom City dispensed with four years ago. Everton brought back the one-time £100million City signing Jack Grealish for another go at redemption. Spurs became a rehabilitation home for Etihad rejects.

City are certainly good sellers, too, thanks in part to their academy, and earned the best part of £90million on talent last year on top of more than £120million the summer before. There’s Rodri’s departure to Barcelona for £65million to factor in, while the many players they’ve willingly shipped on reflect the way you no longer seem to be punished for mistakes amid the lunatic economics of the Premier League.

At £30million, Savinho was supposed to replace Riyad Mahrez, whose No26 jersey he took at City, and he didn’t even come close. But the Tottenham executives at the tiller are so desperate for redemption that they forked out a wild £75million on him, making it a £40million-plus profit on an average player. Madness.

Manchester City have forked out £125m for the Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez

And that is on the back of spending £116m for Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest

Omar Marmoush didn’t float City’s boat either, having arrived for £50million to take the weight off Erling Haaland. It turned out he couldn’t perform against deep-lying defenders but with Spurs around, there was another profit to register. Tottenham's eventual fee will be £60million.

And then there’s also the bigger picture, here. Sure, it will bring the forces of holy hell raining down on those of us who point it out – accusations of bitterness and bias and the dreaded ‘red cartel’ conspiracy theory – but let it be said.

City’s capacity to pick off the best players of virtually any other club as it pleases them, this summer, has laughed in the face of that opaque and interminable legal process by which the Premier League’s 115 charges of alleged financial impropriety and evasion are being supposedly tested.

It’s approaching two years since the opening of the ‘Manchester City v the Premier League’ case and there are no longer even rumours or whispers as to when we might see a verdict.

Not so long back, the Manchester Evening News ran a line about City’s barrister David Pannick spending proportionately more time on House of Lords business and less on the City case. As if to say the whole thing is slipping away.

Bloomberg published a recent piece about the Abu Dhabis expressing interest in spending a fortune on British defence technology and ‘the 115’ being an awkward rider to Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s friendly first phone call with United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan – who is the brother of City’s owner. City deny all the charges.

All that can be said with certainty is that their capacity to swoop for other Premier League clubs’ best players – Forest’s Anderson, Bournemouth’s Antoine Semenyo and Everton’s Ndiaye – yet face no legal outcome, positive or negative, depresses and maddens all who look for virtue and transparency in the game.

Everton are not far off their own third anniversary of being hit with a 10-point deduction, later reduced to six, for overspending by £19.5million – barely eight months of Erling Haaland's vast salary – while in the throes of a relentless fight for Premier League survival. So it’s not hard to see why the departure of their excellent and much-admired playmaker Ndiaye up the M62 to City sticks in the throat for that club's fans.

City also spent blew the rest of Europe out of the water by tabling £85million for Ayyoub Bouaddi – not far off double what his market price was back in June

After being hit with their own points deduction for overspending, it’s not hard not to see why the departure of their excellent playmaker Ndiaye to City sticks in the throat of Everton fans

Ndiaye wasn’t even City’s first choice. The club’s move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo collapsed by a process of deadline-day dominoes, so Ndiaye it had to be.

A product of Everton’s capacity to find and develop good players from the lower tiers – an honest, decent pursuit of value and talent – is about to find out whether he will be competing in the Champions League or Carabao Cup for City this season.

It was Grealish, a player signed for a City club-record sum when he was the bright new accessory, who Everton ended up with on Tuesday. He is open, generous, likeable and if anyone can extract the necessary extra self-discipline out of him then it will be David Moyes, a manager who has spent the summer trying to squeeze every last drop out of a limited budget.

Let’s hope it can happen. As the wait for that Premier League verdict extends towards a third year and City go on as if impervious to it, there would be something rather satisfactory about that.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Club launch review of Old Trafford's leaky roof after latest downpour, players lose free booze, the shock exit in academy clearout and green light for new fanzone outside stadium
Sports.content:
It may be a new season but some old problems resurfaced at Old Trafford on Sunday when the roof over the Stretford End sprang a leak during torrential downpours.

Water was seen cascading down on to the pitch in the second half after the heavens opened during Manchester United’s first home game of the season against Ipswich.

Confidential understands the club have launched a review of the latest problem and will make any necessary repairs, although insiders point out that the biblical scale of the storm was a mitigating factor and say other clubs have experienced similar issues.

Old Trafford’s leaky roof has become a metaphor for the problems with United’s 116-year-old home, and one of the factors in the decision to build a new £2billion stadium next door.

It isn’t expected to be ready until 2035 so United must continue to patch up the Theatre of Dreams in the meantime.

The Ipswich game followed a summer upgrade that has seen the pitch ripped up and relaid for the first time in 14 years. United replaced the foundations and drainage system, and also extended the playing surface to get rid of a hazardous drop-off around the perimeter.

Got a class seat for the season pic.twitter.com/bdBUxxZksE — Ciaran 👽🥈 (@CJT49ers) August 30, 2026

The revamped pitchside slope at Old Trafford, which came under fire for potentially causing injuries when players were unable to stop their momentum

Benjamin Sesko suffered a shin injury in the game against Liverpool in May after falling down the slope and colliding with an advertising hoarding

A low wall has been covered in padding so the pitch is surrounded by a more gentle slope.

There is only so much you can do to protect players against the cut and thrust of English football, however, and two of them were sent flying into the advertising boards in the East Stand during United’s 5-2 win over Ipswich.

Dara O’Shea took a tumble when he challenged Marcus Rashford near the byline in the first half, and Abdul Fatawu also had a painful collision with the boards following a tangle with Luke Shaw in the second period. Fortunately, both Ipswich players were unhurt.

Suite ‘n’ sour

As Old Trafford hosted its first game of the season, the problems were not confined to the roof. United fans in plush hospitality suites costing as much as £5,000-a-year have been left furious at the standard of food and drink.

Confidential is aware of at least one supporter who has submitted a formal complaint to the club over the ‘poor’ and ‘unacceptable’ offerings in the Manchester Suite where the optional buffet-style food costs £900-a-season on top of the cost of the ticket.

In an email to United's executive club support team, seen by Confidential, the fan asked for ‘appropriate compensation or reimbursement’ from the club because of the sub-standard service offered.

Another fan claimed a hostess in the 1968 Suite was reduced to tears because of the volume of complaints. The supporter described it as ‘the worst corporate hospitality I've ever experienced at any sporting event’.

It’s understood the problems during the Ipswich match occurred across multiple hospitality and executive suites, where fans in some boxes resorted to ordering kids meals of chicken nuggets and chips due to the dismal quality of what they had been served.

United fans in plush hospitality suites costing as much as £5,000-a-year have been left furious at the standard of food and drink. Many are blaming Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s cost-cutting measures

Many are blaming Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s cost-cutting measures and the club’s new caterer after United named Levy as a hospitality partner back in June.

The club are aware of the issues and are reviewing the feedback from fans. United say they will work with their catering partners to gain a better understanding of the problems and make improvements.

It’s not the first time there have been problems with executive boxes at Old Trafford. In May 2025, Daily Mail Sport revealed that United had been given a two-star food hygiene rating after mouse droppings were found in hospitality suites, although the problems were later fixed and the rating restored to five stars.

You booze, you lose

There has also been some grumbling within the exclusive confines of the players’ lounge over the decision to charge family members, friends and agents of United’s first-team stars for alcoholic drinks.

Previously, the bar was free but Confidential learns that the policy has changed under Ineos – much to the bemusement of those frequenting the lounge.

While it would be easy to assume that this is the latest cost-cutting measure since minority owner Ratcliffe assumed day-to-day control at Old Trafford, insiders insist this is not the case.

They point out that the move is in line with the protocol towards alcohol at other clubs, and that the guests in the players’ lounge are still treated to a meal without charge.

Touching tribute

There was a poignant moment before the Ipswich game, when United were led out onto the pitch by the sons of PC Matthew Blades, who were mascots for the day.

There was a poignant moment before the Ipswich game, when United were led out onto the pitch by the sons of PC Matthew Blades, who were mascots for the day

Confidential understands United were put in touch with the Blades family last week. The club offered them an open-ended invite to Old Trafford, and Matthew’s wife Sarah and their children said they would like to attend Sunday’s game.

The two boys had their photo taken in the tunnel and got autographs from the players before walking out alongside Bruno Fernandes and Senne Lammens in front of a full house.

PC Blades, who alongside his colleague PC Tom Clough was killed in an accident near Middlesbrough last month, was a dedicated United fan. In a tribute in the match programme, he was pictured with his two boys at Old Trafford.

Sesko’s private party

Since Benjamin Sesko returned for the new campaign, it’s been noted how much the striker has bulked up over the summer – despite struggling with a shin injury that kept him out of all six of United's pre-season friendlies.

The Slovenia striker, who came off the bench against Hull and Ipswich, has clearly been hitting the gym over the last few months. And Confidential has also learned that he took some time out to thank fans at an annual get-together in his hometown of Radece.

The exclusive event, which is held around his birthday every year for the fan club that has followed the 23-year-old since the start of his career, was off-limits to media. However, Daily Mail Sport got a sneak peek behind the scenes as Sesko signed merchandise, posed for photos and took part in a Q&A session.

The player’s most loyal fan club will be hoping he has a big season at United after clearly working hard over the summer in preparation for his second season in the Premier League.

Sesko greets fans in his Slovenian hometown, an event he holds around his birthday every year for the fan club that has followed the 23-year-old since the start of his career

Academy clear-out

It has been noticeable this summer that United have put a great deal of focus on clearing out the academy. Club bosses have been eager to streamline numbers in the Under 18s and Under 21s, keeping just those players they believe have a realistic shot of breaking into the first team.

Toby Collyer, Louis Jackson, James Overy, James Scanlon, Habeeb Ogunneye, Sekou Kone (loan), Dan Gore (loan), Jacob Devaney (loan) and Jayce Fitzgerald (loan) are among those moved on, while Gabriele Biancheri, Chido Obi, Diego Leon and Harry Amass have also been made available.

United have kept too many players for too long and, with Ineos keen to move towards a model that delivers bigger profits on academy players, reducing numbers is seen as the way to go.

Sources close to those departing have praised United for allowing a number of the youngsters to leave for nothing, meaning they got better personal terms and ended up at more prestigious clubs.

Louie U-turn

One of the more surprising moves as part of the academy cull is the decision to let Under 18s striker Louie Bradbury go.

Confidential understands the young Welshman, who only signed his first-year professional deal at Old Trafford on August 12, is joining Stoke in a permanent deal.

Bradbury scored at the weekend in the Under 18s’ 3-0 win over Everton, but is now set for a new challenge in the Potteries.

Louie Bradbury (left) is joining Stoke, while Chido Obi (centre) has been made available for loan

Never too late for freight

United may have walked away from talks with Freightliner and purchased an alternative plot behind Old Trafford to build their new £2billion ‘Wembley of the North’, but the freight terminal site could still be part of the wider regeneration around the stadium.

The club announced in June that they have purchased a 25-acre triangle of land located 350 metres away from Old Trafford and do not anticipate any problems securing the remainder they need.

It signalled the end of protracted negotiations with Freightliner which didn’t look promising from the moment it emerged that the two sides were £360million apart in their valuation of the terminal behind the Stretford End.

However, when Trafford Borough Council unveiled their plan for the regeneration project in July, the land owned by Freightliner was very much part of it – which suggests a deal still needs to be done.

Either way, it will not involve United, who are committed to building on their new plot between Wharfside Way, Europa Way and John Gilbert Way, which sources say was always their preferred choice.

The model on display at the council’s launch also had a generic stadium at the heart of it, and it was interesting that United’s CEO of new stadium development, Collette Roche, said the controversial tent design by Foster + Partners is ‘not set in stone’ as the consultation process begins.

United’s CEO of new stadium development, Collette Roche, said the controversial tent design by Foster + Partners is ‘not set in stone’ as the consultation process begins

All-clear for fanzone

Talking of Trafford Borough Council and the area behind the Stretford End, United aren’t expecting any problems with planning permission for the new Paddock fanzone which is due to open in October.

The permanent structure, which will have room for around 1,300 people and be partly covered by a stretch tent, is set to feature a stage for ‘local talent and club legends’, two bars and three food trucks for supporters with tickets on matchdays.

The fanzone is due to open up to four hours before kick-off and close two hours afterwards for daytime fixtures, with reduced opening times for evening games.

Despite Sunday’s teething problems, United have taken steps to upgrade their food and beverage service for fans inside Old Trafford this summer. As with the leaky roof, the club are continuing to invest in the facilities despite a new stadium being on the horizon.

Lacey lights up Leigh

Shea Lacey looked every bit a first-team player as he toyed with Leicester City’s Under 21s at Leigh Sports Village on Monday afternoon.

His brace lit up a 4-1 win for United and Lacey, playing in front of first-team assistant boss Steve Holland, proved why he can play meaningful minutes in Michael Carrick’s side this season.

Lacey is considered a full-time first-team player now and is simply topping up his fitness and sharpness in Under 21s matches when required.

But this was one of his most dominant performances and showed that he now looks like a senior player in academy clothing. Holland was delighted with his display.

Shea Lacey looked every bit a first-team player as he toyed with Leicester City’s Under 21s at Leigh Sports Village on Monday afternoon

Autograph confusion

Confusion reigned on Monday when an announcement was made to say that United’s Under 21s wouldn’t be signing autographs, with excitable kids already stood against the pitchside barrier waiting for their favourite young players.

‘Players will not stop for photos or autographs because of commitments in the future,’ came the PA announcement, much to the bemusement of the parents and kids who had made the trip to see JJ Gabriel, Lacey, Tynan Thompson and Co. United sources insist that players were available for autographs outside, but no such announcement was made – leading to plenty of grumbles from families on the way out. A very strange move.

I will walk 500 miles …

Finally, a lovely moment at Carrington in the past week when teenage United supporter Zac Knight was introduced to Michael Carrick and the first-team squad after a 500-mile journey by foot from his Surrey home to Old Trafford.

Knight has already raised more than £100,000 for Young Epilepsy since he was diagnosed with the condition at the age of eight, and he got to tell the players all about his efforts. The teenager cycled the 500 miles back, and the hope is his visit to United’s training base will help his cause.

Find out more about Zac's fundraising here.

Sports.title: Arthur Fery is knocked OUT of the US Open in New York first-round nightmare two months after British No1's miracle Wimbledon wildcard semi-final run
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery is knocked OUT of the US Open in New York first-round nightmare two months after British No1's miracle Wimbledon wildcard semi-final run

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

After the Wimbledon dream came Arthur Fery’s New York nightmare as the British No1 was knocked out of the US Open just over two hours after his debut by Lorenzo Musetti, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5.

The British No1’s ranking was only a stone’s throw from receiving a seeded berth in Queens and he was badly punished, drawn against the world No14 who barely broke a sweat on a brutally humid afternoon.

A downpour delayed the start of the match by about four hours, but did little to clear the thick cloud hovering low over Grandstand, the air sticky with heat. Fery’s shirt was soaked through inside the first game, and as the balls slowed in the humidity, the Briton struggled to find the line with his shotmaking.

Fery’s best level came in the opening stages: six thoughtful games where he was able to put early pressure on Musetti with his variety. He put his particular faith in his game at the net, surging up to deliver a stream of drop shots and bulleted volleys.

This was not without fault: more than once, Musetti exploited his willingness to surge forward with a chip that soared over his 5ft9’ frame and landed squarely in play. Even a tweener, struck between his legs after Fery motored back to the baseline, couldn’t save him in the second set.

For the crowd, the early contest was good-looking. Like clever movement? Watch Fery slide up the court to stretch and delicately feed back a sliced volley. More into backhands? Marvel at Musetti’s, a one-handed holdout, struck down the line sumptuously to bring up set point in the first.

Arthur Fery was unable to bypass Lorenzo Musetti on his US Open main draw debut

The Italian has missed the last two majors due to injury but looked a cut above the British No1

But the two men were only level for so long. Musetti missed the last two majors due to injury, but his stronger service game allowed him to remain a cut above Fery. When it dipped briefly in the second set, the Briton failed to pounce, squandering four break points with a string of nervous unforced errors.

A late comeback in the third saw Fery claim two breaks of Musetti’s serve, but each one was chased by his own faltering service game. Fery’s code violation for audible obscenity as he went 6-5 down was understandable, at least.

'Today, (my serve) really let me down,' Fery agreed after the match. 'That was the biggest difference (between us) I think. In the rally, I was going toe to toe, especially towards the end. I was starting to dominate the rallies from the back, and once the play got started, I felt better and better.

'So it's positive that I'm starting the rally down a lot of the time because of the serve. He was serving well. He was serving fast and quite accurate. But even in the rally, I felt like I can do things better, even though I'm already I'd say almost 50-50 with a guy who's top 15 and who has that resume, but yeah, lots of things to work on. They're still fresh.'

Catapulted into the top 40 just two months ago, Fery has close to zero experience managing his calendar. This week, he arrived as a Winston-Salem Open finalist, and his run of five consecutive matches two days before his first match in Flushing Meadows may have delivered a lesson about what he can handle before a Grand Slam. At this stage in his career, Fery has everything to learn. What Musetti has taught him will sting regardless.

For now however, Fery believes he made the right decision in playing Winston-Salem, in itself, a valuable experience.

'The Grand Slams are the biggest tournaments, and everyone has their eye on them,' Fery conceded. 'But at the same time, would I sign for these past two weeks right now? Yeah, probably.

'To be honest, it's a lot of ranking points. It's a first ATP final, so it's good. Even though it meant that my preparation for US Open was not great in terms of practicing on site and resting.'

Next, focus will shift to leading his country in Davis Cup tennis on home soil against Ecuador in two weeks time, and then the Asian swing, with events in Tokyo and Shanghai to come. Having only played a small Challenger tournament outside the Chinese city, Fery is looking forward to the likely polar opposite experience of the player-favourite Masters event.

The 24-year-old is also revelling in the new path his career has taken on. Gone are the days of small tournaments, smaller paychecks, and a nervous wait to see if you might make the cut for a draw.

'It helps a lot,' Fery admitted. 'I know that I'm not going to play qualifying events pretty much anywhere. I know that I'm going to be main draws in pretty much every ATP tournament.

Although disappointed in New York, Fery has much to look forward to in the autumn with Davis Cup and new tournaments to play

'For clarity, it's great to be where I'm at in the rankings right now, and it helps to plan. I know I'm going to go to Australia (next January). I know that I'll be playing these main draws in Asia. The only kind of one that's up in the air is Davis Cup (Finals), and that will affect the rest of the schedule towards the end of the year.'

While Fery’s race is run in New York, qualifier Toby Samuel has his own chance to go toe-to-toe with a seed when he meets world No19 Jiri Lehecka on Wednesday. Ranked 1,871st in the world as recently as January 2025, victory against Lehecka’s fellow Czech Tomas Machac sent him into the top 100.

‘I knew that I had the level to jump up and play here, but obviously not this fast,’ he said. ‘I've always believed in myself and obviously now it's paid off.’

Katie Boulter is another Briton hoping to avoid early Czech-out in the Big Apple with her match-up against Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova, while remaining first-round Brits Jan Choinski and Francesca Jones have seen their Tuesday matches delayed by rain.

Sports.title: Tottenham sign Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk on season-long loan, as Ukrainian attempts to revive career after doping ban
Sports.content:
Tottenham have announced the deadline day addition of Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk on a season-long loan.

Mudryk's 20-month doping ban came to an end in August and he featured briefly in pre-season for the Blues.

Having joined Chelsea for £89m from Shakhtar Donetsk, Mudryk had not played since November 2024 after failing a doping test for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old is now clear to resume his career and will do so on loan at Tottenham where he rejoins old boss Roberto de Zerbi.

'It's a great feeling. I can't wait to start training and playing for the Club, and I'm so excited to be reunited with De Zerbi,' the Ukrainian said of the move.

'I'm a player who brings speed and creativity, and I want to help in both the offensive and defensive areas. I want to make the fans excited.

Mykhailo Mudryk has joined Tottenham from Chelsea on a season-long loan deal

'I can see it's a strong squad here with good players, and I'm looking forward to sharing a pitch and special moments with them.'

De Zerbi said: 'Having worked with Misha earlier in his career, I know exactly what he can bring to our team.

'He has the quality to change a game with his speed and ability in one-vs-one situations, and is an exciting, attacking talent.

'I will demand a lot from Misha and it is our job to help him find the best version of himself. If we do that then he can become a very important player for us. I am very happy he chose to come here, and I cannot wait to work with him again.'

Tottenham faced competition from other Premier League sides for Mydryk, including Leeds, Coventry, Brentford and Sunderland.

Chelsea are understood to have wanted to send him on loan to sister club Strasbourg but the winger wanted to stay in the English top flight.

Mudryk, 25, was handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test but it was ended after a resolution was reached with the FA.

Mudryk has insisted from the very beginning that he never knowingly or intentionally took a prohibited substance. An important factor in the agreed resolution is the change made by the World Anti-Doping Agency to the scientific reporting standards used by accredited anti-doping laboratories when analysing samples for meldonium.

Mudryk will provide pace and dynamism for Spurs and can play on either flank

The laboratories use a qualitative testing method, meaning they estimate concentration levels rather than measure them precisely. Following developments in the scientific guidance, WADA increased the reporting threshold to provide greater confidence that samples reported as positive exceed the minimum reporting level.

After being cleared to play, Mudryk posted: 'After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.

'I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future. This has been the most difficult period of my career.'

Sports.title: Man City complete Enzo Fernandez deal: Chelsea star FINALLY gets his move for joint-record British transfer fee of £125m as Blues cave in to rivals despite signing no replacement
Sports.content:
Manchester City struck a £125million deadline-day deal to secure Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea – but Xabi Alonso's side were left seething after Monaco pulled the plug on their own agreement for his replacement Lamine Camara. The Fernandez sale equals the British transfer record which was paid to Newcastle by Liverpool for Alexander Isak last summer, and is a fixed fee for the 25-year-old Argentinian with no add-ons involved. He was Enzo Maresca's top target in this window. While Chelsea reached an agreement which took their incomings towards the £500m mark for the summer – with club sources pointing out that is also a British record – they did so without having their own replacement at the ready. Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal. However, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached. Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn. Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business. That meant Chelsea were left without cover for Fernandez. Blues sources added they had the opportunity to stop Fernandez from joining City after they learned of the U-turn on Camara – but they had given their word to their Premier League counterparts and, unlike Monaco, they honoured it. Chelsea had spent their deadline day chasing Camara, seeing two bids worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down earlier in the day before having a third accepted. Enzo Fernandez signed for Man City in a massive transfer deadline day deal In a statement released around the same as this bombshell news broke, Fernandez said to his former fans: ‘Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart. But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.’ City leaving their club-to-club negotiations until the final two days of the window had left Chelsea with limited time to secure their own signing. Central to Chelsea agreeing to a deal with City was Fernandez’s relationship with Maresca with the two wanting to work together again. Fernandez was known to have been keen to leave, having flirted with that idea before the last season had even finished. With no Fernandez or Camara – and with Dario Essugo joining Strasbourg on loan – Chelsea’s senior midfield options are Moises Caicedo, Reece James, Romeo Lavia, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson. Malo Gusto can also be used centrally if required. While Fernandez developed a helpful habit of scoring important goals, Xabi Alonso has an impressive attack, having signed Morgan Rogers for £117m this summer to form a front three with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Chelsea fans may be glad that what turned into an exhausting saga is coming to an end at least. Chelsea initially attempted to accelerate a conclusion by creating their own deadline for bids by Friday August 14 at 5pm. That was for a £120m transfer and the terms were communicated to their Premier League counterparts via Fernandez’s camp, led by Javier Pastore. Chelsea’s hope was that it would give them ample time to replace their 2022 World Cup-winning midfielder. However, City did not play along with Chelsea’s deadline. No offer was submitted, and Blues insiders claimed they ‘expected’ Fernandez to stay with them for the entirety of 2026-27. He was even handed the captain’s armband when he appeared as a substitute in their final friendly at home to Real Sociedad, receiving a mixed reception inside Stamford Bridge. Chelsea were left furious by Monaco's handling of Lamine Camara's prospective move Fernandez was booed by fans upon returning to the Premier League following his World Cup taunts Fernandez appeared in their Premier League opener at Fulham as a substitute. While the home fans inside Craven Cottage booed him after Argentina’s behaviour at the World Cup, the away end welcomed him warmly, with those Chelsea supporters even chanting his name. Fernandez continued to train with his team-mates and in Alonso’s main squad rather than the second group including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, but then disappeared. Following talks with Alonso, he was not involved in their Carabao Cup win over Luton, or in their Premier League victory against Brighton. Alonso insisted publicly it was his decision after speaking with the player, but did add he selected a squad that had the ‘desire to play’. Maresca had a good relationship with Fernandez at Chelsea, where he often wore the captain’s armband in the absence of James. Maresca also handed him that armband barely a month after the Argentinian was accused of singing a racist song following his country’s 2024 Copa America triumph. That was in Chelsea’s Premier League opener at home to City. When Maresca eventually exited Chelsea after speaking with City about succeeding Pep Guardiola, Fernandez was among those who spoke up, suggesting it ‘hurt’ the team. The Blues ended up finishing 10th in that season, leaving them with no European football under Alonso for this term.
