Sports.title: The story of Deadline Day: Man City finally land £125m Enzo Fernandez as Chelsea are enraged by Monaco over Lamine Camara - Folarin Balogun changes mind on Everton move, Spurs secure Mykhailo Mudryk and total Prem spend hits £3.2BILLION
Sports.content:
The story of Deadline Day: Man City finally land £125m Enzo Fernandez as Chelsea are enraged by Monaco over Lamine Camara - Folarin Balogun changes mind on Everton move, Spurs secure Mykhailo Mudryk and total Prem spend hits £3.2BILLION

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City struck a £125million deadline-day deal to secure Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea – but Xabi Alonso's side were left seething after Monaco pulled the plug on their own agreement for his replacement Lamine Camara.

The Fernandez sale equals the British transfer record which was paid to Newcastle by Liverpool for Alexander Isak last summer, and is a fixed fee for the 25-year-old Argentinian with no add-ons involved. He was Enzo Maresca's top target in this window.

Chelsea thought they had secured Camara from Monaco with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47m deal. However, in a dramatic twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word as the 11pm deadline approached.

Chelsea sources say the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join. Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the deal for Camara was being withdrawn.

Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Enzo Fernandez poses with a Man City shirt after joining in a £125million deadline day deal

Everton's on-off move for Monaco striker Folarin Balogun is off after the player changed his mind on the move.

A deal sheet had been put in to buy Everton more time after they had renegotiated terms on a £40m deal with Monaco but the USA international went cool on the transfer.

An issue had been raised during the 25-year-old’s medical which caused negotiations to stall. That prompted Everton to seek alternatives and attempt to renegotiate.

They made contact with Manchester United over a loan for Joshua Zirkzee and also spoke to Aston Villa about a loan for Tammy Abraham.

Both attempts were rebuffed as the respective clubs felt it was too late in the window to negotiate.

Everton then found accord with Monaco for a revised structure to the deal and it was progressing only for Balogun to say he no longer wanted the transfer to take place.

Everton gave Prime Minister Andy Burnham his wish by signing Jack Grealish for one more year as Premier League clubs reached a new summer spending record of over £3.2billion after a busy deadline day.

Everton had already been forced to secure a £4m deal for Lyon’s former Arsenal utility man Ainsley Maitland-Niles after Fulham blocked their move for right back Kenny Tete. The Netherlands international had been lined up for a £9.4m switch to Merseyside but Rayo Vallecano’s reluctance to sell Andrei Ratiu meant Fulham couldn’t sign a replacement. Everton had already sold Nathan Patterson to Torino.

Everton striker Beto joined Fiorentina for £15.4m and Iliman Ndiaye completed his dream £65m move to Man City. The 26-year-old signed a contract until 2031. ‘I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this,’ he said. ‘City are one of the best clubs in the world. To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands.’

Jack Grealish signed for another year at Everton on loan from Manchester City

Across the city, Liverpool saw midfielder Harvey Elliott join Valencia on a loan until the end of the season. Liverpool signed 18-year-old goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Belgian side Genk in a deal that could be worth up to £30m.

Brughmans has agreed a six-year contract but will remain at Genk on loan this season before moving to Anfield next summer when No 1 keeper Alisson’s contract expires.

Arsenal did not get the stellar names they wanted to strengthen their attack but still allowed 19-year-old Ethan Nwaneri to join Borussia Dortmund on loan.

Lyon forward Malick Fofana led Sunderland and Crystal Palace a merry dance for most of the day as his representatives eked out better offers from both. Twice the 21-year-old agreed to join Palace, twice he agreed to join Sunderland. He plumped for Wearside after Sunderland owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus travelled to Lyon to persuade him.

Palace turned to Midtjylland’s Chile international Dario Osorio. They also revived talks for Marseille midfielder Quinten Timber and Ben Chilwell returned, while Borna Sosa went to Cologne on loan.

Malick Fofana accepted offers from both Sunderland and Crystal Palace before joining the Black Cats

Tosin Adarabioyo joined Tottenham from Chelsea for £10m plus £2m in add-ons. His Chelsea teammate Mykhailo Mudryk also joined Spurs on loan saying he is 'excited to be reunited' with his old Shakhtar boss Roberto de Zerbi.

Leeds rejected an approach from Sunderland for Noah Okafor but allowed Willy Gnonto to join Fiorentina on loan.

Leeds agreed to loan speedy Eintracht Frankfurt winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya with an option to buy for £21m plus add-ons. They also added NICE left-back Melvin Bard on loan with an option to buy for £4.28m.

Man United's proposed bid to sign 18-year-old midfielder Louis Page from Leicester City was called off. The clubs had been in talks over a deal worth more than £10m, with Leicester looking for £12m rising to a potential £15m and a sell-on.

United were offered Man City left-back Rayan Ait Nouri but their neighbours would only agree to a loan with obligation to buy and the Old Trafford side had no desire for a permanent move.

Newcastle signed forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille for an initial £51.4m and rejected further offers from Nottingham Forest worth up to £15m for 31-year-old winger Jacob Murphy.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo joined Newcastle from Lille in a deadline day deal

Forest defender Morato headed to West Ham on a season-long loan, with the option to make the deal permanent while Forest defender Zach Abbott signed a new contract then joined Southampton on loan.

Aston Villa completed the signings of Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye, 18, from Paris St-Germain for £47m and English centre back Taylor Harwood-Bellis, 24, from Southampton for £25m with £4m in potential add-ons.

Hull City agreed deals for winger Sorba Thomas from Stoke and Olympiacos midfielder Christos Mouzakitis. They also added Genoa wing-back Brooke Norton-Cuffy with Cody Drameh heading the other way while Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam signed too.

Brighton moved to sign defensive midfielder Chema Andres from Stuttgart for £18m and struck a deal with Millwall for Femi Azeez.

Sunderland signed Kevin Danso from Tottenham and agreed a £5m deal for striker Juan Riquelme Angulo, 18, from Ecuador talent factory Independiente del Valle.

Fulham added another Real Madrid player, £3m midfielder Manuel Angel, and moved for Elche defender David Affengruber and Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson.

Ipswich completed the £20m signing of Burnley forward Zian Flemming while Arsenal keeper Tommy Setford, 20, joined League One side Stevenage on loan.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods to change 'not guilty' plea in DUI case months after Florida rollover crash
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods to change 'not guilty' plea in DUI case months after Florida rollover crash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tiger Woods plans to change his not guilty plea in the DUI case stemming from his March rollover crash in Florida, The Daily Mail has learned.

Woods, 50, originally pleaded not guilty to two misdemeanour charges back on March 31. He is now scheduled to appear in court Wednesday for a change-of-plea hearing, according to court records.

It is unclear if he has reached a deal in the case. The Daily Mail has sought comment from both his attorney and Martin County prosecutors.

The 15-time major champion was charged with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test after cops found two opioid tablets in his pocket following the crash.

He has since spent time in rehab in Switzerland but has not been seen publicly since arriving back in America until last month.

According to police, Woods was driving at a high speed along a beachside road in Jupiter Island, Florida when his Land Rover clipped a tractor trailer truck and rolled onto its side, causing about $5,000 worth of damage to the other vehicle.

Court documents showed Tuesday that Tiger Woods plans to change his not guilty plea in a DUI case stemming from a rollover crash in Florida

The golf great flipped his Land Rover clean onto its side during his accident in Jupiter

In April the Daily Mail broke the news that the golfer would leaving the country 'imminently'

Woods is pictured in the back of a police cruiser after being arrested on suspicion of DUI

He was able to crawl out of the vehicle without any injuries before later admitting to officers he was looking at his phone and changing the radio at the time of the collision.

A Breathalyzer test did not reveal any alcohol in Woods’ system, but he refused a urine test, according to police.

The Sheriff’s report obtained by The Daily Mail said deputies found opioids in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment.

His most recent hearing was held on August 4, following a July ruling that allowed prosecutors to obtain Woods' hospital records that were connected to the crash.

Martin County circuit court judge Darren Steele approved an agreement between the State Attorney's Office and Woods' legal team that allowed prosecutors to request records from the hospital that treated the PGA legend following his crash.

Back in May, Steele approved a similar agreement granting prosecutors access to Woods' prescription medication records from his Palm Beach pharmacy between January 1 and his March crash.

Prosecutors and Woods' attorney have agreed to a protective order that limits the release of any hospital or prescription records to the State Attorney's Office, law enforcement, state experts and the defense.

Woods was closing in on a return to golf and was widely expected to compete at The Masters in the days before the crash.

He hasn't competed since the 2024 Open Championship at Royal Troon in Scotland and has since undergone surgery to repair a torn Achilles as well as a seventh back procedure.

Woods' legal problems have since been put into perspective by his girlfriend Vanessa Trump's cancer diagnosis. She revealed her bout with an unspecified form of breast cancer back in May.

Vanessa Trump, girlfriend of Tiger Woods, is seen with him and daughter Kai back in March

Tiger Woods is seen in a police booking photo after his arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence (DUI) May 29, 2017 in Jupiter, Florida. He later pleaded guilty to reckless driving

Tiger's March crash marked the fourth major driving-related incident of Woods' adult life.

Five years earlier, when Woods rolled another SUV down a steep embankment in California, he did not face any accusations of driving under the influence. Instead, the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department claimed Woods was driving at around 80mph, nearly twice the legal limit, at the time of the crash.

What's more, eyewitnesses told TMZ that Woods appeared agitated and impatient while leaving a golf tournament parking lot in the moments before the crash.

Woods was never charged in 2021, but he wasn't so lucky in 2017, when he was pulled over by Jupiter police about 15 miles from his home. Officers said they found him unconscious in his Mercedes-Benz, which was parked awkwardly on the roadside at around 3am.

Upon closer inspection, they noticed damage to his vehicle.

The good news was that Woods didn't have any alcohol in his system, but later tests found the active ingredient for marijuana, two painkillers - Vicodin and Dilaudid - the sleep drug Ambien and the anti-anxiety drug Xanax.

He later claimed he'd been self-medicating for pain caused by his fourth back surgery and insomnia. Woods did not specifically address the marijuana issue and he wasn't found with any of the drug in his possession.

Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving and received a year of probation, a $250 fine and was ordered to undergo 50 hours of community service. He was also banned from drinking alcohol during the probation.

Perhaps one silver lining came in July of 2017, when Woods completed a private program to address his dependency on pain killers.

'I will continue to tackle this going forward with my doctors, family and friends,' he tweeted at the time. 'I am so very thankful for all of the support I've received.'

Woods' most notorious car crash took place in November of 2009, when he rammed his Cadillac Escalade into a fire hydrant, tree and several hedges near his home.

He was treated for minor injuries and received a ticket for careless driving, but while he thanked his then-wife Elin Nordegren for getting him out of the car, there were lingering doubts about the story. After all, it was only days earlier that the National Enquirer claimed he'd had an affair with Rachel Uchitel, a 9/11 widow and New York nightclub manager.

The alleged details of November 27, 2009 were ultimately included in the best-selling biography from Jeff Benedict and Armen Keteyian, titled: Tiger Woods.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher changes Premier League prediction with 'only team' who can top Arsenal
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher changes Premier League prediction with 'only team' who can top Arsenal

Manchester City secured the deadline day signing of Enzo Fernandez and Jamie Carragher has now backed them to be Arsenal's Premier League challengers

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher believes Man City's deadline day signing has given them a shot at the title (Image: PA)

Jamie Carragher believes the signing of Enzo Fernandez has seen Manchester City leap ahead of Chelsea in the pecking order and become "the only team who can wrestle this title from Arsenal."

‌



City spend a record fee to land Fernandez, who had been linked with a Stamford Bridge exit all summer, on deadline day. It completes a total reshuffle of their midfield with the talismanic Rodri leaving for Spain.

‌



Elliot Anderson completed his move to Manchester during the World Cup and, after the tournament, City made Ayyoub Bouaddi the most expensive teenager in Premier League history when they signed him from Lille.

‌



They've continued to be aggressive in the market and have now added the Argentine World Cup winner, who was keen to reunite with Enzo Maresca, who has just taken over at the Etihad. And Carragher now believes City could make a play at winning the title for the first time in three years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Quizzed on whether Fernandez takes City closer to the summit he replied: "I think he does, certainly pushed them above Chelsea, and myself and plenty of others thought Chelsea would have a really good season. Some of that is off the back of not having European football and having a new manager. But losing Enzo Fernandez, who over the last two of three players, has been one of the big players for Chelsea.

‌



"They've always had five or six top players but not a lot around that. They've now lost one of them - and he's gone to Man City. They look a lot stronger and they're going to be the biggest challengers to Arsenal now."

The loss of Rodri, who had been at the club since 2019, was massive. The Spaniard went on to become one of the pillars of their success, winning the Ballon d'Or while at the club.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has completed his joint British-transfer record move from Chelsea to Man City. (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



After winning four Premier League titles and the Champions League he moved to Barcelona, but Carragher is impressed with how they've rebuilt the midfield.

He added: "It is a really good squad, there's been a lot of turnover over the last 12 months. Losing Rodri was really big thing and I thought it would be really difficult to recover from that. But if you said they'd bring in Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez you'd say that's a top midfield. I think that gives them the greatest chance, ahead of any other team, and maybe the only team who can wrestle this title from Arsenal."

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez reveals Chelsea truth in emotional statement on Man City transfer
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez reveals Chelsea truth in emotional statement on Man City transfer

Enzo Fernandez is on the verge of joining Manchester City from Chelsea

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez has released a statement ahead of his move to Manchester City. (Image: PA Wire)

Enzo Fernandez says he hasn't been in a good place ahead of his £125m move from Chelsea to Manchester City in an emotional statement shared on his social media channels. The Argentinian international is in Manchester for a medical ahead of a reunion with Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

‌



Fernandez's future at Stamford Bridge has been up in the air all summer, having expressed a desire to live in Madrid earlier this year. However, Real Madrid released a statement denying any interest in the 25-year-old, with Man City lying in wait.

‌



It's taken until deadline day for City to act on their interest, agreeing a big-money move for the combative midfielder, who has thanked Chelsea fans for the support during his time at the club.

‌



Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit READ MORE :

Enzo Fernandez set for awkward Erling Haaland reunion after Chelsea transfer to Man City READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a statement shared on his social media channel, Fernandez said: "Dear Chelsea, I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, l haven't been in a good place.

"Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

‌



"Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves.

"We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez is on his way to Man City after a deal was finally agreed with Chelsea on deadline day. (Image: (Photo by Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images))

‌



"I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

"But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I've said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club.

"Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart. But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because l am the same.

‌



"And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way. I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

"To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

" Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it. This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too.

Article continues below

"Never doubt that. You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best. Always Blue. Thank you, Chelsea."

Sports.title: Galopin Des Champs tragedy as dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero dies five days after retirement
Sports.content:
Galopin Des Champs tragedy as dual Cheltenham Gold Cup hero dies five days after retirement

The 10-year-old who won the Cheltenham Gold Cup in 2023 and 2024 and finished second in 2025 for trainer Willie Mullins suffered a fatal injury in a field

View 2 Images Galopin Des Champs (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

Legendary dual Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Galopin Des Champs has died just five days after he retired

‌



The 10-year-old became one of the most popular jumpers of recent times, winning 12 races at Grade 1 level, including the most prestigious race of all, the Gold Cup at the 2023 and 2024 Cheltenham Festivals.

‌



He attempted to join an elite group of three-time winners of the big race in 2025 only to finish second to Inothewayurthinkin and missed the race this year due to an injury setback. He last raced at Leopardstown in February in the Paddy Power Irish Gold Cup where he finished a below par third behind stablemate Fact To File.

‌



Trainer involved in extraordinary betting coup suspended after winner fails drugs test READ MORE :

Value Scope Extra: Steve Jones marks your card on the big races ahead READ MORE :

But last week Willie Mullins announced he would not race again.

He said: "We took a collective decision to retire Galopin Des Champs at his age because we felt he could not do himself justice at the level he was used to.

“He retires a good, sound horse who will hopefully have a good second career as a sport horse."

‌



Galopin Des Champs was to spend his retirement with former stable jockey Ruby Walsh, whose daughter was going retrain the horse.

But on Tuesday, Walsh had to break the terrible news that he had passed away as a result of a serious injury.

View 2 Images Galopin Des Champs in Cheltenham action (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

In a statement, Walsh said: "Sadly, Galopin Des Champs suffered an injury in his field this morning and could not be saved.

"He was checked a few times throughout the morning, but late in the morning when I went to get him for exercise, I found him with a severe injury, high up on his near front leg. He was attended to by our vets immediately, but X-rays revealed extensive, unrepairable damage.

"He was a fabulous horse whose short time with us has left lots of broken hearts, but none more so than those of Grey, Audrey and Sarah Turley, and Adam Connolly, who looked after him for so long. He will be sadly missed."

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez set for awkward Erling Haaland reunion after Chelsea transfer to Man City
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez set for awkward Erling Haaland reunion after Chelsea transfer to Man City

Enzo Fernandez is set to join Manchester City from Chelsea, but is set for an awkward reunion with Erling Haaland

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez (Image: (Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images))

Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez looks set for an uncomfortable reunion with Erling Haaland at Manchester City after the two clubs agreed on a £125m fee for the midfielder. Enzo Maresca is set to be reunited with the Argentinian international at the Etihad Stadium after agreeing a joint British-record transfer fee.

‌



It's welcome news for Haaland, who will no doubt be relieved to see an on-field battle with the Blues enforcer finally draw to a close. The Man City striker accused Fernandez of stamping on him during a meeting between the two sides in their 2-0 victory over Chelsea at the start of the 2024/25 season.

‌



Pep Guardiola's outfit got their Premier League title defence off to a flying start with a win over the Blues, though Haaland had plenty to say about Fernandez afterwards.

‌



Chelsea have Arsenal and Tottenham players on five-man Enzo Fernandez replacement list READ MORE :

Chelsea’s late Alex Scott transfer calls with Premier League giants on red alert READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"All the time he stamps on me, he pushes me and everything, not only him," Haaland told BBC Sport after the win. "I don't know what he wants but that's what they do I guess.

"We just won the Premier League so let's take it game by game. It's 37 games left, let's not forget we won the Premier League and now we have won the first game of this season.

‌



"It's amazing to have everyone back. We go from there. It's ridiculous how quick it actually goes, it's my third season now. I'm happy, especially now after the win.

"It's the first game back and we're not in perfect shape, but we did a really solid performance. We just stayed calm and played, it's amazing to see."

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez is on his way to Man City after a deal was finally agreed with Chelsea on deadline day. (Image: (Photo by Pedro Porru/MB Media/Getty Images))

‌



This is not the first occasion Fernandez has been accused of underhand tactics, having elbowed Man City newcomer Elliott Anderson in the back during the World Cup clash between England and Argentina.

The foul went unpunished, much to the fury of England players and staff, with Fernandez escaping a yellow card for the incident.

Tensions boiled over between the two nations, with Anderson and Fernandez locked in a battle throughout the match. Ultimately, however, it was Argentina who came out on top, defeating the Three Lions 2-1.

Article continues below

Fernandez has been given the green light to travel to Manchester to complete a medical at City, bringing an end to the uncertainty about his future.

The Argentinian had been vocal about a potential move to Real Madrid under former boss Liam Rosenior, but Los Blancos have not tried to buy the midfielder this summer.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua closer to Tyson Fury fight deal after key demand met
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua closer to Tyson Fury fight deal after key demand met

Joshua had been adamant he will only face his bitter rival if the long-awaited clash is staged at Wembley but the fight is now headed to New York

View Image Tyson Fury is due to fight Anthony Joshua (Image: Tyson Fury/Instagram)

Anthony Joshua is a step closer to agreeing to fight Tyson Fury in New York.

‌



Joshua had been adamant he will only face his bitter rival if the long-awaited clash is staged at Wembley. But Netflix and the fight's Saudi Arabian backers want the all-British showdown held Stateside. Last month, Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn sent a list of demands they wanted met before they would agree to the switch.

‌



Those included an increase in Joshua's purse to compensate for the higher tax bill he will receive for facing Fury in the Big Apple. Joshua also insisted he be paid his full purse from his last win over Kristrian Prenga - which has now been done. Hearn now wants the rest of their requests agreed to by the end of the week, which could see the fight announced for November 20 at Madison Square Garden.

‌



Tyson Fury provides update on Anthony Joshua replacement READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua appears to agree with Moses Itauma criticism READ MORE :

"We're all good from the last fight, and we're all moving forward amicably," he said. "We don't want to do the fight in the US, but we also understand it has to work for everybody. We've been banging our head against the wall on that for the last two months.

"We've set out our position, mainly in concern to the tax situation that will deplete his net purse by going to America, which can be rectified. There's nothing unreasonable in there. If they want it in the US, they'll sign it. If not, we'll be very happy, and we'll do it in the UK.

Article continues below

"We're speaking multiple times a day, but we're running out of time. I mean, if you want to do the fight on November 20, and they're talking of a press conference next week, it's [already] Tuesday. But the ball's in their court. Our dream and our hope is they just turn around and go, ‘This is too messy, we'll just do it in Wembley.’ But they're adamant that they want the fight in America.”

Sports.title: Eberechi Eze singles out two Arsenal stars who can make difference in title bid
Sports.content:
Eberechi Eze singles out two Arsenal stars who can make difference in title bid

Eberechi Eze has hailed the impact of two of Arsenal's major summer signings after they played their part in the hard-fought 1-0 win over Aston Villa on Monday night

View 3 Images Eberechi Eze is expecting big things from Arsenal new boy's Ezri Konsa and Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC)

Eberechi Eze says Arsenal have got two new “warriors” to help them fight to retain the title.

‌



Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa were both given their Arsenal debuts at Aston Villa after being brought in this summer for a total of £130m. They helped Arsenal grind out a victory to help the reigning champions maintain their perfect start to the campaign with two straight wins.

‌



That will be put to the test in Sunday’s London derby with Chelsea who have also made an impressive 100 percent start to the campaign under new boss Xabi Alonso.

‌



But Arsenal midfielder Eze believes the two new debutants will make Arsenal even stronger this season ahead of an early test of their credentials at the Emirates this weekend.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Eze said: “They're both special players. They have so much experience in the league and so much to bring to our team.

‌



“You can see how strong they are. They're warriors. They're high quality on the ball as well. So it's great additions and people that will help us for sure.

“It’s not easy. Villa are a good team and they have good fans as well. You can sometimes get caught up in it. But we kept strong, kept doing what we're doing, and we continue believing in ourselves.”

Arsenal’s hard fought win must go down as a statement because they won at Villa who finished fourth last season, they won the Europa League and, despite a summer of change, Unai Emery’s men are back in the Champions League.

‌



View 3 Images Eze played a big role in Arsenal's win over Villa

The Gunners are yet to concede a goal in either of their two Premier League games and also kept a clean sheet against Manchester City in the Community Shield.

Eze said: “We want to continue keeping clean sheets. That gives us a good platform to go off. It gives us a lot of freedom as attackers so that’s good.”

‌



England star Eze also had a very different experience at Villa Park compared to last year. He was substituted at half time when they lost to Villa after Emiliano Buendia’s last-gasp winner. Eze took some blame for failing to track back on Matt Cash’s opening goal.

But this time, Eze came on for Christos Tzolis who was substituted at half time and it was Eze who made all the difference.

His strength and skill was crucial, he played a role in Bukayo Saka’s winner and overall formed a strong understanding with Riccardo Calafiori down the left.

‌



Arsenal did start the summer trying to strengthen the left and Tzolis has made a strong start. But they may finish it with Eze looking a strong candidate to play from the left which he insists he is ready to embrace.

Eze said: “You always want to help the team. You always want to put in a good performance. Ultimately you want to affect the game and help the team win. That's the main thing whether you start or come on.

“I think it's all part of football. It's all part of the game, and you can have moments like that go the other way. So it's about staying focused, staying present, being as effective as you can be.

‌



View 3 Images Guimaraes made his first Premier League appearance for Arsenal in Monday's win over Aston Villa (Image: Harry Murphy/Aston Villa FC)

“And as I say, whether you start or come on, you want to be the best version of yourself to help the team. And I think that's what I try to do every time.

“You want to learn, you want to keep on building, you want to improve every year. That's the main thing.

‌



“I think it's a different type of space, but ultimately it's just space that you're occupying. And sometimes I can find myself in a more comfortable position coming in from the left and being in that pocket there.

“So it's just about space, about finding yourself in nice positions to score. And if I'm inside or outside, that’s what I try to do.

“That's what the manager wants me to do. He wants me to affect the game and to be as effective as I can be, whether it's on the left or in the left pocket or on the right pocket, whatever it is.

‌



“He wants me to affect the game and to be active. So as long as I'm on the pitch, I'm there and ready to do it.

“For sure, Riccardo is a special player. He's so creative. He can take up special positions that are awkward for teams to defend against. You try to work off him, and he works off me well. It's a good relationship. As long as we can continue to build on that, it's going to be effective.”

Sports.title: Trainer involved in extraordinary betting coup suspended after winner fails drugs test
Sports.content:
Trainer involved in extraordinary betting coup suspended after winner fails drugs test

British bookmakers were among the victims of the gamble involving five horses, four of which won races in the US on the same day last month

View 2 Images One of two Monmouth Park winners trained by under investigation trainer has tested positive (Image: Getty Images)

A trainer involved in an extraordinary betting coup has been suspended after one of the winning horses tested positive for a banned substance.

‌



British bookmakers were among the targets of the significant gamble involving five horses, four of which won races on the same day in the US last month.

‌



The horses were dubbed ‘the Fair Hill Five’ after the Maryland training centre to which they had been shipped from Florida where they were prepared by little known trainer Angel Quiroz. The unusual betting activity around the horses and their dramatic improvement in form triggered an investigation by US racing regulator, the Horseracing Integrity and Safety Authority [HISA].

‌



On August 9, Quiroz sent The Great Amira to win by nine lengths at Monmouth Park at odds of 17-1 and took the next race with Tepeyac, who was around 4-1.

At Saratoga Classic Rock and M B’s Melanie Cares made nearly all the running in their races to triumph at 8-1 and 12-1. They were listed as trained by Ernesto Ochoa.

Days later Quiroz was notified that another horse in his care, not one of the August 9 runners, had tested positive for the banned substance albuterol.

‌



On Tuesday HISA provisionally suspended the trainer after the same prohibited substance was detected two other Quiroz horses, including from Monmouth Park winner Tepeyac following out-of-competition testing conducted four days after the victory.

View 2 Images HISA issued Angel Quiroz with a provisional suspension (Image: hiwu.org)

HISA said there were “no records in the HISA Portal reflecting the dispensation, prescription, or treatment of Albuterol for the Covered Horse, Tepeyac”.

Article continues below

“As of the date of this Notice, you are facing three (3) Anti-Doping Rule violations involving the Banned Substance, Albuterol.

“These alleged violations are actively being pursued by HIWU. The recent discovery of Banned Substances in multiple Covered Horses under your care – after you were on notice of the first alleged violation – presents an immediate threat of serious injury or death to Covered Horses or Riders.”

Each Anti-Doping Rule Violation involving a banned substance carries a two-year period of ineligibility and a $25,000 fine.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania

Final: Ukraine/Sweden vs Poland/Albania

Play-off Path C:

Semi-final: Turkey vs Romania

Semi-final: Slovakia vs Kosovo

Final: Slovakia/Kosovo vs Turkey/Romania

Play-off Path D:

Semi-final: Denmark vs North Macedonia

Semi-final: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland

Final: Czech Republic/Republic of Ireland vs Denmark/North Macedonia - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: Ex-British boxing champion Darren Barker shares heartfelt Ricky Hatton message as he sets off on epic 1,800-mile fundraising challenge
Sports.content:
Darren Barker has issued an emotional message about Ricky Hatton as he continues his inspiring 'The Longest Round' fundraising challenge, in memory of the boxing great.

Barker, former IBF world middleweight champion, set off from Edinburgh on Wednesday morning on a mega 1,800-mile endurance challenge to Morocco across land and sea.

The challenge sees him cycle from Edinburgh to Dover, swim the English channel (21 miles), cycle from Calais to Gibraltar before he ends off the adventure with an open-water swim across the Strait of Gibraltar into Morocco (nine miles).

The challenge will push Barker to the absolute limits, testing him both physically and mentally but he's determined to complete it for Ricky and 'for all the people out there suffering'.

Barker is raising funds for suicide prevention charity Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM), in which Hatton had been an ambassador of.

Darren Barker is currently on a 1,800-mile endurance challenge in honour of Ricky Hatton

And speaking ahead of the challenge, the 44-year-old said: 'Last September, I had the honour and the privilege to speak to Ricky Hatton on a podcast. And days later he wasn't with us, so it really struck home and hit hard. And made me really understand what a terrible illness mental health is. I want to do something for Ricky, I want to do something to spread awareness.

'I feel like I owe this to Ricky. He gave up his time to speak to me, so this is something I need to do for him, and I want to do - and I need to do for the bigger picture. I need to do this for all the people out there suffering, to know that it's OK to not be OK. I want to encourage these people to have these uncomfortable conversations, and hopefully save lives in the future.'

He added: 'He will always be a hero of mine. He was the man that brought the big nights to British boxing. The man that brought the big crowds.

'But away from boxing, he was so likeable - he was the man next door - everyone could relate to Ricky. So funny, charming, just a real good guy with a big heart and someone that people could look up to. He is massively missed.'

Barker spoke from the heart as he explained what 'The Longest Round' and CALM mean to him.

Barker spoke to Hatton on a podcast a few days before his friend was found dead at his home

He continued: 'It means an awful lot. It means that I, along with the team, and everybody else following this - that we have an opportunity to make a real difference here. This is about changing lives, helping people. This is bigger than swimming and cycling, this is a huge opportunity to try and make a difference, and that's what I want to do.

'You, I guess, go through your early stages of life, being selfish, and you're on your own journey, trying to fulfil dreams and aspirations to do this and that, and then you kind of - in my situation anyway - achieve that - and it's about what next. And for me, it feels right to help and just try and raise money and awareness for something now that has really resonated with me.

'Even myself as a retired fighter, grieving the loss of boxing, grieving the loss of my brother, my grandad - understanding that grief is a part of mental health. So along with everyone else, this isn't just me - I may be getting on the bike and in the sea - but this is all of us pulling together and being there for one another. Let's be nice to one another, let's be there, let's support. So much hardship in the world as it is, so if we all pull together - we're halfway there you know.'

Barker is being sponsored by Just Eat, alongside the likes of the Royal Navy, INEOS Grenadier, kp-pharma and Pretty Sailing, and they have been providing the former world champion with food daily to keep him going during this gruelling challenge.

'We've been fuelling heavily. Lots of protein, the carbs have been so important for the energy. Been eating lots and lots throughout the day. It has been quite difficult during the challenge but we've been snacking.

'Lots of gels, lots of electrolytes, just fuelling correctly and it has been pivotal because I could not do it without it. We've also had some brilliant Italians, lots of pasta, lots of chicken. It has been great, it has been thoroughly enjoyable.'

Any donations can be made to: https://www.justgiving.com/page/thelongestround

Sports.title: Where next for Moses Itauma? Filip Hrgovic's savage verdict has shattered the Mike Tyson hype as Britain's fallen prodigy begins his long road back, writes JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
Where next for Moses Itauma? Filip Hrgovic's savage verdict has shattered the Mike Tyson hype as Britain's fallen prodigy begins his long road back, writes JEFF POWELL

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The most alarming contribution to the inquest into the slaying of Moses came from the national hero of Croatia who was the real story of a Saturday night at the O2 which was dark for British boxing but dazzling to behold.

Filip Hrgovic said of our young Itauma: ‘No, I didn’t feel his power.’

That will be as devastating to the lad previously hailed as the next Mike Tyson as James Bond being told he is no longer attractive to women.

It will hurt even more than the punches which sent him reeling from domination to defeat and hospital on the evening he was supposed to become the second youngest world heavyweight champion of all time.

Power has been Moses Itauma’s middle name since he began felling giants like saplings. Suddenly, at 21, he is being likened to Samson who lost his mythological strength when he had a haircut.

Were there clues in how Hrgovic survived the first eight rounds of this IBF world title fight and countless punches, every one of which looked as if it would have knocked out a horse?

Moses Itauma saw his hope of becoming the second youngest heavyweight world champion ended by Filip Hrgovic

Hrgovic, right, declared afterwards that he 'didn't feel his power' in another blow to Itauma

To suggest as much would be to downplay the superhuman heart and phenomenal resilience of chin with which Hrgovic realised his own lifelong ambition of global glory. Just in time at 34.

Nevertheless, Itauma could not finish him off. Which brings other factors into issue. It is concerning, also, that Britain’s young lion should gas out on the first time in his career he was required to go beyond six rounds. Trainer Ben Davison finds himself under inquisition as to whether presumption of another early KO left Moses short on stamina build-up. Or did he simply punch himself out?

Whatever the reason, it was worrying to see one so young that exhausted as he staggered to extinction as early as the ninth round. Certainly Hrgovic put into words what many of us felt. That he was beaten in a large part by experience. The new champion who had vowed to ‘smash the kid’s face and send him back to high school’ had this to say after he had done just that: ‘He is a tremendous talent but he boxed like an amateur and must learn to fight like a professional.

‘With more experience he would have known he was winning every round and what he should have done was box out the fight to a points decision behind his jab. Not keep trying to knock me out. Although I did know he would tire the longer the fight went.’

But no power in his punches? Of being dropped once, a flash knock-down in the second round, Hrgovic said: ‘I didn’t feel it. He is very fast and caught me off balance with a punch I didn’t see.’

And so it would come to pass that in the battle of their ages it was from the kid’s corner that the white towel came fluttering in. By then not to great surprise. As early as the fifth round Itauma was beginning to grimace at the physical demands being made of him and the heavy hits he, too, was taking. In the eighth he launched a desperate assault which Hrgovic not only rode out but also inflicted damage of his own.

To his credit Itauma prodded out some punches at the start of the ninth but looked more like a fish floundering out of water. Hrgovic speared him with what he called ‘strength which came from Jesus Christ’.

So what next for he who was hailed as the next Mike Tyson? Hrgovic’s advice: ‘Several easier fights to gain more experience and rebuild his confidence. And I do think that with his speed of hand he will become a world champion one day.’

Hrgovic highlighted how he had used his experience to see off the challenge of Itauma

Hrgovic showed phenomenal resilience to achieve his lifelong dream at the age of 34

Hrgovic advised Itauma to take some easier fights to rebuild his confidence after the defeat
