Sports.title: Formula 1 fan’s video reveals the strange sound of super-clipping | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has repeatedly claimed fans of the sport either don’t know ‘clipping’ exists or don’t understand it.

Under the series’ current technical regulations, cars are so short of energy ay many tracks they are forced to slow significantly as they approach high-speed corners. This robs drivers of the challenge of attacking the championship’s most spectacular corners at full speed and denies fans the thrill of watching them.

One fan highlighted the problem during the British Grand Prix weekend. Silverstone is one of the quickest tracks on the calendar and Max Verstappen admitted he laughed when he first saw how poor the cars would perform at the circuit.

The result is exactly the kind of footage F1 is at pains to avoid showing in its broadcasts this year. Instead of attacking Silverstone’s fastest corners at full speed with the engines howling, the cars coast through quietly, with none of their former drama:

Formula 1

Sports.title: Janibek Corners Hamzah Sheeraz Before WBO Deadline
Sports.content:
Sheeraz has already built a possible defense for refusing the fight. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, he called the WBO’s ruling a “joke” and criticized the organization for rewarding Janibek after his positive test for meldonium.

The clean-sport objection has merit. The WBO shortened Janibek’s suspension, allowed him to move directly into a mandatory position at 168 pounds, and selected him over Jacob Bank despite Janibek never fighting in the division. Bank had actively campaigned at super middleweight and petitioned for the same opportunity.

Still, Sheeraz’s moral position also provides a convenient exit. He can vacate while claiming he refused to cooperate with a sanctioning body order he considers disgraceful, rather than admitting that Janibek presents too much danger for too little money.

Surrendering the title would harm Sheeraz’s reputation. He won the vacant belt against 39-year-old Alem Begic and struggled through a majority verdict over Simon Zachenhuber in his first defense. Leaving before facing Janibek would support the Kazakh’s claim that Sheeraz was only a “champion by name.”

Facing Janibek carries the greater career risk. He is a precise southpaw counterpuncher with the power to punish the defensive lapses Sheeraz showed against Zachenhuber. A decisive loss would cost Sheeraz his belt and reduce his value for larger fights against Canelo Alvarez or Chris Eubank Jr.

The history makes an escape harder to disguise. Sheeraz withdrew from negotiations when the WBO ordered him to challenge Janibek at middleweight. After Sheeraz moved to 168 and became champion, Janibek followed him into the division.

Vacating can be presented as a principled business choice. Getting stopped by the opponent who pursued him through two weight classes would be far worse. Janibek has left Sheeraz to choose which consequence he is willing to accept.

Sports.title: Two Minutes in Tokyo: George Foreman Slaughters José Roman
Sports.content:
Roman had little chance of testing him. The Puerto Rican challenger stood 5-foot-10 and weighed between 196½ and 197 pounds, leaving him considerably smaller than the 6-foot-4, 219-pound champion. He had been outside the rankings when the fight was signed before being elevated to No. 9 by the WBA and WBC.

That placement gave the promotion official legitimacy, but it did not make Roman a genuine threat. Foreman was 38-0 with 35 knockouts and had just destroyed Frazier in two rounds to seize the championship. Roman brought a 43-7-1 or 44-7-1 record, depending on the source, with 21 knockouts.

Once the bell rang, even two minutes proved too long.

Foreman did not merely follow Roman and swing wildly. Under trainer Dick Sadler, he had learned to take broad lateral steps that closed escape routes. His lead hand served as more than a jab. He posted it against Roman, pushed him off balance, and turned him toward the right hand.

That rough leverage helped Foreman control opponents before the power punches landed. Some of it crossed into boxing’s gray area, particularly when he shoved or extended his lead arm, but Roman lacked the strength and composure to resist it.

The destruction of Frazier also followed Foreman into the ring. Roman knew that six knockdowns had reduced the previous champion to a helpless target. His tense movement and reluctance to commit gave Foreman little reason to respect anything coming back.

Foreman cut down the available space, drove Roman toward the ropes, and attacked his body. Roman fell along the ropes near the one-minute point, but referee Jay Edson initially treated it as a slip or loss of balance rather than a knockdown.

The decision became controversial when Foreman landed a right while Roman was sitting on the canvas. Roman’s manager, Bill Daly, and trainer, Al Braverman, jumped onto the apron demanding a disqualification. Edson ruled that Foreman had been following through and that the punch carried little force. Because the original fall was ruled a slip, Roman received neither a mandatory count nor additional recovery time.

The challenger rose, only to be dropped by a right hand. Roman made it up once more, but Foreman finished him with a right uppercut at exactly 2:00 of the opening round. Roman’s corner later called Foreman “the dirtiest fighter in the world,” while some members of the Tokyo crowd booed the abrupt ending.

Roman’s ranking exposed the business behind the defense. He was outside the WBA and WBC ratings when the fight was arranged, then elevated to No. 9 so the organizations could approve him as a challenger. The placement did not make him a mandatory contender or establish championship credentials. It allowed an overseas title defense to proceed against an opponent selected for limited risk.

Promoters advertised Foreman’s purse as $1 million, a figure that became attached to the fight in later records. Contemporary reporting placed his actual guarantee near $250,000, while other accounts and Foreman’s later recollections put his earnings in the $250,000 to $300,000 range. Roman received approximately $100,000.

Attendance reached roughly 7,500 to 8,000 in an arena capable of holding nearly twice that number. The midday Saturday scheduling and expensive tickets hurt local sales, leaving Japanese promoters braced for a financial loss despite televising the bout free to domestic viewers.

Foreman followed the Roman destruction by stopping Ken Norton in two rounds the next year. Across the Frazier, Roman, and Norton fights, he needed only five rounds to dispose of three heavyweights who had a combined 91 professional victories.

The two-minute result also concealed a flaw that Muhammad Ali later exploited. Foreman committed heavily to his power punches and expected resistance to collapse under the first sustained attack. Roman rewarded that approach by folding almost immediately.

Ali refused to provide the same response in Zaire the following year. He forced Foreman to keep punching after the quick finish failed to materialize, turning the champion’s aggression and confidence in his strength into an exhausting trap.

Foreman’s comeback decades later produced one of boxing’s greatest stories, capped by the heavyweight championship at age 45. Yet the older Foreman relied more on patience, positioning, and conservation. The 1973 version brought something more frightening: youth, crushing strength, and an appetite for immediate destruction.

Roman was never equipped to disprove it.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says Crawford Resents His Boxing Takeover
Sports.content:
“I gave my honest opinion, saying that he left a lot on the table. That’s all I said. Crawford is the one that’s always coming up and slightly hating on me little by little. In the meantime, you’re retired. You should be in Turks and Caicos chilling on a yacht, enjoying your family. He’s desperate, bro,” said Ryan to Fight Hub TV. “Nobody knows him outside of boxing, so he’s doing everything he can to continue his name. He actually likes the attention. I used to think Crawford didn’t, but now I know he does. He realized nobody cares after you retire.”

Ryan also dismissed Crawford’s presence at Benn’s gym. “I feel like I’ll beat your ass, so what are you going to teach him?” he said.

Their bad blood highlights the fundamental difference between the two men. Crawford pursued championships, pound-for-pound recognition, and technical supremacy. Garcia measures his position through audience size, financial leverage, and the ability to command boxing’s most valuable dates.

Crawford built the greater traditional legacy, but Ryan attracts the larger mainstream audience. If Garcia defeats Benn and becomes boxing’s leading commercial figure, he will have achieved something Crawford never managed despite accomplishing far more inside the ring.

Working with Benn does not necessarily prove Garcia’s accusation that Crawford craves attention. It may represent a retired fighter transferring his knowledge to another contender. Garcia has turned that mentorship into an insult, reducing Benn to a pupil who cannot be saved even by one of boxing’s finest technicians.

That approach also keeps Benn’s abilities outside the discussion. By treating the fight as a proxy battle with Crawford, Garcia portrays him as little more than the vehicle for another man’s resentment.

The claim brings considerable risk. Garcia’s argument carries force only if he beats Benn. A loss would damage his attempt to place drawing power above championships while giving Crawford every reason to question both his boxing and his self-appointed status.

The message was simple: Crawford had his run and should either return to face someone such as Jaron Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr. or stay quiet in retirement.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Faces Duty as Oleksandr Usyk Exits
Sports.content:
The champion would naturally prefer a larger fight. Revenge against Dubois carries commercial value after Hrgovic’s stoppage loss to him in 2024, while a unification would pay considerably more than defending against Sanchez. The IBF mandate leaves little room for shopping around unless Sanchez accepts another step-aside agreement.

Dubois first has his own business to settle. He defends the WBO title against Fabio Wardley in their October 17 rematch at London’s O2 Arena. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round of their May meeting, but the punishment he absorbed makes the return dangerous. Hrgovic cannot build his plans around Dubois retaining.

Oleksandr Usyk is operating outside that championship traffic. The former unified champion is targeting Deontay Wilder for a final fight in the United States in 2027. It offers Usyk one more famous name, but little clarity about the division’s best heavyweight.

Usyk struggled more than anticipated against boxing novice Rico Verhoeven in May. He trailed on one scorecard and was level on the other two before producing an 11th-round stoppage. Wilder also carries the wear of a long career and no longer releases his right hand with the conviction that once made him boxing’s most feared puncher. Their proposed fight sells history and name recognition rather than determining the division’s leader.

The active championship race now belongs to Hrgovic, Dubois, WBA champion Murat Gassiev, and WBC interim champion Agit Kabayel. Gassiev stopped Peter Kadiru in six rounds in July, while Kabayel demolished Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. A Gassiev-Kabayel unification would immediately reduce the number of competing titleholders.

Hrgovic wants access to those lucrative fights, but Sanchez remains positioned directly in front of him. Beating Itauma won Hrgovic the belt. Defeating his mandatory would prove that he can keep it.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Waits for the Winner of Canelo-Mbilli
Sports.content:
Martinez was much more effective and landed the harder punches. Lester had the support of the Guatemalan people with a healthy attendance of 6,848 at the USC Galen Center. The interim WBC super middleweight champion is the only boxing champion of any kind for Guatemala; Martinez is held in high esteem, receiving the full support of his country. After the victory, he celebrated at Lafayette Park at the Festival Chapin with his fellow countrymen.

ProBox promoter Garry Jonas stated at the post-fight press conference they’re exploring the options of holding a Lester Martinez fight at a soccer stadium somewhere in Guatemala, hopefully for January of 2027. The energy and crowd at the Galen Center was electrifying as the crowd would erupt in cheers every time Lester would land a big punch.

Holding an event in Guatemala would definitely draw a crowd. Lester is becoming a bigger star with every fight, and if he’s able to secure a fight with the winner of the Canelo Alvarez-Christian Mbilli fight, he would only become that much bigger. Trainer Esau Dieguez said of the fight, “The truth is we would like to face the winner, but because of name recognition and what it would bring, we would like to fight Canelo. Being that we already fought Mbilli, but I expect Canelo to win. I think Canelo will win, I hope we can make the fight. I know the WBC may beat around the bush, but our hope is Lester will fight for the full world title.”

It was the fight against Mbilli that raised Lester’s profile and introduced him to the world. Although it was ruled a draw, there are many who believe Martinez should have been awarded the decision. Lester stood toe-to-toe with the power puncher, exchanging punch for punch with him. Martinez outlanded Mbilli 412 to 273 in total punches, outlanding him in 9 of 12 rounds (Compubox).

He tried securing the rematch with Christian, but the fight never materialized. Expecting a tough fight against the Canelo-Mbilli winner, Lester said, “I think for now I will relax, but I know what is coming will be more difficult, and we will prepare for it.”

Knowing that he will have to perform at his absolute best against whomever the winner may be. Lester has proven he has the skills to compete at the championship level, and he has the full support of an entire country with him in Guatemala; they want nothing more than to have their first full world champion.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Questions Daniel Dubois’ Sudden Attitude
Sports.content:
“It’s way too early for all of this. Last time I saw him, we shook hands. We congratulated each other on a great fight. I lost and took it on the chin, but then he turned up with a bit of attitude. I was like, ‘Hang on, what’s going on here?’ But if that’s what he needs to do to get himself geared up for another fight, if you know what war you went through last time, if that’s what he’s got to do to get himself in the right frame of mind, then be my guest. I’m just going to stay cool as a cucumber,” Wardley said to DAZN.

Confidence comes partly from Wardley’s two fights with Frazer Clarke. Their first meeting ended in a draw after 12 exhausting rounds, but he changed his approach and demolished Clarke in the opening round of their second encounter.

That comparison also exposes the danger in Wardley’s thinking. An explosive start solved the Clarke puzzle, but it contributed to his defeat against Dubois. After dropping Dubois twice, Wardley burned through his energy trying to force the stoppage. His output and defensive discipline declined as the rounds passed, allowing Dubois to take control with his jab before finishing an exhausted opponent.

Those knockdowns also demonstrated that hurting Dubois does not guarantee he will unravel. He used the jab to regain his balance, interrupt Wardley’s attacks, and buy the recovery time needed to survive the crisis. Clarke never received that opportunity in his rematch.

A different result will require more than another fast start. Wardley must shorten his right hand, recover his guard after throwing it, and resist loading up during pocket exchanges. His eagerness to finish left his head exposed to Dubois’ counters throughout their first fight.

The decisive adjustment will be psychological as much as technical. Wardley cannot allow two knockdowns, another roaring crowd, or Dubois showing vulnerability to convince him the fight is already won. Remaining “cool as a cucumber” during a face-off is easy. Maintaining that restraint after hurting Dubois will determine if the rematch produces a different result.

Sports.title: Hrgovic Shows Why Joe Joyce Keeps Fighting
Sports.content:
Hrgovic reversed the result as a professional in April 2025, winning a 10-round unanimous decision. The Croatian has since stopped Moses Itauma in the ninth round to capture the vacant IBF belt, showing how quickly one major result can transform an aging heavyweight’s career.

That example may reinforce Joyce’s belief that he can do something similar. If he survives an early attack and overwhelms a recognizable opponent late, one fortunate result might return him to contention. The immediate difficulty is finding that fight. Five defeats in six appearances leave promoters with little reason to offer him a major name without a rebuilding win first.

His former intimidation has also disappeared. Joyce’s pressure once forced opponents to expend energy while backing away because they doubted they could hurt him. Zhilei Zhang broke that psychological advantage by stopping him twice. Suslenkov then held his ground, committed to power punches, and treated Joyce as a target who could be hurt rather than an advancing force who had to be escaped.

As a result, the style Joyce used during his best professional years no longer works the same way. He was never difficult to hit, but his punch resistance allowed him to accept clean shots while exhausting opponents with his jab, size, and output. Once rivals stop fearing that exchange, his slow entries give them repeated chances to load up before he reaches punching range.

Excess weight has become another obstacle. Joyce scaled 255 pounds for his professional debut against Ian Lewison in 2017, already looking slower than he had during his amateur years. He reached a career-high 289 for July’s stoppage loss to Artem Suslenkov.

For comparison, Hrgovic arrived lighter against Itauma. Under Abel Sanchez, he dropped from 248¼ pounds against David Allen to 236¼. He looked more agile and preserved enough energy to take control after Itauma exhausted himself.

He may need to work gradually toward the 260-pound range as a starting point before SugarHill Steward can determine how much mobility and sustained output remain.

His recent record also changes how promoters will view him. A 40-year-old who has lost five of six is more likely to be offered as a test for a younger heavyweight than positioned for his own title run. Accepting that role may produce another recognizable fight, but Joyce would enter as the opponent rather than the investment. His best chance of changing that calculation is to return lighter and defeat a domestic name before another prospect’s team comes calling.

Shedding weight cannot make Joyce young again. It can remove an unnecessary burden and give him a better chance of earning the type of opening Hrgovic just seized.

Sports.title: Hearn Puts Jaron Ennis-Josh Kelly Fight At 80%
Sports.content:
Matchroom also controls both sides, sparing Hearn the promotional conflict that often delays major unifications. Final details still need to be settled, but there is no rival promoter protecting a separate television agreement.

The recovery timetable may determine how quickly the fight can be completed. Kelly suffered a nose injury against Agyarko in late July and later underwent minor surgery. A November date would leave limited time for the injury to heal before Kelly begins heavy sparring and prepares to absorb Ennis’ power.

The IBF champion has another reason to accept the biggest offer available. Kelly narrowly defeated Murtazaliev and then endured a difficult defense against Agyarko. Remaining in the IBF rotation would expose him to contenders such as Brandon Adams, Israil Madrimov, Nikita Tszyu, and a possible Murtazaliev rematch without offering the same purse or recognition.

Beyond the third belt, Kelly’s counterpunching and movement would test the defensive openings Ennis showed during his stoppage victory over Xander Zayas. Boots recovered after Zayas hurt him, eventually breaking the young champion down. Kelly is more comfortable slowing the action and forcing an aggressive opponent to lead.

Ennis remains the favorite due to his faster combinations, finishing power, and inside attack. Kelly must control the distance for 12 rounds without repeating the lapses that made his last two fights dangerously close.

Adding Kelly’s IBF belt to his WBA and WBO titles would leave only WBC champion Sebastian Fundora between Ennis and undisputed status. Hearn’s 80% estimate is encouraging, but a missing date and venue prevent the matchup from being treated as complete.

Ghana News.title: GIS urges public to channel donations to social welfare and credible NGOs instead of street beggars
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) is urging members of the public to stop giving alms directly to migrant beggars, particularly children, following its latest anti-human trafficking operation in the Greater Accra and Ashanti Regions.

The service says direct donations may be sustaining organised begging networks that exploit vulnerable migrants and children.

The appeal comes after GIS apprehended 1,055 people during the intelligence-led operation, including 662 children, 248 women and 145 men in an operation on August 29.

According to the service, some Ghanaian nationals are also suspected of acting as local agents for the exploitative begging networks.

The Comptroller-General of Immigration, Samuel Basintale Amadu, says removing the financial incentive from street begging will help reduce the profitability of organised networks and discourage traffickers from exploiting vulnerable people.

This was contained in a statement signed by Deputy Commissioner of Immigration (DCI) Maud Anima Quianoo dated August 29.

GIS is therefore encouraging members of the public who wish to support vulnerable persons to channel their donations through the Department of Social Welfare, recognised children’s homes, credible non-governmental organisations or other authorised charitable organisations.

The service says the move will ensure that assistance reaches people in need through appropriate structures while supporting efforts to combat human trafficking and exploitative street begging.

The 1,055 people apprehended during the operation have been transferred to a designated holding centre for profiling and immigration processing.

GIS says it is working with relevant stakeholders, including the Ministry of Gender and Social Protection, to ensure that victims, particularly children, receive appropriate care, protection and support throughout the removal process.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian businesses cautiously optimistic about 2026 performance – Chamber
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian businesses have remained resilient and cautiously optimistic about their performance in the first half of 2026, with improved macroeconomic conditions providing some relief to the private sector.

Stephane Miezan, President of the Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI), said the first half of the year had been relatively good compared with the same period in 2025, citing improvements in the stability of the cedi, inflation and interest rates.

Mr Miezan observed that the improved economic conditions had created a better environment for businesses to plan, although global developments and domestic operating challenges continued to require caution.

He made the observation at a media forum powered by the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA), where he assessed the performance and prospects of Ghana’s business community.

He said businesses could not afford to be overly optimistic because developments in the global economy, including geopolitical tensions, could affect inflation, energy prices and business operations in Ghana.

Mr Emmanuel Doni-Kwame, Secretary-General of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) Ghana, indicated that the economy had achieved some level of stability, particularly in foreign exchange, which had improved predictability and created room for businesses to undertake longer-term planning.

Mr Doni-Kwame, however, cautioned that Ghana remained part of the global economy and could therefore be affected by international developments, particularly those affecting energy and trade.

Mr Doni-Kwame said investor confidence was improving, stressing, however, that infrastructure and connectivity remained critical to sustaining investment.

He said businesses required efficient road, rail and other transport networks to move raw materials from production areas to factories and finished goods to ports and markets.

He noted that infrastructure and inadequate connectivity could undermine Ghana’s efforts to attract and sustain investment despite improving investor confidence, stressing that infrastructure remained critical to investment because businesses needed reliable transportation networks to move raw materials, finished products and other goods efficiently.

He said that while investor confidence had improved, the country needed to accelerate infrastructure development and improve connectivity within Ghana and across the West African sub-region.

According to him, an investor whose raw materials were located in the middle of the country would consider the cost and efficiency of transporting them to factories and ultimately to the ports before committing capital.

He said improved infrastructure would therefore strengthen the country’s competitiveness and make investment more attractive, and therefore called for improved connectivity along major regional corridors, including the Abidjan-Lagos corridor, to facilitate trade and investment across West Africa.

Mr Doni-Kwame further stated that the private sector also required improvements in sea transport and other logistics systems to reduce the cost and time associated with moving goods.

He also called for measures to reduce delays at Ghana’s ports, particularly delays associated with inspections by multiple agencies, and proposed better coordination among the agencies responsible for inspections, saying a coordinated inspection timetable could reduce congestion and shorten turnaround times.

He said reducing delays at the ports was important because time and logistics costs ultimately affected businesses and consumers.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Reference Rate drops to 10.18% in September, could ease borrowing costs
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Reference Rate (GRR), the benchmark used by commercial banks to price loans, has dropped marginally from 10.61% in August to 10.18% in September 2026.

The latest figure represents a 0.43 percentage-point decline over the past month.

The reduction is based on JOYBUSINESS calculations using the industry-approved formula and market data from industry players.

Drivers of reduction

The decline was largely influenced by lower Treasury bill and interbank rates.

The Treasury bill rate fell from 5.7881% to 4.8856%, while the interbank rate declined from 10.23% to 10.20%.

The Bank of Ghana’s Monetary Policy Rate, another key component used in calculating the GRR, remained unchanged during the review period.

The Ghana Reference Rate is calculated using these three variables and serves as the base benchmark for pricing loans across the banking industry.

Impact

The marginal decline could offer some relief to borrowers with variable-rate loan facilities, as lending costs continue to ease.

Customers with fixed-rate loans, however, are unlikely to be affected by the latest reduction.

The development could also benefit new borrowers as banks compete to offer credit at lower rates.

Average lending rates have fallen to around 15%, while some customers are reportedly accessing credit at rates between 11% and 12.5%.

This reflects increased competition among banks and improved financing conditions for selected borrowers.

The Ghana Reference Rate has recorded mixed movements throughout 2026.

The benchmark stood at 11.71% in March before declining to 10.06% in April. It eased further to 10.03% in May and 10.02% in June before rising to 10.59% in July.

It increased further to 10.61% in August before falling to 10.18% in September.

Introduced in 2017 by the Bank of Ghana in collaboration with the Ghana Association of Banks, the Ghana Reference Rate was designed to provide a transparent and uniform benchmark for determining lending rates across Ghana’s banking sector.

Ghana News.title: Chief Imam backs optional Arabic in public schools
Ghana News.content:
The Office of the National Chief Imam has backed the introduction of Arabic as an optional subject in public schools.

‎It said the policy would give students valuable linguistic skills for global engagement and urged addressing concerns about the teaching of Arabic through constructive dialogue.

‎A press statement signed by Dr Abubakari Mohammed Marzuq Azindoo, Personal Assistant to the National Chief Imam, said Arabic was a global language used in diplomacy, science and commerce, rather than a religious identity or practice.

‎The statement followed a recent announcement by Mr Haruna Iddrisu, Minister of Education, to introduce Arabic and Chinese as optional subjects in public schools.

‎Some stakeholders have raised concerns about the policy, citing the perceived neglect of Ghanaian languages in favour of foreign languages.

‎However, the Office said: “an increasingly interconnected global economy, equipping the youth with diverse linguistic skills is a strategic investment in their future,” the statement said.

‎It noted that Arabic was one of the six official languages of the United Nations and a major language of communication across economically vibrant regions of the world.

‎The Office commended the Ministry of Education for introducing a standardised curriculum through the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), saying it would provide quality assurance for students who opted to study the language.

‎It said the curriculum would also enable students to participate effectively in international diplomacy, trade and research.

‎The Office welcomed the Ministry’s clarification that Arabic remained strictly optional and was neither compulsory nor intended to undermine the secular character of Ghana’s public education system.

‎It said Ghana’s constitutional order guaranteed religious freedom while prohibiting the establishment of a state religion, and urged that public discussion of the policy be guided by facts.

‎The statement compared Arabic to foreign languages such as French, German, and Spanish, saying that it had enriched academic development without altering students’ cultural or religious identities.

‎It urged educationists, policymakers and the public to approach the policy objectively and verify information from credible sources to guard against misinformation and disinformation.

‎The Office reaffirmed its commitment to working with the Ministry of Education, the Ghana Education Service and other relevant institutions to promote an inclusive, peaceful and globally competitive education system.

Ghana News.title: Mahama lauds Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s pioneering role towards NAM formation
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama has lauded the pioneering role of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, towards the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to steer an independent path during the Cold War era.

Speaking at the 65th Anniversary Conference of NAM in Belgrade, Serbia, President Mahama also paid tribute to other pioneering leaders of the NAM, such as President Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of India, President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, and President Sukarno of Indonesia.

He underscored that Belgrade holds a distinguished place in the history of international relations.

“Sixty-five years ago, leaders of newly independent and developing nations gathered here at a defining moment in world affairs, united by a shared determination to safeguard their sovereignty and independence, oppose colonialism and foreign domination, promote peaceful coexistence, and contribute to the emergence of a more just, equitable, and peaceful world order,” he stated.

He reiterated that the history of Ghana’s anti-colonial struggle and the history of the Non-Aligned Movement were inextricably linked, a connection Ghana takes immense pride in.

President Mahama said Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, was among the foremost leaders of the generation that gave political expression to the Non-Aligned Movement in the historic Belgrade Conference in 1961.

He said that alongside President Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of India, President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, and President Sukarno of Indonesia, they came together at a time when the world was sharply divided by the Cold War rivalry and newly independent nations faced the danger of exchanging colonial subordination for dependence on competing power blocs.

He said that Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s vision was clear and that Ghana’s independence had to be matched by an independent foreign policy and an unwavering commitment to the sovereignty and self-determination of nations.

President Mahama said Dr Kwame Nkrumah believed that the newly independent states must have the freedom to determine their own course, maintain constructive relations with all countries, and exercise independent judgment on matters of international concern.

He said in articulating this vision, Dr Kwame Nkrumah declared, “we neither face east or west, we face forward”.

Adding that that profound and powerful declaration defined and articulated with clarity Ghana’s position at a defining moment in world history.

President Mahama said Ghana chose not to be drawn into the geopolitical rivalry between the power blocs.

He said Ghana chose instead to look forward to peace, to sovereignty, and to the freedom of nations to determine their own destinies.

“We want to be friends of all and enemies to none. The vision of Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah drew strength from the Historic Asian-African Conference held at Bandung, Indonesia in 1955, which laid an important political and structural foundation for the emergence of the Non-Aligned Movement.”

President Mahama said although the Gold Coast had not yet attained independence, Dr Kwame Nkrumah ensured that our voice was present at this conference.

He said the Gold Coast delegation, led by Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s close associate, Mr Kojo Botsio, joined the representatives of Asia and Africa in advancing the causes of decolonisation, sovereign equality, peaceful coexistence, and African-Asian solidarity.

The President said Ghana, therefore, in 1961 came to Belgrade with a tradition of engagement already shaped by the Bandung Conference, a tradition that connected our struggle for independence with the wider determination of newly emerging nations to secure an independent voice in world affairs.

“Sixty-five years after the historic Belgrade Conference that gave birth to the Non-Aligned Movement, Ghana is honoured to be present once again here in this historic city of Belgrade, which occupies a profound significance in our shared journey,” he said.

“Our presence here today provides an opportunity for us to reflect on the principles that inspired the founding of the Non-Aligned Movement, and in particular the vision, the leadership, and enduring contribution of our leaders of the time whose statesmanship helped define our affirmed conviction that newly independent nations must be free to determine their own destinies and to contribute on equal terms to the shaping of a more peaceful, just, and balanced international order.”

President Mahama said the world had changed profoundly since that first conference in 1961.

He emphasised that the end of the Cold War and the fall of the Berlin Wall opened a new page in international relations, but the pressures that could constrain the strategic autonomy of developing countries to make their own determination have not disappeared.

He noted that they now manifest themselves through renewed geopolitical competition, economic vulnerabilities, and unequal access to finance and technology, climate change, and an international architecture in which the voice of the global South was still not adequately reflected in world affairs.

President Mahama said in the tradition of Kwame Nkrumah, they understand non-alignment as a policy of positive, principled, and active engagement.

“As he aptly stated, our politics of positive neutrality is not passive or neutral politics. This is affirmative politics based on our firm belief in positive action,” he said.

President Mahama said it was this spirit of positive action that must continue to guide our non-aligned movement.

He said in an increasingly fragmented and multipolar world, the non-aligned movement must preserve its strategic autonomy and resist the pressures of the politics of power blocs.

“We must neither be silent spectators of global developments nor instruments of competing geopolitical interests,” he said

“Rather, we must be an independent, collective voice for peace, dialogue, disarmament, development, and justice, capable of influencing the international system and advancing a more representative and equitable global order.”

He said however, Ghana reaffirms that non-alignment must never be understood as neutrality in the face of injustice, conflict, or the erosion of international law. He said the Movement remains highly relevant in today’s international system, and although it emerged during the Cold War as a political movement, its role had evolved to address contemporary economic, political, and developmental challenges.

Adding that NAM continues to have an important role in advancing the interests of the Global South and promoting a fairer and more equitable international economic order.

President Mahama said with its broad membership, NAM provides developing countries with a strong collective voice in the multilateral system.

He noted that it could further strengthen South-South cooperation and advance common positions on development, finance, trade, climate change, debt, technology, and the reform of global financial architecture.

“Looking ahead, we must build on this historical legacy while adapting to this changing world,” President Mahama stated.

Ghana News.title: UK pledges additional £50 million to help contain Ebola outbreak in Congo
Ghana News.content:
Britain said on Tuesday it would provide more than £50 million ($67.56 million) ​in new funding to support ‌efforts to contain an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where confirmed ​cases have surpassed 6,000 in the ​country's largest-ever epidemic.

Britain allocated up to £20 ⁠million to the Ebola response in ​May, and the latest funding brings ​its total contribution to £78 million.

The funding will support disease surveillance, frontline health workers, treatment access, ​infection control, community outreach and ​safe burials, Britain's Foreign Office said.

British public health ‌experts ⁠have been deployed in Congo to support the efforts.

"As the outbreak intensifies, we are accelerating our response to ​match the ​pace and ⁠scale of the challenge," Britain's Minister for Africa Kirsty ​McNeill said.

The epidemic — the second-largest ​and ⁠fastest-spreading on record — was caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus, ⁠for ​which there are no ​approved vaccines or treatments.

Ghana News.title: Oil prices extend gains as US and Iran trade fresh strikes
Ghana News.content:
Oil prices rose in early trading on Wednesday, extending the previous session's surge, as concerns over supply disruptions intensified after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, dimming hopes for a quick easing of tensions in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures rose 75 cents, or 0.8%, to $95.40 a barrel by 0345 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.66.

Both contracts soared more than $4 on ​Tuesday, marking Brent's largest gain since July 24 and WTI's largest since July 23.

The U.S. said it had ​launched a series of airstrikes against targets in Iran overnight, prompting a response from Tehran, in ⁠the most serious escalation of the conflict between the two countries in weeks.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the ​U.S. attacks would further restrict traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that carried about one-fifth of the ​global oil consumed before the conflict and which Iran has effectively closed to commercial shipping.

"Developments in recent days brought risks to regional oil supplies back into focus...We’ve seen oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz despite the stalemate between the US and Iran, but rising ​tensions clearly put crossings at risk," said ING analysts in a client note.

The IRGC also said it had targeted a U.S. ​military base in Jordan with ballistic missiles that it claimed had killed a large number of U.S. forces, while Iranian state media ‌reported ⁠a large-scale drone attack on a U.S. base in Bahrain in response to the American strikes.

Jordan's military said its air defences intercepted 10 of 13 ballistic missiles that entered its airspace, while two U.S. officials said no American casualties had been reported so far from the attacks. Separately, Kuwait said its armed forces were responding to hostile drone activity.

The latest ​exchange followed a weekend flare-up ​in hostilities, the first ⁠since July, and came after attacks on two tankers departing the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, causing further disruptions to oil supplies and forcing traders to seek alternative crude shipments.

"The ​oil market is no longer pricing just the risk of war; it is increasingly ​pricing the cost ⁠of an unresolved war," said Priyanka Sachdeva, Phillip Nova's head of market insights.

"Until there is clear evidence that negotiations can produce a lasting resolution and that normal oil flows through the Strait are returning, the risk premium in crude is likely to ⁠remain elevated."

Meanwhile, ​in the U.S., the world's largest oil producer, crude inventories fell by ​2.6 million barrels in the week ended August 28, while distillate stocks, which include diesel and heating oil, declined by 265,000 barrels, market sources said, ​citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

Ghana News.title: Dropbox says about 5,000 accounts compromised in August hack
Ghana News.content:
Dropbox said on Tuesday that around 5,000 accounts were compromised last month, with hackers viewing ​and downloading content stored on the cloud-storage ‌platform.

Here are a few details:

Some Dropbox users received an email from the company on Monday notifying them that their accounts ​have been accessed without authorisation between August ​4 and August 21, Dropbox confirmed after Bloomberg News ⁠reported the hack earlier in the day.

Hackers accessed ​files in fewer than a third of the compromised accounts, ​the company said.

Shares of Dropbox fell around 2.4% in extended trading on Tuesday.

Dropbox told Reuters that it identified unauthorised access ​affecting accounts linked to a Lenovo ID ​that did not have its two-factor authentication enabled, prompting the company ‌to terminate all sessions authenticated through a Lenovo ID.

The company has removed any links between Lenovo IDs and Dropbox accounts and changed its systems so ​that users must ​enter their ⁠Dropbox password before accessing an account through Lenovo.

Dropbox said it had reported ​the incident to data protection regulators.

Lenovo identified ​a "legacy ⁠integration" between Lenovo ID and Dropbox that "could be used to improperly authenticate certain Dropbox accounts". The company ⁠said ​its own customers were not ​affected and that an investigation was ongoing.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
