World.title: Trump’s theory of global power faces a reckoning in Iran and Canada
World.content:
Donald Trump’s presidency rests on the premise that he and the United States are so powerful that allies and enemies alike must submit to his will.

His break with decades of US foreign policy doctrine is laced through his speeches and national security strategies. It was best explained in January by top aide Stephen Miller, who told CNN’s Jake Tapper that “iron laws” dictate a real world that is “governed by strength, that is governed by force, that is governed by power.”

But the philosophy faces its most serious tests in deepening showdowns with Iran and Canada.

Iran has defied the might of the US military for six months in a war Trump started but has been unable to end.

Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney, who shut down trade talks with Washington, has meanwhile argued more forcefully than any other Western leader that the US under Trump “has changed.” He told his country Saturday that Trump was using “economic integration as a weapon.”

It is a commentary on the extreme disruption of the Trump era that Canada, one of America’s most loyal friends, has found itself in a similar state of economic warfare with the US as Iran, one of Washington’s worst foes.

But the Trump administration left no doubt Monday what it wants as it fights a trade war with Ottawa and a shooting war with Tehran.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an “economic onslaught” against Iran’s global financial connections, drawing an analogy with the D-Day invasion that turned the tide in World War II.

Trump, meanwhile warned on social media that “The U.S.A. will always be far bigger, richer, and stronger than Canada.” He added: “Someone should get these clowns to ‘fall in line.’”

President Donald Trump speaks during a campaign rally for in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on August 21. Evan Vucci/Reuters

Will Trump stay the course?

The administration’s rhetoric Monday suggests that Trump is now sending the US economy to war.

Trump hopes to chalk up a lopsided trade deal with Canada and to finally bring about the downfall of Iran’s regime.

But the way forward is uncertain on both fronts because the president often backs down when the economic consequences of his attempts to assert his authority become clear.

Any prolonged US effort to prevail over Canada and Iran — and third-party nations sanctioned in his bid to shut down Tehran’s financial networks — could trigger retaliation that causes energy and food price hikes for US consumers. It could also rattle US markets at a time when some investors fear a bond crisis.

If Monday’s threats are the precursor to more TACOs (“Trump always chickens out”), the president will undermine his own power and the nation’s, and slip closer to lame-duck status as difficult midterm elections loom in November.

What Trump could achieve by strangling Iran’s economy

Bessent’s announcement was the latest US effort to find a new way out of the war with Iran.

But the D-Day analogy seemed tonally off, given the terrible sacrifices made by American soldiers to liberate Europe. And unlike Bessent, allied commander Gen. Dwight Eisenhower didn’t spent days in 1944 previewing a massive attack only to follow through with new threats of sanctions and no timeline.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent points as reporters raise their hands during a news conference at the Treasury Department in Washington, DC, on August 24. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

Still, administration skeptics often ignore the genuine power that Trump could wield by clever use of economic warfare.

A truly global effort to cut off Iran’s pathways to finance and trade could inflict extreme damage on an already devastated economy.

“It can work if we can get the buy-in of our partners,” Max Meizlish, a former senior Treasury official, said on CNN News Central Monday, specifically referring to Bank Melli, an Iranian commercial bank controlled by the government that operates in France, Germany and elsewhere and is a cog in Iran’s efforts to evade sanctions.

Kenneth Rogoff, a former IMF chief economist who is now a Harvard University chair, told CNN’s Richard Quest: “Fundamentally, sanctions work if you can get most of the world behind you. But if they’re not, it’s very hard.”

Trump might have had more success with such an approach before alienating US allies with a war many regard as unwise and illegal.

And the White House may be misreading its capacity to influence events inside Tehran. Signs of disagreement between pragmatists and hardliners over the economy are encouraging. But Washington has for decades over-read such tea leaves and assumed regime collapse would follow.

Most damagingly, the Trump administration is sending signals that it may not be serious about its own policy.

There was no immediate action against an array of Chinese banks that facilitate Beijing’s trade in cut-price Iranian oil. China has already said it will defend its interests — code for potential retaliatory reaction against the US that could further raise prices and anger US voters. It showed last year in threatening to curtail rare earth mineral exports critical to the US defense and tech industries that it can counter Trump’s power.

And the US leader also has a big date circled on his calendar — the state visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping next month. It’s hard to see him souring the atmosphere before then.

In a revealing moment, Bessent only reinforced doubts about the administration’s staying power. He was asked why he was not immediately imposing secondary sanctions on entities that deal with Iran.

“Well, we are giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behavior; why would I want to blow up the global financial system?” he replied.

A worker secures a coil of steel at an ArcelorMittal Dofasco facility in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, on August 24. Cole Burston/AFP/Getty Images

Canada sees a showdown that goes beyond a trade dispute

The administration is less wary of sanctioning the manufacturers of Canadian hockey sticks than Chinese banks.

And cross-border rhetoric is increasingly toxic.

“We have to remember, Canada is a state. Sorry, Freudian slip. That was actually an accident,” Vice President JD Vance said Monday.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford said at a news conference that “I have a lot of real estate on my ass, so (Trump) has a lot of room to kiss my ass.”

Venting can sometimes create political room to relaunch talks.

But Canadians believe they are embroiled in more than a trade dispute.

Drew Dilkens, the mayor of Windsor, Ontario, just across from Detroit, explained the damage inflicted by Trump’s 51st-state claims. “When you say it the first time, perhaps you can laugh it off, but it was the doubling down and certainly continuing to reinforce that,” he told CNN’s Brianna Keilar.

Ottawa said that, among other disputes, Carney ended trade talks after the US sought to water down its constitutional guarantees of bilingualism. Printing packaging for products sold in Canada in French as well as English is an inconvenience for US firms. But it’s a validation of the cultural and linguistic diversity that keeps Canada whole. Carney also implied Washington sought to restrict trade deals that his government could make with third countries.

“We will not allow any nation to dictate our future,” Carney said Saturday.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney speaks at a new conference in Ottawa, Ontario, on August 22, after trade talks with the US collapsed. Dave Chan/AFP/Getty Images

As the smaller economy, Canada would suffer the most harm in a trade war with the US. But it can challenge American power. A long tariff duel could result in the mutually assured destruction of the auto industry on both sides of the border. And the growing impact of Canadian boycotts could weaken Republicans in key contests in border states Michigan and Maine, which could decide who controls the US Senate next year.

And in seeking to impose his dominance, Trump may have revealed another iron law of power that Miller did not mention back in January.

When people see their sovereignty and independence threatened by a hostile greater power, there is almost no price they will not pay.

World.title: Vance casts El-Sayed as ‘evil’ and tells him to ‘keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth’
World.content:
Vice President JD Vance said in Michigan on Monday that “there’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very, evil,” arguing that the state’s Democratic Senate nominee is symptomatic of a growing trend in America of fighting “for one group at the expense of others.”

His sharp criticism of El-Sayed — which included telling the Democrat to “keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth” — underscored how heated the rhetoric has become in this competitive Senate race, which could be critical in the larger battle for control of the chamber.

Vance cast the choice between El-Sayed and GOP nominee Mike Rogers as about who would fight for all Michiganders — even if they don’t agree 100% with Rogers — while obliquely suggesting that El-Sayed cared more about members of the Muslim community than other voters.

“There’s something about Abdul El-Sayed that is very, very evil and on the rise in the United States of America today, and it’s people who see themselves not as citizens of a common nation, fighting for every single person … but see themselves as fighting for one group at the expense of others,” Vance said at a rally in Sterling Heights hosted by MAGA Inc., a super PAC aligned with President Donald Trump.

“What I see is a man who has sympathy and compassion for people who share his religion, but have nothing for people who don’t. A person who will apologize for a murderer so long as he looks the right way, but will not understand the plight of an innocent child if that person has the wrong faith,” Vance said, calling on voters to “reject it in November” and back Rogers.

El-Sayed on Monday pushed back on Vance’s comments, casting the Trump administration and Republicans as the ones perpetrating evil.

“Evil is ripping healthcare away from working people in exchange for tax breaks for billionaires. Evil is making people pay more for groceries and gas while pushing for trade wars and actual war. Evil is dividing people for your own gain. Evil is selling out your morals for a little bit of power,” he said in a statement.

“Michigan is better than being lectured to by sock puppets from Ohio and Florida. We understand what’s at stake, and Michiganders will show you at the ballot box this November when we send Mike Rogers packing,” he added.

El-Sayed recently apologized for saying after a March attack on a Michigan synagogue that “violence is a cycle” and that “hurt people hurt people.” (The attacker lost family in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon a week before the Michigan attack.) At the time, El-Sayed also condemned the synagogue attack and antisemitism broadly.

Vance’s speech became more personal as he took aim at recent comments from El-Sayed that some viewed as racist. Earlier this month, the Democratic candidate responded to a clip of Vance at a rally referencing his late grandfather, “Papaw,” by mentioning second lady Usha Vance, who is the child of Indian immigrants and was raised Hindu.

“So do we think JD is taking Usha with him back in time to meet Papaw, or no…” El-Sayed wrote on X.

“I’d rather not talk about spouses at all,” El-Sayed told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins Monday evening on “The Source,” as he sought to clarify his comment about the vice president’s wife. “The point that I’ve been making about his wife is that he believes in a political philosophy that says that some people are somehow more American than others.”

Vance on Monday said El-Sayed has a “weird habit of talking about my family,” going on to lob a series of misleading claims at the Democrat — a pattern that’s emerged from the GOP since El-Sayed won the Senate nomination in early August, with some Republicans resorting to overtly Islamophobic attacks.

“My message to Abdul El-Sayed is: You can pal around with terrorist sympathizers, and you can say that America deserved 9/11, or you could empathize not with the children who were targeted at Temple Israel, but with the attacker,” Vance said.

He continued: “But whatever you want to talk about, Abdul, keep my wife’s name the hell out of your mouth, because she’s way out of your league.”

While El-Sayed campaigned during the primary with Hasan Piker — a far-left Twitch streamer who once suggested that the country “deserved” 9/11 — El-Sayed did not say that. Piker has since walked back the remark, saying it was “inappropriate,” and El-Sayed has downplayed his relationship with him.

Still, at a state party convention over the weekend, El-Sayed remained largely dismissive about concerns over his relationship with Piker, a strident critic of Israel, telling reporters, “This is not a campaign that is about a single streamer in California.”

This story has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Rashwan: Accurate, timely information vital to combating rumors
World.content:
Egypt’s Minister of State for Information Diaa Rashwan emphasized the vital importance of coordination among government spokespersons, media advisers, and print, broadcast and television media outlets to ensure the rapid flow of accurate information on state and community affairs.

He said providing official accounts of events, decisions, measures and achievements would help close information gaps and prevent the spread of rumors and false reports aimed at undermining state efforts and social stability.

Speaking at an expanded meeting attended by 35 government spokespersons and media advisers, Rashwan said improving their performance was part of presidential directives to enhance Egyptian media and strengthen its role in raising public awareness and positively influencing public opinion.

This requires government officials to provide information promptly and respond to media requests in order to present the facts and the views of state institutions, he added.

Rashwan also pointed to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s repeated calls for opening up the public sphere and allowing space for different opinions on issues and topics within the framework of the Constitution, the law and national interests.

Participants highlighted several challenges, including the spread of inaccurate information and fabricated reports on social media, as well as the reliance of some media outlets on social media as a source of information.

They also raised concerns that some newspapers and websites do not give sufficient attention to information provided by official sources.

The participants called for a clear definition of the roles and responsibilities of government spokespersons and media advisers, greater access to information within their institutions, and advanced training programs for spokespersons, media advisers, journalists and media professionals covering ministries and government institutions.

Rashwan said developing the performance of government spokespersons and media advisers was among the ministry’s main priorities and that training programs for various segments of the media sector were currently being prepared.

He added that the ministry would coordinate with government bodies and media organizations to establish clear mechanisms for continued cooperation and ensure the timely and adequate flow of information.

He also said the ministry would establish a framework for sustained coordination among government spokespersons and media advisers to prevent contradictions in the state’s media messaging.

He noted that several ministries and state bodies were working to regulate social media use and limit risks such as privacy violations.

Rashwan concluded by saying that efforts were underway to accelerate the issuance of a freedom of information law that would require government bodies to provide information to citizens, the public and the media, and regulate the ways in which such information is transmitted and shared.

World.title: Local Development Minister discusses development of nature reserves
World.content:
Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad discussed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, a number of projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.

She also stressed the need for regular follow-up of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards, along with establishing a continuous environmental monitoring plan.

The remarks came during the 76th meeting of the board of directors of the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) which discussed a number of issues related to developing the environmental work system, supporting environmental projects and investment, maximizing the sustainable utilization of natural resources and following up on the implementation of decisions and recommendations issued at previous board meetings. These efforts aim to enhance institutional performance and support the state’s efforts to protect the environment and improve citizens’ quality of life.

The meeting was attended by CEO of the EEAA Sherif Abdel Rahim as well as representatives of the ministries of defense, industry, foreign affairs and international cooperation, planning and economic development, water resources and irrigation, health and higher education and scientific research in addition to a number of environmental experts and officials from the ministry of local development and environment.

At the beginning of the meeting, Awad affirmed the ministry’s commitment to continuing to develop the environmental work system and improve performance, as well as supporting projects that contribute to environmental protection and the preservation of natural resources.

She stressed the importance of coordination and integration among all relevant authorities and accelerating the implementation of environmental policies and programs to ensure that plans are translated into tangible results on the ground.

She explained that the board began its session by approving the minutes of meeting No. 74 and reviewing the implementation status of the decisions and recommendations issued by it, as well as the implementation status of the decisions of meeting No. 75.

This reflects the ministry’s commitment to continuously monitoring implementation rates and enhancing institutional efficiency.

Awad also pointed out that, as part of the state’s drive to promote environmental investment and encourage the private sector to participate in developing natural destinations, the board discussed several projects and proposals for developing nature reserves in a manner that ensures the sustainable use of natural resources and supports ecotourism.

The board reviewed the technical and financial assessments, permit durations and technical and financial proposals concerning several applications submitted by companies seeking to invest in nature reserves, while preserving their geological and environmental characteristics.

Awad further stressed the need for regular monitoring of investment projects in nature reserves to ensure compliance with environmental requirements and standards.

She called for a continuous environmental monitoring plan, environmental awareness programs and measures to encourage visitors to adopt sustainable practices, while ensuring that environmental impact assessment studies are conducted and coordination is maintained with the EEAA and relevant authorities to safeguard biodiversity and ensure the sustainability of reserve resources.

Awad directed that new environmental projects should focus on generating tangible benefits for citizens and visitors by improving the quality of services provided in nature reserves, developing infrastructure and facilities and enhancing the visitor experience. This would increase the attractiveness of environmental destinations and support ecotourism while ensuring full protection of nature, biodiversity and natural resources.

Awad also directed efforts to create a favorable environment for the private sector to expand environmental investments and encourage projects that generate economic returns and provide job opportunities for members of local communities, while ensuring compliance with environmental requirements and standards. This would strike a balance between supporting investment and maximizing the benefits of natural resources while protecting and sustaining them.

World.title: PM discusses with Fujairah officials steps to complete implementation of “Fujairah-Alamein” oil, gas company project
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, the attention that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi is giving to the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company, describing it as a promising strategic project whose agreement was recently signed.

He noted that completing the procedures for establishing Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company and holding its inaugural general assembly meeting at the Al-Hamra Petroleum Port, affiliated with the Western Desert Petroleum Company (WEPCO) in New Alamein, comes within the framework of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting at the government headquarters in the New Capital with Director of the Fujairah Amiri Diwan Mohammed Saeed al Dhanhani to follow up the procedures and steps required to complete implementation of the project following the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company.

The meeting was attended by Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi.

Madbouly stressed the vital importance and the project’s multiple developmental dimensions in the energy sector.

He also emphasized the importance of accelerating efforts and intensifying joint work to expedite the establishment of a special free zone under the name “Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company” in New Alamein City. The company will engage in the storage and trading of petroleum products and crude oil and enter actual operational phases, in a manner that serves the mutual interests of both sides and reflects the depth of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

For his part, Dhanhani thanked Madbouly and his government for their efforts on this matter and particularly to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources for its support for the establishment of the company.

Dhanhani expressed the keenness of Sheikh Hamad bin Mohammed Al Sharqi, Member of the UAE Supreme Council and Ruler of Fujairah, to strengthen ties of cooperation with the Egyptian side.

He affirmed the commitment to expediting implementation of the project.

The meeting reviewed the project’s implementation steps, which come within the framework of supporting and enhancing Egypt’s role as a regional hub for energy trading and handling.

The project aims to develop Al-Hamra Port through cooperation and integration with the Fujairah Oil and Gas Corporation. It also includes the transfer of expertise and the application of the latest systems and technologies in use, thereby enhancing the port’s efficiency and bringing it up to international standards.

The project will also involve storing crude oil using the storage facilities at Al-Hamra Petroleum Port in New Alamein, maximizing the economic benefits and returns from Egypt’s infrastructure and capitalizing on the port’s unique location and advanced infrastructure to make it a strategic hub for crude oil storage and transportation.

For his part, Badawi stressed the importance of the project and the substantial government support provided by both the Egyptian and the UAE sides to ensure the success of this project on Egypt’s Mediterranean coast and to replicate the successful experience of the existing project in the Emirate of Fujairah.

Badawi explained that ensuring the success of this major project is a top priority.

He affirmed that joint teams from both sides are working in full and continuous coordination to achieve this objective, complete the procedures and steps necessary for implementation and establish a specific timetable for the various stages of execution.

He stressed that the ministry would provide all necessary support and overcome any challenges that might arise during implementation.

World.title: President al-Sisi: Together for more prosperous future for Egyptian, Chinese peoples, humanity
World.content:
This year we celebrate the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the People’s Republic of China. Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with China in 1956, as an extension of the civilizational and historical ties between two nations whose roots extend deep into history.

As we mark this special anniversary between our two friendly countries, we also celebrate the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to Egypt as an honored and cherished guest.

Throughout history, Egypt and China have been united by enduring bonds of friendship and a shared legacy of civilizational achievement, embodied by the Nile River, the birthplace of Egyptian civilization and the lifeline of its people, and the mighty Yangtze River, the cradle of Chinese civilization and a timeless source of Chinese wisdom, culture, and philosophy.

Through the knowledge, sciences, and innovations they cultivated, these two ancient civilizations made profound contributions to human progress, creating an enduring arc of achievement stretching from the Pyramids of Egypt to the Great Wall of China.

Egyptian civilization made seminal contributions to fields such as medicine, engineering, and astronomy, while Chinese civilization pioneered transformative innovations that were remarkably advanced for their time.

The knowledge and discoveries generated by these civilizations were transmitted, developed, and built upon by successive generations of scholars and scientists, helping to lay foundations for the Industrial and Technological Revolutions and the unprecedented advances that followed.

Without this cumulative intellectual and scientific heritage, humanity could not have attained its present level of development across such a broad range of fields.

This shared legacy reinforces the legitimate aspiration of Egypt and China to participate fully and equitably in contemporary technological progress and to benefit from its advances, which will advance comprehensive and sustainable development for the peoples of both countries and other nations, and enable Egypt and China to continue their historic contribution to the advancement of human civilization.

The two countries were connected by a historic trade route that contributed to the movement of people and goods and extended from the Chinese Silk Road to the Red Sea and the Egyptian Suez Canal, the lifeline of global trade.

Along this route, missions and trade caravans journeyed from the coasts of China and Asia to Egyptian ports on the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, which continue to serve today as an indispensable link between East and West.

For centuries, Egyptian ports served as major commercial hubs for the exchange of goods among Asia, Europe, and Africa.

These vital routes also enabled the exchange of cultures, knowledge, and ideas between the two peoples, further strengthening the historic bonds between Egypt and China and laying the foundations for centuries of extensive people-to-people, commercial, and cultural interaction.

This long history of engagement ultimately culminated in the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries seven decades ago—a landmark moment that opened a new chapter in bilateral relations and paved the way for their continued development and flourishing.

Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China, at a pivotal moment when Egypt affirmed its support for the right of peoples to freely choose their own political and economic systems.

Egypt thereby paved the way for Arab and African relations with China, which have expanded and flourished over the decades, culminating in the establishment of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

Egypt has consistently adhered to the One-China principle and rejected interference in China’s internal affairs. It supported the restoration of China’s permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, while China supported Arab rights and the right of the Palestinian people to establish their independent state.

These historic positions remain deeply engraved in the collective memory of both nations as enduring milestones in their relationship.

As the Egyptian and Chinese peoples commemorate this cherished anniversary, they recall this shared history not only with pride, but also as a lasting foundation for solidarity and a source of renewed momentum for deeper cooperation, mutual support, and partnership in the years ahead.

Over the past seven decades, Egypt-China relations have witnessed remarkable development, culminating in the establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries in 2014, during my first official visit to the People’s Republic of China.

At that pivotal juncture, Egypt was determined to broaden and deepen its relations with countries across the world, diversify its foreign policy, and reach out to its friends and partners to forge stronger and more comprehensive partnerships founded on mutual respect, solidarity, and mutual benefit.

Egypt also exerted efforts to advance joint development in infrastructure, investment, trade, manufacturing, and technology transfer. China was among the first countries to demonstrate its keenness to consolidate relations with Egypt on the basis of these firmly established principles, which constituted the solid foundation for enduring and longstanding relations that have succeeded in achieving benefits for the two peoples and safeguarding the interests of the two countries.

Accordingly, the comprehensive strategic partnership established by the two countries has brought about a major transformation in bilateral relations. China has become a major trade and economic partner for Egypt, and Chinese direct investments have increased, including in the Suez Canal Economic Zone SCZONE, which has provided tremendous opportunities for Chinese investors to generate returns and benefit from the significant advantages available to foreign investors in the zone.

The SCZONE contains industrial areas hosting numerous factories of international companies from various countries seeking to benefit from these opportunities, as well as from Egypt’s geographical location at the heart of the world, as an essential link between East and West.

Chinese companies have also contributed to numerous major national projects, such as the construction of the Central Business District in the New Capital, the launch of the electric railway to the Tenth of Ramadan City, the construction of renewable energy power plants, the development of ports, and other projects that formed part of the Egyptian state’s national plans to overhaul its infrastructure, which Egypt undertook with the cooperation with a number of different countries, including China.

This has contributed to Egypt’s globally advanced position in the field of infrastructure, which is pivotal to laying the foundations for an advanced and integrated industrial base, and transforming Egypt into a global logistics hub for industry, trade, and services.

This significant progress in strengthening and modernizing Egypt’s infrastructure has reinforced its position as an attractive destination for major industrial investments from around the world. China has been among the leading countries keen to expand its industrial presence in Egypt and capitalize on the country’s strategic location, advanced infrastructure, and the significant investment opportunities and competitive advantages it offers.

Egypt and China share a common commitment to harnessing the synergies between Egypt’s strategy for industrial localization and China’s strategy for high-quality development, with a view to attracting greater Chinese industrial investment to Egypt. Priority sectors include electric vehicles, energy-storage batteries, renewable energy, electronics, components for seawater desalination plants, shipbuilding, and other advanced industries.

This cooperation also extends to promoting technology transfer in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and space sciences, which represent key priorities for economic and technological development and promising avenues for expanding Egypt-China cooperation in the next phase of our strategic partnership.

China’s development and its ability to achieve remarkable economic progress and eradicate extreme poverty have been an inspiration to developing countries seeking to realize their aspirations for modernization and advancement.

Egypt views this development positively, while at the same time believing that developing countries have a tremendous opportunity to achieve economic advancement in accordance with a development model suited to their respective circumstances and compatible with their historical and cultural contexts.

In this vein, it is important to underscore the need to create an appropriate international environment that enables these countries to achieve this desired objective.

From this standpoint, Egypt has played its constructive regional and international role over the past decades and adhered to the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the rules-based international order. Egypt has worked to contribute to supporting international organizations in carrying out their essential role in safeguarding international peace and security.

It has made tangible contributions to peacekeeping and peacebuilding operations and participated, alongside all parties of the international community, in efforts to enhance the role of international economic organizations in achieving global sustainable development and advancing the United Nations development goals.

Egypt has firmly maintained its position in support of strengthening the voice of the Global South and promoting its representation in international institutions, in a manner that respects the right of these countries to express their will and takes their concerns into consideration.

Egypt has joined a number of emerging institutions and joined BRICS in 2024, as well as the New Development Bank affiliated with it and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

It also joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a dialogue partner, out of its keenness to strengthen South-South dialogue and openness to broad and diverse partnerships with all countries of the world.

I therefore take this opportunity to congratulate China on assuming the BRICS presidency next year, and wish to express that Egypt looks forward to continued coordination and consultation with China in this regard.

Egypt has also adhered to a policy of strategic balance as a guiding principle of Egyptian foreign policy at a time when waves of polarization and competition are intensifying, emphasizing its independent foreign policy and calling for the international community to coordinate its efforts to overcome the global challenges that have come to threaten the entire world.

Egypt and China have become partners contributing together to enhancing the role of the Global South in the international system, in a manner that achieves greater justice and fairness for developing countries.

From the same viewpoint, Egypt has undertaken intensive diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the situation in the Middle East and prevent the escalation and expansion of the conflict, as the region undergoes a dangerous phase of conflicts that threaten regional security and stability and, indeed, threaten international peace and security.

In this context, Egypt and China agree on the necessity of resolving conflicts through peaceful means, taking into consideration the security concerns of all parties, and respecting the sovereignty of states as a basis for the peaceful settlement of conflicts. It is not in the interest of any regional or international party to widen the conflict or exacerbate armed hostilities.

In the same vein, the Nile River has been the foundation of Egyptian civilization and a vital source of its prosperity throughout history. Egypt and its fellow Nile Basin brothers have benefited from the Nile for thousands of years, with its waters serving as a shared resource and a basis for life, development and human well-being.

Throughout its history, Egypt has remained committed to supporting the development of the countries of the Nile Basin, particularly in the areas of water resources development and dam construction, including in the Sudan and Uganda, and, most recently, through its contribution to the mega-project of the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project in Tanzania.

Egypt will remain steadfast in advocating for transboundary cooperation in accordance with the principles and rules of international law, rather than unilateral approaches that result in harm to downstream States.

Egypt firmly believes that the sustainable management of shared water resources can only be achieved through prior notification, consultations and consensus among riparian States.

In this regard, Egypt highly values China’s position that has affirmed its recognition of the vital importance of the Nile River to Egypt as its principal lifeline, and reiterates the importance of refraining from unilateral measures and strengthening collaboration in good faith to achieve Win-Win cooperation and mutually beneficial outcomes.

Just as Egypt and China have, over the years, written remarkable chapters in the history of cooperation and friendship between our two countries, we look forward to writing together a new chapter in this enduring relationship, whose roots stretch back thousands of years. We aspire to many more decades of progress and prosperity for our two friendly peoples, and to a future in which the world enjoys greater stability, security, peace, and development.

World.title: Liberia: Bassa Students in Rwanda Honor Superintendent Karyou Johnson for Support, Receive US$1,200 Donation
World.content:
Monrovia – The Bassa Students Association in Rwanda (BASIR) has honored Grand Bassa County Superintendent Karyou Johnson for what the students described as his outstanding support for their education and welfare in Rwanda.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

The recognition was presented during a gathering of Bassa students in Rwanda, where Superintendent Johnson reaffirmed his commitment to supporting Liberian students pursuing higher education abroad.

As part of his continued support, Johnson donated US$1,200 toward BASIR’s student programs, fulfilling a commitment he had previously made to the association.

The superintendent used the occasion to encourage graduating students to return to Liberia and use their education and skills to contribute to national development.

Johnson told the students that obtaining an education abroad should not be viewed simply as a pathway to employment, but as an opportunity to acquire knowledge that can be transformed into solutions and opportunities back home.

“When you don’t fight for your team or job, to make people know that what you are learning here can create positive impact in your country, yet you don’t get the opportunity,” Johnson said, urging graduates to demonstrate the value of their education through their work.

He challenged students completing their bachelor’s and master’s degrees to return home prepared to face the realities of the Liberian job market.

“Those who are graduating, go back now, start the struggle, fight for the job, rebuild your home,” he said.

Johnson said graduates must help Liberians understand that the education they receive abroad is relevant and capable of contributing to a better future.

He also praised BASIR for its organization, describing the association as an example of what Liberian students abroad can accomplish through unity and cooperation.

“There are a lot that I have learned from you guys. One, you guys are really, really organized,” he said, adding that he was proud to see scholarship students maintaining such a high level of organization even without direct sponsorship.

Johnson also pointed to the achievements of some Rwandan-based Liberian students as evidence that they are helping to put their educational community on the map.

He encouraged students not to give up when they encounter difficulties in seeking employment or establishing themselves after graduation.

“Those who are graduating, go back there, take the challenge, and never give up,” he said.

Beyond Degrees: Johnson Urges Creativity

The Grand Bassa superintendent further encouraged graduates to look beyond traditional employment and become creative in using their education and skills to create opportunities.

He recalled his own experience as a young graduate, saying the transition from university to professional life can be challenging and requires a different mindset.

“I was like you when I came for my graduation,” Johnson said, reflecting on his own experience.

He cautioned students against assuming that obtaining a degree automatically guarantees employment.

Instead, he encouraged them to develop innovative ways to earn a living and contribute to Liberia’s economy.

“One thing you need to do is that when you leave, you have to be very creative,” he said. “It’s just not about the economic things that you learn. It’s about being creative, using your brain to make money.”

Johnson said Liberia offers opportunities for educated young people to create their own employment rather than waiting solely for government or private-sector jobs.

“In Liberia, you can create your own job to make money,” he told the students.

A Broader Commitment to Liberian Students

Johnson’s visit to Rwanda comes as he continues to engage with Liberian students and scholarship beneficiaries abroad.

He noted that he had also received an invitation and communication from scholarship students from Lofa County, explaining that his family background connects him to both Lofa and Grand Bassa.

“My father is from Lofa County. My mother is from Grand Bassa County,” he said.

Johnson said this connection made his participation in activities involving students from both counties particularly meaningful.

The BASIR recognition underscores the growing engagement between county leadership and Liberians pursuing education abroad, while Johnson’s donation provides direct financial support for the association’s activities.

The superintendent pledged to maintain his support for the students and encouraged BASIR members to remain united, organized and focused on ensuring that their education ultimately benefits Liberia.

World.title: British Embassy Celebrates 5 Liberian Scholars Selected for Chevening Awards in the United Kingdom
World.content:
The British Embassy and the British community in Liberia are delighted to announce the 2026 cohort of Liberian Chevening Scholars as they prepare to begin their studies in the United Kingdom.

Chevening is the UK government’s prestigious scholarship programme for future world leaders. It provides fully funded scholarships to aspiring leaders, including around 400 scholars from Sub-Saharan Africa each year.

For many Chevening Scholars, the opportunity to further their career and study at the best universities in the world is an opportunity which might otherwise be unaffordable to them.

The academic skills and the connections scholars make whilst on the Chevening programme enable them to become pioneers in their specific field – from finance to healthcare to governance – and bring back these skills to benefit their home country.

Chevening boasts an alumni network of 50,000+, including an illustrious list of senior figures in politics, business, the law and other fields. No less than eighteen former and current heads of state are Chevening alumni.

A Chevening Scholarship also provides an opportunity to experience life in the United Kingdom, furthering the ties of friendship between our two countries.

Chevening has been active in Liberia since 2015. Today we are proud to announce that 5 Liberian Scholars have been awarded the Chevening Scholarship and will be traveling to the UK to complete a 1 year masters in the United Kingdom.

William M. Yarsiah , Special and Inclusive Education at University of Nottingham.

, Special and Inclusive Education at University of Nottingham. Hawa M. Kamara, Education Studies at Bangor University.

Education Studies at Bangor University. Darcess Dossen, Environmental Hazards and Disaster at Cardiff University.

Environmental Hazards and Disaster at Cardiff University. Francis M. Bee, Water, Sanitation and Health Engineering at the University of Leeds.

Molley M. Korleh, Port Management at Liverpool John Moores University.

On behalf of the British Embassy, we congratulate the latest scholars and wish them every success in their studies and future contributions to Liberia’s development.

World.title: Stakeholders call for monitoring of mining activities
World.content:
North-western Province Council of Elders Secretary Kenneth Kapata has called for closer monitoring of mining activities and spillages into rivers and streams.

Speaking during the recently held North-Western Provincial Development Coordinating Committee (PDCC) meeting, Mr Kapata stated that concerns raised by community members on the pollution from mining operations in areas such as Dengwe, Lufupa and lLungwa should be considered, adding that pollution in streams can kill fish and contaminate water sources used by local communities.

He added that the Zambia Environmental Management Authority ZEMA and other relevant authorities should assess the impact of mining spillages on small streams and ensure measures are taken to protect the environment and communities.

Mr Kapata recommended that regular monitoring of mining activities will help in the planning of emergencies.

He added that water in mining areas should be tested and assessed for its safety.

The Council of Elders Chairperson emphasised that ground water should also be assessed for contamination to safeguard the health of the people.

“We appeal to authorities to look into the concerns of the people in mining areas and monitor activities to ensure that our streams are not contaminated,” he said.

Meanwhile the Zambia Environmental Management Authority in the province says it is not aware of any spillages but says the authority will visit the areas for an informed report.

World.title: FRA buys over 17,000 bags of maize-Kasama
World.content:
Over 17, 500 bags of maize have been purchased by the Food Reserve Agency FRA at Mwamba satellite depot in Kasama district in Northern Province.

Mwamba satellite depot Clerk Elizabeth Chilolo says the maize purchase process is going on smoothly.

She told the media in an interview in Kasama district today that the farmers are cooperating with the officers employed by the Food Reserve Agency (FRA).

“So far work is going on smoothly without any challenges, the farmers and buyers are cooperating with us,” Ms Chilolo explained.

She said the Mwamba depot was officially opened on August 1st and purchase of maize commenced.

“We started buying maize on August 1st from the farmers and we have bought over 17 500 bags of maize,” Ms Chilolo said.

Emmanuel Mutale, a farmer in Chief Mwamba’s chiefdom praised the FRA for conducting a smooth process in the on-going crop marketing season.

Mr Mutale says the farmers have enough bags as well, making it easier for them to package the maize.

He has however called for transporters to continue transporting the maize as the stack at the depot is almost full.

“I want to appeal to the transporters to speed up the process of collecting the maize so that we create enough space for maize which has not been bought yet,” Mr Mutale appealed.

He added that if the transporters delay in transporting commodities, it will affect the purchase of maize at the depot.

World.title: Kasempa admin worries over increased teen pregnancies
World.content:
Kasempa District Administration has raised concern over teenage pregnancies and limited access to reproductive health information among adolescents, prompting it to call on traditional leaders to take an active role in addressing the challenges.

District Administrative Officer Francis Makanga said traditional leaders were important partners in addressing sexual and reproductive health challenges, including teenage pregnancies, sexually transmitted infections and limited access to information.

Mr Makanga said this during a traditional leaders’ engagement meeting on integrated sexual and reproductive health services in Kasempa District, North-western Province.

“As a district, we remain concerned about challenges such as teenage pregnancies, sexually transmitted infections and limited access to reproductive health information among some members of our communities,” he added.

Mr Makanga said sexual and reproductive health was a human right and key to sustainable development, enabling individuals and communities to make informed life decisions.

He explained that integrated sexual and reproductive health services combined family planning, maternal and child health, HIV and STI prevention, adolescent health and gender-based violence response.

“This integrated approach ensures that people receive comprehensive care in a convenient, effective and cost-efficient manner,” he said.

Mr Makanga called for a supportive environment where adolescents can access age-appropriate information and services without facing unnecessary barriers.

“I therefore call upon parents, teachers, traditional leaders and departmental heads to work together in providing accurate information and guidance to young people,” he said.

Mr Makanga said the government remains committed to strengthening the health system and improving access to reproductive health services.

However, he said these efforts required active participation from communities and stakeholders to succeed.

Mr Makanga commended traditional and religious leaders, government departments, the media and partners, particularly Marie Stopes, for supporting efforts to improve health and wellbeing in Kasempa.

He said continued collaboration among stakeholders would help strengthen access to sexual and reproductive health information and services, while contributing to healthier families and communities.

World.title: Hichilema Begins Second Term, Pledges Growth-Focused Agenda
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema and Vice President Mutale Nalumango took the oath of office on Tuesday for a new five-year mandate running through 2031, committing to govern with honesty and accountability.

Addressing the crowd at Heroes Stadium in Lusaka, Hichilema reached out to his political rivals and asked citizens to accept differing political views, arguing that election outcomes shouldn’t drive Zambians apart permanently. He said his administration would make sure every citizen’s perspective counted and would push development that meaningfully improves daily life in communities across Zambia. He urged all Zambians, regardless of party, faith, tribe, gender, or economic standing, to unite behind both diligence and smart strategy in building the nation forward.

The centerpiece of his new term is what he’s calling the Grow Zambia Agenda, meant to carry forward the economic stabilization gains of his first term into a new phase centered on growth, wealth-building, employment, and broadly shared prosperity. He said his government would push harder on reform in mining, farming, tourism, and energy, paired with infrastructure and industrial development, to tap into the country’s economic capacity.

He also laid out a set of numeric targets guiding the term, dubbed 10-10-5-3-3-1-1-1, covering 10 million tonnes of maize production, 10,000 megawatts of power generation, five million annual tourist visits, three million tonnes each of copper and soybeans, a million tonnes each of wheat and sugar, and beef exports worth at least $1 billion.

He stressed that growth needs to show up concretely in people’s lives through employment for graduates, dependable markets for farmers, more room for business, and stronger revenue to fund ongoing development.

On social policy, Hichilema pointed to free schooling, better health services, a boosted Constituency Development Fund, and empowerment programs aimed at women and youth as key priorities. He noted that 2.6 million school-age children who had previously dropped out are now back in classrooms. He also promised to push more authority and funding down to local government so development reaches every part of Zambia, and he framed proportional representation as a way to bring more women, young people, and people with disabilities into governance.

Calling education the great equalizer, Hichilema called for continued investment in schooling, skills development, and healthcare, alongside a cultural shift that puts children and future generations at the heart of national planning. He also pledged continued modernization of the civil service, with better delivery, more digital tools, and stronger accountability and anti-corruption efforts, and told public officials to prioritize the national interest over personal gain.

On the international front, he said Zambia would keep pursuing economic diplomacy and regional stability while deepening ties with neighboring states, Africa, and the broader global community, positioning the country as a dependable, investment-friendly partner.

The inauguration unfolded against a tense backdrop. Hichilema had been declared the winner of the August 18 election with roughly 60% of the vote, per the Electoral Commission of Zambia, continuing the country’s largely peaceful electoral track record since multiparty rule returned in 1991. His closest rival, Brian Mundubile, took about 38% and disputed the outcome, alleging irregularities.

Days after the vote, security forces searched Mundubile‘s residence. He says he went into hiding fearing for his safety before he and running mate Makebi Zulu turned themselves in on August 24 after taking shelter at a United Nations building. Both are now held at Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison on treason allegations, with courts closed to legal challenges of the election result during this period.

Heads of state from across the continent attended the ceremony, including Kenya‘s William Ruto, Botswana‘s Duma Boko, and Zimbabwe‘s Emmerson Mnangagwa.

World.title: HH pledges to scale-up investments in all sectors
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has pledged to scale – up investment in education and skills development and health sectors, under his renewed mandate to govern Zambia.

He has noted that in his last term, reforms introduced in the education sector, notable among them, the introduction of signing of free education into law, saw about 2.6 million learners who had previously dropped out, return to school.

Guided by the ‘Go Zambia Agenda’ under his new mandate, President Hichilema has assured that his administration will therefore continue to build on the gains scored in his previous term.

Speaking shortly after his inauguration, the Head of State noted that continued investment in education will, therefore, ensure equal access to opportunities for all Zambians.

“Education remains the greatest equalizer, best investment and indeed inheritance that we can pass on to our children. Education gives them a lasting sense of value and protection for whatever else they are left with”, the President highlighted.

The President assured of increased economic empowerment for women and young people in order to enable them to contribute to job creation and economic growth.

He added that continued empowerment of young people will not only curb the culture of handouts but also enable them to contribute to economic growth, noting that social protection programmes are meant to uplift the livelihoods of vulnerable citizens.

President Hichilema further stated that his administration will expedite decentralisation, which saw the increase of the Constituency Development Funds (CDF) from 1.6 to 40 million kwacha in his previous term, in order to ensure development reaches all parts of the country.

Meanwhile, visiting Heads of State have pledged their countries’ support towards President Hichilema’s new developmental agenda.

President of Zimbabwe, Emmerson Mnangagwa assured that his country will continue to partner with Zambia to achieve mutual developmental targets.

He called for the two countries to harness regional opportunities for the benefit of citizens’ economic growth.

“The responsibility to build and industrialise our countries remains with us”, he stressed.

And President of Kenya, William Ruto expressed confidence in President Hichilema’s new mandate, further stressing the need for Zambia to maximise on its various resources, including a youthful population to create wealth.

“We have resources and the youngest population on earth. The challenge before us isn’t the absence of resources but how we use them”, President Ruto emphasised.

World.title: Tanzania, Eswatini dignitaries leave Zambia
World.content:
Tanzanian President Samia Hassan has left the country after witnessing the inauguration ceremony of President Hakainde Hichilema.

President Hassan was accorded a half-guard of honour, one of the highest military honours accorded to a visiting Head of State.

She was accompanied by Tanzanian Minister of Foreign Affairs Ngwapu Maghembe.

Meanwhile, Eswatini Deputy Prime Minister Tulusile Dladla has also left Zambia for her home country.

President Hassan and Ms Dladla were seen off at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport by Deputy Secretary to Cabinet Oliver Kalabo, Lusaka Province Permanent Secretary Joe Kalusa, Defence Attachés accredited to Zambia and other senior government officials.

Ms Dladla departed Zambia at 16:12 hours while Ms Samia left at 16:27 hours.

World.title: Presidents Boko, Ruto leave Zambia
World.content:
Botswana President Duma Boko has become the fourth African Head of State to leave Zambia after attending the inauguration ceremony of President Hakainde Hichilema, at the National Heroes stadium in Lusaka this afternoon.

President Boko, who was accompanied by Minister of Foreign Affairs Phenyo Butale and other senior government officials, left Kenneth Kaunda International Airport at 16:50 hours.

He was seen off at the airport by Deputy Secretary to Cabinet Oliver Kalabo, Lusaka Province Permanent Secretary Joe Kalusa, Zimbabwean Ambassador to Zambia Charity Chiramba, Defence Attachés accredited to Zambia and other senior government officials.

Meanwhile, President of Kenya William Ruto has also left the country.

The presidential plane carrying Mr Ruto left the country at 17:05 hours.

The two Heads of State are among other international dignitaries who attended President Hakainde Hichilema’s inauguration ceremony at the National Heroes stadium in Lusaka following his victory in the August 13 general elections.

World.title: President Hichilema emphasises inclusive development
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema says his administration intends to continue with inclusive development of not leaving anyone behind.

President Hichilema says that this is to ensure that every Zambian enjoys a share of the country’s social and economic growth, regardless of political or social standing.

The Head of State said this in a speech read on his behalf by Vice President Mutale Nalumango during the inauguration luncheon in Lusaka.

He reminded that Zambia was coming from a collapsing economy which was stabilised and the debt restructured in the last five years.

The Head of State indicated that Zambia was now moving from stability to prosperity and growth.

The President reiterated that part of the agenda in the new five-year mandate was to double the economy.

President Hichilema added that the government will also work with traditional leaders to advance peace and development.

Emphasising on the need to guard peace, the Head of State explained that peace is the greatest ingredient for development.

Meanwhile, the Head of State highlighted that Zambia will deepen global partnerships in trade, investment, technology and skills for youth and women empowerment.

“Zambia remains a reliable friend and constructive partner. We continue to promote peace, regional integration and economic cooperation,” he stated.

And he thanked the Zambian people for a renewed mandate, accepting it with humility to serve, deliver and remain accountable.

Mrs Nalumango led a toast to continued peace, unity and prosperity for all Zambians.

World.title: South Africa: Western Cape Braces for Hot Summer - South African News Briefs - September 2, 2026
World.content:
Western Cape Braces for Hotter, Drier Summer

Western Cape residents have been urged to prepare for a potentially hotter and drier summer, reports EWN. Experts are warning of increased wildfire risks and growing pressure on water resources. Local Government, Environmental Affairs and Development Planning MEC Anton Bredell said the province was taking the warnings seriously, particularly because extreme heat could pose greater risks in informal settlements. Authorities are securing firefighting aircraft, investing in equipment and training. They are urging residents and landowners to clear fire hazards and create firebreaks. Dam levels are already lower than last year. The province is also working to repair leaks, upgrade infrastructure and secure alternative water sources.

Ramaphosa's Phala Phala Bid Goes to Court

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

President Cyril Ramaphosa's application to set aside the Section 89 independent panel report on the Phala Phala saga is set to be heard in the Western Cape High Court, reports SABC News. The report found strong evidence that Ramaphosa may have violated his oath of office by stealing $580,000 in cash from his Limpopo farm. The National Assembly initially voted against the report. The Constitutional Court later invalidated that decision and ordered Parliament to establish an impeachment committee. The committee's proceedings were temporarily halted in July pending the outcome of Ramaphosa's application to review the report.

eThekwini Debt Tops R47 Billion

eThekwini Mayor Cyril Xaba has raised alarm over the municipality's growing debt, which has surpassed R47 billion, reports EWN. Households account for the largest share of the debt at R35 billion, followed by commercial clients owing R10 billion and government departments owing more than R2 billion. Xaba said the municipality could not function effectively with such a large and growing debt burden. He outlined plans to recover some of the money, including through disconnection campaigns and identifying residents who may qualify for indigent support.
