It had said that "the right of the people staying in a particular locality should not be exposed, and any kind of prejudice or discrimination because of the voting pattern should be avoided".

In a U-turn, EC in its affidavit filed on Aug 31 said, "Experience of litigations has revealed that the present system which includes a simultaneous audit by the candidates is necessary to ensure that frivolous and baseless allegations do not cloud the outcome..." It said the introduction of the totaliser system would give fresh anxieties, misgivings and allegations regarding data, machine tampering and transmission glitches.

World.title: Barefoot mom in sari runs 3km to win Rs 5k for kids' education
World.content:
Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

PUNE: Ramabai Ranvir had no idea what running a race meant. All she had heard was there was Rs 3,000 to be won if she finished first.So, the 47-year-old widow hopped onto the pickup with a group of police aspirants from the Beed academy where she worked, hoping to compete in what would be the first race of her life. It didn't bother her that she hadn't trained for the rigours of a long-distance run. It hardly mattered that she was the lone runner without shoes.In her sari, barefoot after her slippers gave up midway through the run, Ramabai ran 3km with the indomitable spirit of a mother competing for a cash prize that would ease her struggle to pay for her daughters' education."I ran like my life depended on it. I didn't know how much time I needed to cover the distance. I only sto-pped once I was past the finish line," she told TOI. "I am so happy they gave me Rs 5,000 instead of Rs 3,000. I bought notebooks and pens for my daughter Pooja. The remaining money is for Arti."Ramabai works in the kitchen at Dnyandeep Acad-emy, making over 200 chapatis a day for a monthly salary of Rs 9,000.The native of Potra, Hingoli, took the job to fund the education of her two daughters after her husband died in 2012.On Aug 28, her younger daughter Arti (20), a BSc computer science student who lives alone in Nanded, called asking for money for food and rent. Ramabai, who didn't have any cash to spare, had a sleepless night.At dawn, she heard the academy's trainers rounding up aspirants for a running competition nearby. She instantly decided to join in."There is no pain worse than that of not being able to take care of your children. The moment I came to know of the race, winning was the only thing on my mind."Datta Darade, who heads the academy, said Ramabai's determination moved him. The academy had enrolled her elder daughter Pooja (22) free of cost and given her employment and a room to stay in. "I was taking my students to the marathon. When Ramabai said she wanted to come along, I asked her, 'What will you do there?' She said, 'I will run.' I couldn't believe it when she won in the above-30 category."Pooja finished second in the 18-30 age group and won Rs 2,000. Arti said she was dumbstruck when her sister called to say their mother had won."Our mother studied till Class 7 and has worked all her life, not taking breaks even when she was unwell. She didn't hesitate to send me to Nanded for my studies. I am not surprised she decided to win a race for her family," she said.

World.title: Pak takes SCO chair, PM Modi slams use of terror as strategic asset
World.content:
Framing security as a non-negotiable prerequisite for regional progress, PM Narendra Modi delivered a thinly veiled warning to Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit.

With Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif in attendance, Modi said countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.

Also Read:

The remarks are significant also because of the timing. Pakistan assumed rotating chairmanship of SCO from Kyrgyzstan on Tuesday and will host the heads-of-state summit next year, for which it will invite Modi, along with others.

Modi made the remarks, in which he also warned against double standards on terrorism, while expanding on India's SCO vision - Security, Connectivity and Opportunity - that he articulated in Tianjin last year.

With Chinese President Xi Jinping also present, PM reiterated India's position that all connectivity initiatives must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states as this is also the "fundamental spirit" of SCO charter.





Modi said that terrorism continued to pose a serious challenge to humanity and it's important to not remain confined to an action-reaction approach in the fight against the menace.

âWe must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation, and safe havens. We must speak with one voice and make it clear that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,â said PM, without naming Pakistan as SCO charter doesnât allow members to raise bilateral differences.

Also Read:

India and Pakistan together joined the China-dominated Eurasian grouping as full members in 2017. For India, the security-oriented SCO has served as a platform not just to assert its strategic autonomy but also flag regional risks from state-sponsored terrorism. Modi said that the blocâs shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also closely linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan and that India will continue to contribute to the development and provision of humanitarian assistance to people of the country.

Modi addressed West Asia crisis, saying it was affecting energy security, maritime trade and supply chains around the world and recalling his message earlier that conflicts cannot be resolved on the battlefield. âCountries of Global South bear greatest brunt of such disruptions. Therefore, India has consistently called for all tensions and conflicts to be resolved not on battlefield, but through dialogue and diplomacy,â he added.

While underlining the importance India attaches to SCO, Modi said that at a time when the world is passing through instability, the organisation must transform the shared geography into opportunities and bring about positive change in peopleâs lives. Describing SCO as a confluence of great civilisations, cultures, and ideas, he said that over next 25 years, people-to-people ties should remain at the heart of cooperation among the member states.

âTrue measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts create, how many new markets open up for entrepreneurs, how much farmers benefit from tech, and how much better the lives of our citizens become,â said the PM. According to an Indian readout of PMâs participation, Modi stated that strong and trusted connectivity initiatives were important for the groupâs shared progress and prosperity.

World.title: India on board, SCO reiterates condemnation of Iran attacks
World.content:
Expressing deep concern over developments in "the Middle East and around Iran", the SCO member-states including India reiterated the bloc's condemnation of military strikes on Iranian territory that resulted in numerous civilian casualties and significant damage to Iran's economy, said the Bishkek Declaration.

India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

This was the second time that the SCO denounced the strikes on Iran after the West Asia war started on February 28, the first in an early March standalone statement that called the attacks unacceptable. India had endorsed that statement too, even though bilaterally it has not explicitly condemned the attacks on Iran the way it has missile and drone strikes on the GCC countries.

India also joined other member-states in expressing condolences over the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei

However, unlike the Tianjin Declaration last year that too condemned the June 2025 US and Israeli strikes on Iran, the Bishkek Declaration did not name the US and Israel.

"Such actions violate the principles and norms of international law and the UN Charter and create serious risks to international peace, security and stability," said SCO's Bishkek Declaration.

India and others backed Iran's sovereignty and territorial integrity, advocating a resolution to the conflict solely through political and diplomatic means.





In this regard, they welcome all efforts aimed at de-escalating the situation in the region and, as the declaration said, noted that the only possible way to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East is a comprehensive and just settlement of the Palestinian question.

PM Narendra Modi met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek on Monday and backed expansion of bilateral economic ties with Tehran, while the Iranian president sought India's help to end the war.

After distancing itself from a statement by SCO in June last year condemning Israel's strikes, India has signed on to joint documents by the bloc censuring US-Israel military action against Iran.

The Declaration reflected a major Indian concern as it strongly condemned

in all its forms and manifestations, emphasised that "double standards" in the fight against terrorism are unacceptable, and called on the international community to combat terrorism, including the cross-border movement of terrorists.

It called for the UN playing a central role by fully implementing relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy in accordance with the UN Charter and the principles of international law to jointly combat all terrorist groups.

"Member States, reaffirming their firm commitment to combating terrorism, separatism, and extremism, emphasize the inadmissibility of attempts to exploit terrorist, separatist, and extremist groups for selfish purposes.

They recognize the leading role of sovereign states and their competent authorities in countering terrorist and extremist threats," said the Declaration.

Significantly, targeting use of economic sanctions by the West, the leaders came out in support of an open, fair and non-discriminatory multilateral trading system focused heavily on the framework established by the WTO, while slamming unilateral coercive measures.

"Member States oppose unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to the UN Charter and other norms of international law, the rules and principles of the World Trade Organization, that are detrimental to the interests of ensuring international security, including its food, energy and humanitarian components, and that have a negative impact on the global economy," said the Bishkek Declaration.

World.title: Two Turkish-flagged commercial vessels collide off Istanbul
World.content:
Two ​Turkish-flagged commercial vessels collided off Istanbul ‌in the Sea of Marmara on ​Wednesday (September 2, 2026) and contact ⁠has been lost with one of the ships, the Istanbul governor’s office ‌said.

The Turkish-flagged Alsu, en route to the Aegean ‌port of Aliaga, and the ‌Turkish-flagged ⁠Tugberk Imamoglu, en route ⁠to the Black Sea port of Karadenizeregli, collided off the Silivri district of ​Istanbul at ‌around 3 a.m. (0000 GMT) on Wednesday, the governor’s office said in a statement.

Coast guard ships ‌and helicopters were dispatched to ​the scene for search and rescue, and there ⁠was no visible damage on the Alsu, the statement said. But ‌authorities were unable to establish contact with the Tugberk Imamoglu and its 10 crew members.

According to data from the Istanbul Chamber of Maritime Commerce, the ‌Tugberk Imamoglu, owned by Zeybe Denizcilik, operates ​as a bulk carrier, while the Alsu, owned ⁠by Ozpulathane Deniz Tasimaciligi, operates as ⁠a chemical tanker.

The search and rescue operation was ‌still under way, the governor’s office statement said.

World.title: Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma scripts history with AVM-rank appointment
World.content:
In a historic milestone for the Indian Air Force, Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma has become the first woman officer (non-medical) in the country’s armed forces to attain the rank of Air Vice Marshal or equivalent, officials said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).

She assumed the appointment of assistant Chief of the Air Staff (education) at the air headquarters on September 1, they said.

The air officer previously held the rank of air commodore, an IAF official said.

“In a historic milestone for the Indian Air Force, Air Vice Marshal Shakti Sharma became the first woman officer (non-medical) in the Indian Defence Forces to attain the rank of Air Vice Marshal (or equivalent),” the Defence Ministry said.

Commissioned into the Education Branch of the IAF on June 18, 1994, AVM Sharma brings a wealth of experience to her new role, spanning diverse postings across training establishments, field stations, command headquarters and the Air Headquarters, it said.

“Throughout her career, she has spearheaded key institutional initiatives, including establishing the IAF Chairs of Excellence at IIT Kanpur and Pune University to drive academic and strategic defence collaboration. She also created history as the first woman officer from the Tri-Services to command a Sainik School, serving as principal of Sainik School, Kapurthala,” the Ministry said in a statement.

This landmark achievement marks a new chapter in the journey of women officers in the Indian defence forces. With over three decades of distinguished service, she continues to inspire generations to ‘Touch the Sky with Glory’ — the motto of the IAF, it said.

World.title: ED raids payment companies, CAs in online betting case
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) conducted fresh multi-state searches covering payment companies, chartered accountants, and company secretaries in a money laundering investigation involving online betting firm Parimatch and a few others, officials said.

Raids were made at five locations in Maharashtra, four in Delhi-NCR, two in Rajasthan, and one in Gujarat, they said.

Under scanner are payment companies, which allegedly converted betting proceeds into cash through chartered accountants and company secretaries and helped send the money abroad in illegal remittances and "sham" Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) routed via payment gateways on behalf of Parimatch, the officials said.

The case stems from an FIR filed by the cyber police station of Mumbai Police against parimatch.com for "duping" users through online betting.

The agency has carried out searches and attached assets in this case in the past.

World.title: Failed delivery ruse, ₹1.5 lakh plot: Niece kills uncle in Rohini, stages attack to mislead police
World.content:
A failed attempt to enter a 60-year-old man’s house posing as a delivery agent did not deter a group of four who were after ₹1.5 lakh in cash. Hours later, the man’s niece (wife’s sister’s daughter) returned with three associates while his family was at a Janmashtami fair and helped them gain entry, and he was subsequently killed.

The Rohini police have arrested the niece, Simran Taneja (24), primary school teacher, and two other associates identified as Chirag (22), a gym trainer, and a class 12 student in connection with the murder of Rakesh Khanna in Sector 3, Rohini, on Tuesday night (September 1, 2026). Simran’s boyfriend Himanshu is currently absconding.

Speaking to The Hindu, Rohini DCP Shashank Jaiswal said Khanna had recently sold his house and shifted to a rented accommodation in Sector 3. Simran, who was aware that the family had a large amount of cash at the house, planned the burglary.

According to the police, Himanshu first conducted a recce of the house three days before the crime, posing as a delivery agent. He returned in the same guise around 3 p.m. on Tuesday (September 1, 2026), hoping to gain entry. However, the plan failed when Khanna did not open the door, telling him that no order had been placed.

With the delivery-agent ruse failing, Simran came up with another plan.

She visited her aunt and suggested that her mother and aunt, who are sisters, go together to a Janmashtami fair in Paschim Vihar. After the family left, Simran returned early with Chirag and Paras to Khanna’s house, while Himanshu stayed outside to keep watch, the official said.

Inside the house, the three attacked Khanna with a knife and killed him before fleeing with ₹1.5 lakh in cash and two gold rings.

The police said that Simran called her aunt that evening to check if the family had begun their journey back from the fair, ensuring the accused had enough time to execute the plan.

The crime came to light around 7.30 p.m. when Khanna’s wife returned home to find the house in disarray and her husband unconscious.

After receiving the distress call, the Rohini police took Khanna to the hospital, where he was declared dead. His body was sent for a postmortem, and four suspects were arrested around 2 a.m. as they attempted to flee the city.

The police said Simran also tore her clothes with the knife and claimed that the three men had attacked her in an attempt to portray herself as a victim and mislead the police about her involvement in the crime. The police have recovered ₹75,000 in cash and the two gold rings taken from the house.

Further investigation is underway.

World.title: West Asia conflict LIVE updates: Iran says 11 dead in U.S. strikes on its territory
World.content:
Iran said on Wednesday (September 2, 2026) that U.S. strikes on its territory killed 11 people, state media reported, after a fresh attack in the southwestern province of Khuzestan.

Meanwhile, Iran pushed ahead with strikes targeting American interests around the West Asia on Wednesday (September 2, 2026), vowing “severe” consequences to U.S. attacks.

The latest flare-up is part of a cycle of retaliation that followed U.S. strikes on Iran, with fighting over the Hormuz strait expanding to Washington’s Gulf allies, military bases and commercial shipping. It began when Washington hit Iranian targets on Sunday (August 30, 2026), the first known strikes in several weeks, after which Tehran’s forces targeted US troops in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, and projectiles struck two oil tankers in unclaimed attacks.

(With inputs from agencies)
