Over the full term, the borrower would repay more than 347,000 manats (about $204,000) to the bank. Including the down payment, the total cost would exceed 375,000 manats (about $220,600). Insurance, property valuation, notary fees and other associated costs are not included.

A monthly payment of 1,158 manats is almost equal to the average salary across the country and represents 78% of the average salary in Baku. Under the Fund’s rules, mortgage payments must not exceed 70% of borrowers’ combined income after tax. This means that a Baku resident earning a single average salary would find it practically impossible to service such a mortgage alone.

In a household where two people earn the average Baku salary, the monthly mortgage payment would account for 39% of their combined nominal income. After tax, the share would exceed 40%. According to OECD and Eurostat methodology, housing costs exceeding 40% of disposable income are considered an excessive housing burden.

Under the subsidised mortgage scheme, the annual interest rate is 4%, the loan term can be up to 30 years, and the maximum loan amount is 100,000 manats (about $58,820). Although the monthly payment would be around 477 manats (about $280.60), buying a 65-square-metre flat at Baku’s average price would require around 78,000 manats (about $45,882) in the buyer’s own funds. The lower interest rate therefore does not solve the main problem for families without substantial savings.

Is renting cheaper?

The median advertised rent in Baku is 11 manats (about $6.50) per square metre per month. Renting a 65-square-metre flat would therefore cost around 715 manats (about $420.60) a month – 443 manats (about $260.60) less than the monthly payment on a standard mortgage. However, this still amounts to around 48% of the average salary in Baku, excluding utility bills.

If an investor bought such a flat for 178,000 manats and rented it out for 715 manats a month, the gross annual rental yield would be around 4.8%. After accounting for maintenance, periods when the property is vacant and other associated costs, the actual return would be even lower. Buying a flat with a mortgage and then renting it out therefore generally does not allow the owner to cover the full cost through rental income alone. The model may make sense primarily for investors with substantial capital who are betting on further increases in property prices.

What is driving prices higher?

The Chamber of Appraisers attributes the rise in new-build prices to strong demand in the mid-to-upper and premium segments, the availability of mortgage financing and the perception of housing as an investment asset. The Chamber’s land price index also points to rising prices and limited supply in premium areas. This may put additional pressure on the cost of newly built homes.

At the same time, according to the State Statistics Committee, investment in residential construction fell by 2.7% in real terms in the first half of the year. These figures strengthen the suggestion that demand, growing faster than household incomes, is running up against limited supply.

State-backed mortgages make housing more affordable for some families: in the first half of the year, 2,242 families received mortgage loans worth a total of 226.3 million manats (about $133.1 million). Since 2019, just over 10,000 families have used the rent-to-own scheme. However, it remains unclear whether these programmes are large enough to curb the overall rise in property prices.

Buying a home in Baku today is therefore more affordable for a household with two stable official incomes, substantial savings for a down payment or another property that can be sold than for someone living on a single average salary. Those who qualify for subsidised mortgages and have tens of thousands of manats in savings are also in a stronger position.

For everyone else, the choice is essentially between increasingly expensive rent and taking on long-term, substantial debt.

Buying a home in Azerbaijan

World.title: Kyrgyzstan carries out paving works on Ala-Buka–Karavan road
World.content:
Photo: Press Service of the Ministry of Transport and Communications of Kyrgyzstan

BISHKEK, Kyrgyzstan, September 2. Asphalt paving continues on Ala-Buka–Karavan road in Kyrgyzstan.

According to the Kyrgyz Ministry of Transport and Communications, the 2026 road construction plan provides for the paving of seven kilometers of the road.

"Asphalt paving works are continuing on a seven-kilometer section of the Ala-Buka–Karavan road in the Jalal-Abad region," the ministry’s press service said.

The No. 17 Road Maintenance Department is currently carrying out the works in line with the approved schedule. A range of measures is being implemented to improve road conditions and ensure traffic safety.

Furthermore, the rehabilitation of the section is expected to improve transport connectivity for local residents and enhance road safety.

The progress of the road construction and rehabilitation works is being monitored by the Ministry of Transport and Communications.

Meanwhile, the Ala-Buka–Karavan road is located in Kyrgyzstan’s Jalal-Abad region and serves local communities in the area. Its rehabilitation is part of ongoing road maintenance and infrastructure works aimed at improving road conditions and transport connectivity.

The route is particularly relevant for local traffic and access between settlements in the region. Continued rehabilitation and paving works are intended to improve the condition of the road and create safer conditions for motorists and passengers.

World.title: Iran claims attacks on U.S. military bases in UAE, Bahrain
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 2. Iran’s military claims it has attacked U.S. military air bases in the UAE and Bahrain.

This was reflected in a statement, published by the Iranian military.

“The Iranian military, in response to U.S. airstrikes on Iran, carried out strikes with dozens of kamikaze unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) against radar systems and military personnel at the Al Dhafra and Al Minhad US air bases in the UAE,” the statement said.

It added that the Iranian military had also attacked the U.S. Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain using a large number of Arash kamikaze UAVs. “The attack on residential areas and a wedding ceremony reflects the objectives of the U.S. strikes and will inevitably be met with a response from the Iranian military,” the statement said.

On July 8, U.S. President Donald Trump said the ceasefire had been violated and ordered new strikes against Iran. In response, Iran targeted U.S. military facilities in the Persian Gulf region with missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles.

While Washington has not ruled out the possibility of Iran returning to negotiations, disagreements over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s nuclear program and other issues have left the prospects for a peace process uncertain. Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has once again been brought close to a standstill.

World.title: China's company proposes wind, solar projects in Kazakhstan's Abai region
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 9. China Energy Engineering Group Xinjiang Electric Power Design Institute Co., Ltd. has proposed implementing two renewable energy investment projects in Kazakhstan's Abai Region, according to the Abai Region akimat.

The proposal were made during a meeting between Abai Region Akim Berik Uali and Chinese investors led by Ma Yong, General Director of China Energy Engineering Group Xinjiang Electric Power Design Institute Co., Ltd.

"The Chinese company proposed implementing two investment projects in the region. The first envisages the construction of a wind power plant with a capacity of 100-200 MW near Zhangiztobe village in the Zharma district. The second project involves the construction of a solar power plant near Aktogay village in the Ayagoz district," the akimat said.

The sides discussed the development of renewable energy sources in the Abai Region, reducing the electricity deficit and improving the region's energy infrastructure.

During the meeting, Uali noted that the proposals put forward during the meeting would be considered and that the akimat would provide the necessary assistance within the framework of the law.

Implementation of the proposed projects is expected to help improve the reliability of electricity supply in the region, develop renewable energy sources, strengthen the sustainability of the energy system, and create new jobs.

China Energy Engineering Group Xinjiang Electric Power Design Institute Co., Ltd. specializes in power system planning, engineering consulting and design, EPC projects, as well as wind and solar power projects, energy storage systems, power grids and substations.

World.title: Azerbaijan and SCO: Baku becomes strategic connection point for organization
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 2. The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the meeting in the SCO+ format held yesterday in Bishkek have once again brought the organization's priorities for the coming period to the agenda.

The course of the Bishkek summit, the messages and proposals given by the country's leaders show that the organization aspires to become the main center determining the future development map of the Eurasian continent. In this regard, transport and logistics issues are no longer only of economic, but also geopolitical importance. The development of alternative routes connecting different regions of Eurasia is of great importance for the SCO countries in terms of both expanding trade opportunities and increasing the sustainability of global supply chains.

The role of Azerbaijan in this process is particularly noteworthy.

The country's advantage isn't limited to its location at an important geographical point in Eurasia. In recent years, the transport infrastructure created by Azerbaijan, the international corridors it has developed, and its participation in regional logistics projects have turned this geographical position into real economic opportunities. At a time when relations between Central Asia, China, the South Caucasus, and Europe are expanding, Azerbaijan is becoming one of the important connection points for access to European markets from the SCO area.

In this regard, the role of Azerbaijan is particularly evident in the development of the Middle Corridor. The route connecting China and Central Asia with Europe via the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, the South Caucasus, and Türkiye creates alternative access to global trade for the SCO countries. Azerbaijan's Baku International Sea Trade Port, the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway, and other transport infrastructure are among the main elements of this connection.

Azerbaijan contributes to the Middle Corridor not only by increasing the cargo transit volume. Baku is implementing specific projects to expand the capacity of the route and is also investing in the development of the transport capabilities of other participants of the corridor.

Statistical indicators show that the Middle Corridor is growing rapidly. While the volume of freight traffic on the route from 2019 through 2021 was approximately 0.6–0.8 million tons, in 2025 this figure exceeded 4 million tons. The more than 5-fold increase in freight traffic over several years indicates that the Middle Corridor has transformed from a regional route into an important alternative transport route on a Eurasian scale.

One of the important examples of Azerbaijan's contribution to the development of the Middle Corridor is the modernization of the Georgian section of the Baku-Tbilisi-Kars railway line. As a result of the modernization work carried out on the territory of Georgia on the BTK, one of the important segments of the Middle Corridor, the annual freight capacity of the line has been increased from 1 million tons to 5 million tons. This shows that Azerbaijan is not only increasing its own transit capabilities, but also contributing to the expansion of the infrastructure capabilities of other participants in the route. In other words, the infrastructure projects implemented and financially supported by Azerbaijan serve to increase the capacity and competitiveness of the Middle Corridor as a whole.

Thus, for Baku, the issue is not only about increasing transit revenues. The infrastructure projects implemented by Azerbaijan serve to increase the overall throughput capacity of the Middle Corridor and the competitiveness of the route, as well as expand the access of the participating countries to global markets.

Azerbaijan’s transport strategy is not limited to the East-West direction. The country is also an active participant in the International North-South Transport Corridor, which connects the Indian and Persian Gulf regions with the markets of Northern Europe via Iran, Azerbaijan, and Russia.

The agenda of the SCO summit in Bishkek also shows that transport and logistics issues will play a greater role in the organization’s future development. The new transit map emerging in Eurasia expands the trade opportunities of the SCO countries, accelerates the development of alternative routes, and increases the sustainability of global supply chains.

Azerbaijan’s approach shows that Baku is interested not only in taking advantage of the routes passing through its territory, but also in expanding the logistics capabilities of all participating countries by investing in boosting the infrastructure and throughput capacity of these routes.

As a result, the Bishkek summit once again confirmed that the future and sustainability of the SCO directly depend on the effectiveness of transport and logistics corridors. This new transit map, which is being formed on the Eurasian continent, both strengthens the economic sovereignty of the organization’s countries and turns Central Asia and the South Caucasus into indispensable transit centers of global trade.

Azerbaijan’s position in this new transport architecture is particularly noteworthy. Strengthening the East-West connection through the Middle Corridor and the connection between Northern Europe and South Asia through the North-South Corridor, Azerbaijan is no longer just a transit country, but also one of the main logistics actors connecting various transport directions of Eurasia and making a practical contribution to the development of these routes. This indicates that Azerbaijan’s strategic weight in the regional and global trade system will continue to grow.

As the SCO's economic agenda expands, the need for reliable, diversified, and competitive transport links between Asia and Europe also grows. Azerbaijan's geographical position, modern infrastructure, and active participation in international corridors further increase Baku's strategic weight in this process.

World.title: Azerbaijani oil elevates in price
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 2. The price of Azerbaijan’s Azeri Light crude rose by $4.72, or 5.08%, from the previous level to $97.61 per barrel on a CIF basis at Italy’s Augusta port, a source from the oil market told Trend.

At Türkiye’s Ceyhan port, the price of Azeri Light increased by $5.02, or 5.59%, to $94.74 per barrel on an FOB basis.

The price of Urals crude grew by $5.05, or 7.66%, to $70.98 per barrel.

Meanwhile, the price of Dated Brent crude produced in the North Sea scaled up by $4.32, or 4.82%, to $93.96 per barrel.

Azerbaijan’s 2026 state budget is based on an average oil price of $65 per barrel.

According to Trading Economics, crude oil prices edged closer to $91 a barrel on Wednesday, trading at their highest level in nearly six weeks, after rising for a third straight session. The rise was driven by rising tensions between the U.S. and Iran and concerns that energy flows from the Middle East could be further disrupted.

"The U.S. military has launched new strikes on Iranian positions around the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump said the strikes were in response to Iran's attempts to mine the waterway and an earlier attack on a U.S. military base. Trump also warned of a more extensive response if Iran retaliates.

Iran has already announced that it is targeting U.S. bases in the region and has fired missiles towards Jordan.

Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Iran's bankruptcy is "accelerating." He also noted that 17 million barrels of crude oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, indicating that Iran does not have full control over the strategic waterway," the report said.

World.title: Kazakhstan plans to raise oil refining capacity to 40 million tons per year
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 2. Kazakhstan plans to increase its total oil refining capacity to 40 million tons per year, the Ministry of Energy of Kazakhstan said.

Under the plans, existing oil refineries will be expanded, increasing their combined oil refining capacity from 18 million to 29 million tons per year. In addition, Kazakhstan plans to build a new large-scale oil refinery with a capacity of 10 million tons per year.

The plans are reflected in the Concept for the Development of the Oil Refining Industry for 2025-2040, approved by the government. The main objective of the concept is to significantly increase refining capacity and improve the efficiency of existing oil refineries.

"The development of oil refining is one of the key areas in the transformation of Kazakhstan's oil and gas industry - from a predominantly raw-material model toward the creation of a full production and scientific cycle and an increase in the output of products with high added value," the ministry said.

The concept also envisages increasing the depth of oil refining from 89% to 94%, raising motor fuel production and further developing the petrochemical industry. The quality of petroleum products is also planned to be gradually upgraded from the K4 environmental standard to K5+.

"Kazakhstan is consistently strengthening the development of its oil refining industry, focusing on increasing oil refining volumes, expanding the production of petroleum products and developing products with high added value," the ministry said.

In 2024, oil refining in Kazakhstan amounted to 18.3 million tons, exceeding the planned target by 2.23%, while petroleum product output reached 14.75 million tons.

In 2025, oil refining increased to 18.4 million tons, 4.5% above the plan. Petroleum product production amounted to 15.47 million tons, exceeding the planned target by 6.3%. In 2026, the country plans to produce 15.49 million tons of petroleum products.

World.title: Former Bondi Rescue lifeguard Matt Dee dies
World.content:
Former Bondi Rescue lifeguard and mental health advocate Matt Dee has died, according to a statement posted online by the company he co-founded.

"Matt touched the lives of many, he also did amazing work and he will be deeply missed and forever remembered by those who knew and loved him," the statement, posted on the FTW Revolution Instagram page said.

"Funeral arrangements and details will be shared once they have been finalised."

The statement also included the numbers of mental health and suicide prevention services such as Lifeline and Beyond Blue.

Dee's cause of death has not been publicly confirmed.

Dee became a well-known cast member of the Bondi Rescue reality television series and appeared on the show between 2008 and 2017.

Tributes and messages of support flowed on the Instagram post confirming his death today, including from the official Bondi Lifeguards account and former lifeguard Trent Maxwell, who commented "rest easy brother".

Dee co-founded clothing and events brand FTW Revolution as a suicide prevention resource for young Australians. He would later go on to become an ambassador for the Suicide Prevention Australia (SPA) peak body.

The company said it had raised at least $500,000 for SPA.

"We send our war cry to the government asking why the f---k more is not being done about suicide, Australias [sic] biggest killer for people under 44," Dee said in a LinkedIn post about the company.

" We represent the underdogs in the trenches, the battlers in the dark places. "

Matt Dee featured as a cast member on the reality television series Bondi Rescue for almost a decade. (Supplied: Instagram/FTW_Revolution)

In 2015, Australian big wave surfer Justen "Jughead" Allport said in an interview that Dee sought to offer FTW as an outreach service for young people who may not contact traditional mental illness helplines.

"Matty just wanted kids that were down, that were from poor backgrounds, to connect with something that could help them," he said.

"Matt's just trying to be an alternative for the people who aren't gonna [sic] ring Lifeline. Matt and FTW are about turning negatives into positives."

In 2011, he shared his own experience with mental health and suicide — telling the Sun-Herald about the loss of his brother and sister within a year after battles with mental illness.

Dee's young sister, Rachel Dee, lived with schizophrenia while his older brother Jonathan had bipolar disorder.

''What happened was not their fault,'' he told The Sun-Herald.

''They did their best to manage their illnesses. It wasn't their fault. They had a problem inside their heads.

"It's something we don't understand. How would we know what it's like?''

World.title: Fatal hit-and-run driver thought he had hit animal, court hears
World.content:
A young driver who hit and killed a woman who had been kneeling on a road in Adelaide's north-east has issued an apology in court, saying he could "only imagine the indescribable pain" he had caused.

The court also heard from the victim's sister, who described her overwhelming grief at losing "a remarkable young woman".

Ashton Friend, 20, of Banksia Park, hit international student Samia Malik, who had been kneeling on North East Road at Hillcrest for about four minutes before the crash about 11pm on May 6 last year.

Friend's defence barrister, Jane Abbey KC, told South Australia's District Court the circumstances were "very unusual" and that her client had neither seen Ms Malik nor realised he had hit her when he was driving home from his girlfriend's house.

"He was checking his rear vision, but he did not see her — he should have," Ms Abbey said.

"He was absolutely at a loss about what had just happened. He hadn't been aware that there was something on the road. He heard this noise.

"What he hoped was that it had been an animal, or something like that."

A screenshot of CCTV following the hit-and-run incident in which Samia Malik was killed. (Supplied)

Ms Abbey said Friend's car had sustained "relatively little" damage, which was consistent with his belief he had hit a small animal.

"He did not think he had hit a person. Initially, he just did not realise he had hit a person," she said.

There was no explanation given in court as to why Ms Malik was kneeling on the road.

Driver 'deeply sorry' to family

Ms Abbey said that, within the next two days, Friend saw a news report about what had happened but was in a "state of paralysis" and "just could not reconcile what he had done".

The court heard it was not until a week later that he was identified by police and arrested.

It also heard Friend was not affected by drugs or alcohol, was not speeding at the time, took full responsibility and had pleaded guilty "at the earliest opportunity" to charges of causing death by careless use of a motor vehicle and leaving the scene of an accident after causing death.

North East Road at Hillcrest the day after Ms Malik's death. (ABC News: Lincoln Rothall)

During the hearing, Friend stood in the dock, and read aloud an apology, telling the court he was "deeply sorry" to Ms Malik's family for the loss he had caused, as well as his "actions and inactions" on the night.

"I can only imagine the indescribable pain and trauma I have caused," he said.

"I will have to carry my failures with me for as long as I live."

Friend also told the court he knew no apology could undo what had occurred or bring Ms Malik back, but he would continue to "carry the weight" of what he had done.

"I am deeply sorry for the life that was lost, the grief and the trauma caused to Samia's family and loved ones," he said.

"There is no excuse for my actions, or my failure to act — and I should have acted. I do not place responsibility on anyone else, it is mine alone.

"I take full responsibility for my actions and their consequences. I stand before this court with genuine remorse and a commitment to reflect on, learn from and be accountable for what I have done."

He also apologised to the court and his own family for the "turmoil" he had put them through as a result of the crash.

Victim's family left 'empty'

In a victim impact statement read aloud by prosecutor Frank Niemann, Ms Malik's sister Qudisya Malik told the court her family was grappling with profound grief and heartbreak over their loss.

"Grief has become part of my everyday life and there are moments where the pain feels just as fresh as it did on the day we lost her," she said in the statement.

"Every important milestone reminds us that someone deeply loved is missing. There is always an empty place where Samia should have been.

"Nothing can ever replace Samia. We have lost a daughter, a sister, a friend and a remarkable young woman who had so much life ahead of her.

"Samia will always remain part of our family. She may no longer be physically with us but she continues to live on in our hearts."

Mr Niemann told the court that before Ms Malik was struck, other drivers had swerved around her.

He said a police vehicle which had been travelling some distance behind Friend was able to brake and stop without striking Ms Malik.

He said it took "impressive police work" to find Friend after the crash and that he had not turned himself in, even after he became aware he was the person who had struck Ms Malik.

"The defendant has effectively not presented to police for some time, and waited for them to find him," Mr Niemann said.

Both the prosecution and defence agreed a suspended jail term would be an appropriate penalty when he is sentenced next month.

World.title: Police speak with four men over Sydney Swans scandal
World.content:
Victoria Police detectives have spoken with four Sydney men as part of their sexual assault investigation linked to the Sydney Swans.

In a statement, police confirmed they travelled to NSW this week.

Sexual Crimes Squad detectives spoke with a 26-year-old Randwick man, a 30-year-old Maroubra man, a 25-year-old Randwick man and a 25-year-old Paddington man.

Investigators say the interview process with the four men has now concluded.

The allegations relate to events at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel where it is understood players were joined by several adult entertainers in the early hours of August 17.

Three women subsequently made a report to police.

No-one has been arrested and no charges have been laid.

Authorities say they also spoke to, or will speak with, three men also believed to be in the hotel room, who are being treated solely as witnesses at this time.

The club stood down five players — vice captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordan, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey — for breaching club standards for drinking and bringing women to the hotel in the hours after the team's round 23 clash against Essendon.

Police now believe they have identified all parties who were in the room at the time of the alleged incident.

The investigation into the alleged incident remains ongoing, and Victoria Police said it does not expect to provide any further updates for about eight weeks.

World.title: Judge tells retiring triple murder jury to consider if survivor truthful
World.content:
The presiding judge in a triple murder and attempted murder trial in north Queensland has told a retiring jury to consider if evidence from a man who said he survived the alleged shooting is truthful.

The jury in the trial of Queensland grazier and coal miner Darryl Valroy Young has retired to consider its verdict.

Mr Young, 63, is charged with three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder.

He pleaded not guilty to all charges in the Supreme Court trial in Townsville.

Mr Young pleaded not guilty to three counts of murder and one count of attempted murder. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

The jury retired to consider its verdict on Wednesday after hearing three weeks of evidence and two days of closing addresses from prosecutors and defence lawyers.

Two reserve jurors, who had been with the panel of 12 jurors for the duration of the trial, were discharged.

The trial heard that married couple Mervyn Schwarz and Maree Schwarz and her son Graham Tighe were found dead at the gate of Mr Young's Shannonvale Station at Bogie on August 4, 2022.

Maree (left) and Mervyn Schwarz (middle), and Graham Tighe were found dead outside the gate of the Bogie cattle station. (Supplied/ABC News)

The trial heard from Ross Tighe, Graham Tighe's brother, who told the court he saw the accused shoot his family.

Ross Tighe also told the court that he was shot by Mr Young but that doctors did not remove the projectile from his body.

On Tuesday morning, Mr Young's defence lawyer Anthony Kimmins said Ross Tighe could be the "murderer" and could have "shot himself".

Prosecutor David Nardone dismissed the suggestion on Tuesday afternoon as a "fantasy".

Ross Tighe was called to give evidence as a witness in the trial of Darryl Young. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

In his summing up on Wednesday, Justice Christopher Johnstone told jurors that Mr Kimmins never asked Ross Tighe if he was lying.

"You may recall that it was not suggested in cross-examination of Ross Tighe that any of his evidence was a lie," Justice Johnstone said.

He said the jury must consider if Ross Tighe was truthful.

"Mr Kimmins suggested to you that the evidence that has been led suggests that Ross Tighe was the murderer," he said.

"The prosecution has made many submissions to you about the credibility of Ross Tighe and the evidence which it relies on to support Ross Tighe's version of events as he described them.

" It remains necessary for you to satisfy yourself that he is truthful. "

Justice Johnstone reminded the jury that a doctor who treated Ross Tighe told the trial he believed he would have died from his wound, due to blood loss or infection, if not for medical intervention.

In his closing address, prosecutor David Nardone said Ross Tighe told the truth in his evidence.

Alibi consideration

Justice Johnstone told the jury that if they accepted an alibi claim by Mr Young, he should be found not guilty.

He also said if the jury did not accept Mr Young's alibi that it did not necessarily make him guilty.

"His defence is that he was somewhere else," he said.

" It is for the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Mr Young was at the gate at the time. "

Mr Young said he was not at the gate and did not shoot anybody. (ABC News: Carole Howlett)

On Tuesday afternoon, Mr Nardone recalled evidence of ammunition in Mr Young's home which matched spent rounds found at the scene of the alleged shooting.

The prosecutor also said that wind farm workers identified Mr Young as being at the scene of the alleged shooting about half an hour before it is said to have occurred.

He repeated evidence from two witnesses who said they overheard Mr Young angrily demand a meeting with the family the evening before the alleged shooting.

Defence lawyer Mr Kimmins said Mr Young did not own the ammunition found in his home or at the gate and did not arrange a meeting.

World.title: Another plan unveiled to tackle long-standing issues in Port Augusta
World.content:
Aboriginal leaders and those on the front line of Port Augusta's long-standing crime and violence issues have seen attempts to address it come and go.

As another plan is unveiled, this time a government taskforce, there is optimism but also some frustration over a lack of Indigenous consultation.

Barngarla elder Aunty Linda Dare says crime and violence is on the rise.

"As far as I'm concerned, the state needs to come and sit down with the community, because we are the ones that see it on a day-to-day basis," she said.

Barngarla elder Aunty Linda Dare says crime and violence is on the rise in Port Augusta. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

"They need to come and sit down, have a forum with us so we can put our opinions across to them."

For Kuyani and Adnyamathanha elder Malcolm "Tiger" McKenzie, the lack of political presence in the neighbouring Aboriginal community of Davenport is an issue that needs to be addressed.

He said repeated invitations to visit the community had been ignored.

From alcohol to illicit substances

The introduction of heavy restrictions on alcohol in 2022 was another positive step that those on the front line welcomed.

Restrictions included limits on the volume of takeaway alcohol as well as an ID scan process to ensure those limits were followed.

However, Alinda Hogg, the project coordinator at Stepping Stones – an Aboriginal drug and alcohol service provider – said the problem had shifted over the past two years as methamphetamine use increased.

Alinda Hogg, project coordinator at Stepping Stones, an Aboriginal drug and alcohol service provider. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

She said a colleague told her a client was using methamphetamine as ID was not needed to purchase the substance.

In April this year Port Augusta Council issued a public safety notice, warning residents about the uptick in discarded needles.

Both Ms Hogg and Aunty Linda Dare said methamphetamine was fuelling more crime than alcohol now.

Danger of rhetoric stoking racism

Eli Partridge and Christian Khan, two Indigenous youth advocates, have warned that rhetoric regarding spikes in "crime", "substance abuse" or "anti-social behaviour" can turn into an attack on "young Aboriginal men".

The two 19-year-olds are both part of the Davenport Community Alliance, which was set up in late 2024.

Both say they have lived experience of being profiled, and that it has had a devastating impact on young men.

Youth advocates Eli Partridge and Christian Khan, both 19, have felt racially profiled. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

Mr Partridge says at times he's wished that his skin was lighter.

Mr Khan expressed a similar experience of feeling "ashamed of just walking around".

The pair say there was no easy answer, but praised initiatives like Mangrove Court — particularly as the program involves supporting the family units of young offenders.

"Sit with them, find out why they're doing these things, how we can remove them from that place," Mr Khan said.

History of programs in Pt Augusta

It's not the first attempt to address longstanding issues in Port Augusta.

In 2020 the Port Augusta City Safe Program was axed with the then-council stating that it was not core council business.

The program had run for 11 years, using security officers and a K9 unit to help reduce crime and violence.

Ms Hogg said it was effective at diffusing situations without needing police.

Heavy restrictions were put on alcohol in Port Augusta in 2022. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

"They'd come in and calm things down … [people] didn't feel as threatened … it's not as confrontational with them," she said.

"It was pretty sad to see them go."

Aunty Linda Dare expressed similar sentiments and said there was an immediate increase in violence once the program was discontinued.

"The K9 guy, he was brilliant and I've got to give it to him," she said.

"He actually stopped a lot of fights."

Both elders say measures to address Port Augusta's level of crime need to have measurable KPIs that can be easily reviewed.

Aboriginal elders and those on the front line say violence and crime is on the rise in Port Augusta. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

In 2021 the Port Augusta Responsible Communities (PARC) was established replacing the City Safe Program.

That too lost the support of council before a government changeover in 2022 saw its end.

In 2024 $12 million was allocated for three years, from both the state and federal governments to form the Port Augusta and Davenport Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan.

There has been little detail released as to how the taskforce will function, with representatives from several government departments, the local member and council meeting on Friday to discuss next steps.

Davenport's overgrown sporting field which used to be a place of connection and community. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

The taskforce is designed to complement the work that has already been launched by the state and federal government's Wellbeing Plan.

This includes Mangrove Court, which began in March to address the causes of youth offending.

Breaking down barriers

Looking over the derelict buildings and overgrown sporting grounds of the long-defunct training grounds in Davenport fills Tiger McKenzie with deep sadness.

He fondly remembers how the facility and adjoining football and cricket pitch allowed Indigenous and non-Indigenous people to mingle and connect.

The former training centre and sporting grounds at Davenport have fallen into disrepair since their closure. (ABC News: Stephen Opie)

"They engage … those non-Aboriginal people engage with Aboriginal people to understand Aboriginal people," he said.

"Then they become mates."

Before its closure roughly 15-20 years ago, Mr McKenzie said it was a great meeting place, with teams travelling from Roxby Downs, Leigh Creek and Copley to play sport and socialise.

On nearby dunes people would "light a fire and cook kangaroo".

World.title: 'The Family' serial killings suspects should be named, victims' relatives say
World.content:
Relatives of some of the victims of "The Family" murders are demanding the public release of the long-suppressed names of suspects linked to the case.

Five young males were murdered in South Australia in the late 1970s and early 1980s, in a series of unsolved abductions police have linked to a group known as "The Family".

With the support of other victims' families, Robyn Barnes — the sister of Alan Barnes — is seeking half a million signatures to a public petition to lift 80-year suppression orders on the names of suspects who were allegedly involved.

"One of the points is that we have to prove public interest outweighs the orders, and that's what we're trying to do," Ms Barnes said.

Alan Barnes's body was found beneath the South Para Bridge near Williamstown in June 1979.

Robyn Barnes is the sister of Alan Barnes. (ABC News)

The 17-year-old was last sighted in the presence of two other males the evening before his body was discovered.

The report is considered credible by police, and the two males are known to police.

Four other males — Mark Langley, Neil Muir, Peter Stogneff, Richard Kelvin — were each murdered between 1979 and 1983.

Notorious child killer Bevan Spencer von Einem was convicted of the murder of 15-year-old Richard Kelvin but he was thought to have been connected, alongside "The Family" group, to the brutal murders of the four other young men.

Von Einem died of cancer while in prison in December 2025, and had refused to cooperate with police as they attempted to bring other perpetrators to justice.

"The Family" group, it has been speculated, potentially included members of the state's elite.

Court documents revealed that, at the time, police told the media the five crimes were linked, sexually motivated "serial killings".

Ms Barnes has turned to the public in an effort to show there is support for lifting the decades-old suppression orders.

Richard Kelvin was murdered in 1983. (Supplied: SA Police)

"In many ways, there's quite a few areas where we've gone as far as we can," she said.

"We know we will never, ever see the inside of a courtroom. We're never going to see justice as we know it.

" This is the next best thing we can do for these boys. "

Ms Barnes said she had received strong support from the community on social media, and was optimistic that would translate to signatures.

"I like to believe in the public, I like to believe they agree with what's right," she said.

Bevan Spencer von Einem was jailed for the murder of Richard Kelvin. (ABC News)

Investigation remains open

While Ms Barnes is seeking signatures to her petition to demonstrate public interest, a Supreme Court spokesperson told ABC News a petition was not necessary for a court to consider revoking a suppression order.

"Applications to revoke suppression orders may be made under s 69A(6) of the Evidence Act 1929 (SA) by a range of people specified in s 69A(5), which include the person who sought the order, the parties to the proceedings, media representatives and others," they said.

"A petition is not required under s 69A," they said.

SA Attorney-General Kyam Maher told 891 ABC Adelaide the state government did not object to the suppression orders being lifted, but that it would not apply to the courts to do so.

He said any interested parties could apply for the lifting of a suppression order.

"It's the prosecuting investigating authorities who are in the best place to advise the court about what their ongoing investigations are, and what they need," Mr Maher said.

"We as a government don't have any objection at all to suppression orders being lifted — but, quite rightly, it shouldn't be up to politicians or the government of the day."

Mr Maher said he did not know the names of the individuals whose identities were suppressed, and whether the individuals themselves were still alive.

An SA Police spokesperson urged anyone with information about the murders to contact Crime Stoppers.

"Investigations into the murders of Alan Barnes, Mark Langley, Neil Muir, Peter Stogneff and Richard Kelvin remain open and will remain so until resolved," they said.

World.title: The turquoise home that withstood a torrent
World.content:
When the floodwaters tore through the town of Trishuli in the Nuwakot district in Nepal, most of the valley vanished in minutes.

Homes folded, bridges collapsed and the Trishuli river rose by up to nine metres in just 30 minutes.

But on the second floor of this turquoise home, a family of five stood watching the disaster swallow up their town.

What happened on the day?

An aerial view of the house after it withstood flash floods and a mudslide in Nepal. (Reuters: Francis Mascarenhas)

On the morning the flood hit, the river rose with a speed that left residents little time to react.

Lakshmi Pandey said she was at their shop, about five minutes away from their home, when she realised the flood was coming.

"We ran back as fast as we could because my mother-in-law and my daughter were at home," she said in an interview with The Economic Times, translated by the ABC.

The mother of two told her mother-in-law, "The flood is coming, we need to run".

A surge triggered upstream saw a deluge of ice, rock, mud and debris carve a trail of destruction through the country's valley towns and villages.

Within minutes, streets were underwater.

"The old bridge broke and a huge amount of water suddenly came rushing down from above, and at that point, I realised that we could no longer escape by running outside," she said.

Loading...

Inside the turquoise house close to the riverbank, the mother, her husband, daughter, in-laws and their neighbour remained trapped.

Her son was at school at the time.

They watched from their balcony, standing next to their washing machine, as the flood ripped through the bottom floor of their home.

In a viral video, the family can be seen huddling around the balcony rails in what's been dubbed the "miracle house" and "greenhouse" on social media.

"Water was hitting the house from both sides, and the whole house started shaking; it felt just like the huge shaking we experienced during the 2015 Nepal earthquake," she said.

Loading...

As the houses around them collapsed from the force of the flood, the couple described feeling like there was no chance that they would survive.

"I thought my son would be all alone now, an orphan," the mother said.

"We thought if we survive we will all survive, if we die we will all die."

Her husband, Prakash Pyakurel, recalled thinking "this is the end," deciding the family should stay together for what felt like their last moments while "chanting the God's name."

Waiting to be rescued, the mother said she told herself "we are five people, we should be patient".

Footage circulating on Saturday showed rescue workers using a makeshift bridge to reach the family, with mud seen stuck on the walls slightly below the balcony.

Loading...

The mother said four neighbours risked their own lives and came to rescue them.

"Somehow, they managed to get all of us out safely," she said.

Do you know more or are you affected? Tell us here.

Why is the turquoise house still standing?

The head of engineering at the University of the Sunshine Coast, Adrian McCallum, said it was likely the water was able to flow underneath the house, similar to a traditional Queenslander, lessening loads upon the structure.

"Crucially, the turquoise house appears to be built on rock and constructed of concrete with reinforcing steel," he told the ABC.

The house appears to be protected from the main river flow by a small headland protruding immediately upstream, so this may also have saved it from the main brunt of the flood, he said.

It is thought that a headland protected the house from the full force of the flood. (Reuters: Francis Mascarenhas)

The disaster is believed to have activated when part of a Himalayan glacier broke off and crashed into the river below and triggered flash flooding and a mudslide.

As of Tuesday, the death toll surpassed 1,000 as rescuers deployed heavy machinery, helicopters and excavators to reach thousands still missing for nearly a week.

Hundreds remain stranded at devastated hydropower stations and are the focus of rescue efforts.

Specialised rescue teams from China, India and Nepal have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dig through the ruins of hydropower projects, using excavators to try to rescue the nearly 300 workers trapped inside tunnels.

A drone view shows mud covering properties following a flash flood in Trishuli. (Reuters: Navesh Chitrakar)

Family returns to 'miracle home'

On Monday, the surviving family walked back through their home — that remains standing — to assess the damage.

What had been their town just a few days earlier was now a field of mud.

The mother expressed gratitude that her family, including her son, had been "reborn".

If you want to help support the thousands affected by the crisis, the ABC is supporting the Emergency Action Alliance member charities and their local partners. You can find more information here.

World.title: Telstra outage caused by failure to address well-known network issues
World.content:
Telstra failed to prioritise fixing known vulnerabilities in its systems despite being warned about them months before they triggered a major nationwide outage.

An independent report investigating the July 8 outage, which affected about 45 per cent of all calls and data sessions on Telstra's mobile network and saw hundreds of Triple Zero (000) calls unable to connect, was released by the telco yesterday.

The review by Technology Audit Partners (TAP) found that a lack of oversight and ownership of key elements of the network contributed to the outage, including that two of the telco's key engineers were on mandatory leave at the time it occurred.

It found that the outage began at 2:50am — nearly an hour earlier than Telstra had previously disclosed — and was triggered after a faulty power supply was replaced that then reset a GPS card date to 2006, which then flowed through the rest of the mobile network.

The review said the alarms that would usually alert staff to the error were only monitored during business hours by a "limited number" of people, and a lack of "knowledgeable staff" contributed to the telco taking "several hours to determine the root cause of the outage".

"There were several reasons for this, primarily due to insufficient clarity of responsibility regarding NTP (Network Time Protocol) ownership and support, lack of visibility to the planned event to replace the Melbourne chassis that night, as well as a lack of understanding of the alarms that were the earliest indicators of a problem in the network," it said.

Reform demanded after outage Advocates demand change to how telecommunication companies are regulated and held accountable for outages after Telstra's network failure.

The report also noted that the telco did not treat its timing system as a priority, nor did it treat it as a "high risk function" of the network.

Telstra chief executive Vicki Brady said the company accepts the findings of the report and is working through its recommendations.

"The cause … was consistent with what we said at the time, so it was not due to infrastructure failing, it was due to an undocumented design change in October, and it was due to a software update having not been done on a GPS card," she told a media briefing.

"The overarching finding is that we did not prioritise our timing system inside our networks at the highest level as a critical capability, which is exactly what it should have been.

" That is a miss on our side. We should have had it prioritised at the highest level. "

The company has already reallocated resourcing to the team to improve its capability, Ms Brady added.

A known issue

The report's findings come after the ABC revealed in the days after the July outage that Telstra had been warned for months by federal government agencies and academics that it was vulnerable to the type of error it experienced.

In 2024, Australia's government-run Cyber and Infrastructure Security Centre put out a public alert about how "Australia's critical infrastructure increasingly relies on the delivery of positioning, navigation and timing".

In October last year, another alert from the centre singled out "critical communications assets" as being dependent on these timekeeping systems, including space-based satellites. It reiterated the legal obligations to ensure providers had backups if those systems failed.

A review into Telstra's outage found it began almost an hour earlier than previously disclosed. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

That same month, Telstra staff were working on addressing a timing issue that resulted in one of its clocks in Melbourne losing connectivity multiple times a day to another clock in Sydney, triggering NTP alarms.

"A 'Network at Risk' ticket should have been raised to find the real root cause of the frequent loss of the Sydney source and restore the NTP server back [to] the intended design but this did not happen," the report said.

"At the time of the October 2025 incident, the personnel involved did not recognise the meaning of Melbourne NTP at stratum 5 … this anomaly was observed but not noted and no problem ticket was created for further investigation."

In hindsight, Ms Brady admitted that there "could have been more curiosity" about the incident.

"Particularly looking back in October last year when we did put a design change in to address an issue that didn't end up being documented and was not followed up," she said.

" That is a lesson we've got to take. "

Telstra chief executive Vicki Brady at a press conference following a nationwide Telstra outage 10 July 2026. (ABC News: Julia Andre)

Clear 'preventable failures'

The TAP report also found that there were eight additional Triple Zero calls that were unable to connect during the July outage.

Telstra had previously told a Senate inquiry examining its outage that 604 Triple Zero calls failed.

No guarantee outages won't happen again, Telstra CEO says The national Telstra outage last week was triggered by maintenance work that caused the system's clocks to go back two decades, the telco says.

Of the additional eight missed calls, five did not need assistance or were "misdials", one successfully "camped on" via a different network, one connected after making a subsequent call, and one caller that could not be identified, even after police visited the premises.

Ms Brady said those eight calls had since received the required welfare checks, and stressed that there had been "no adverse outcomes" reported.

"We know how important Triple Zero is, and that's why any time there is an issue we will focus very quickly on making sure we make the changes needed to ensure our processes are even more resilient," Ms Brady said.

In a statement, Communications Minister Anika Wells said she expected Telstra to act on "the findings and recommendations without delay".

"This was an outage that should not have happened, and it caused an extraordinary disruption across the country which impacted people, businesses and transport," she said.

"What this report has unearthed is concerning and clearly shows there have been preventable failures.

"Australians rightly expect to reach Triple Zero when they need it most, and telcos are legally obligated to ensure that connection occurs.

"The industry must learn from its mistakes."

The Australian Communications and Media Authority is still investigating the outage, which could see Telstra fined up to $30 million.

Ms Brady said it was "too early" and the telco had not yet made any budget allowance for any potential financial penalty.

She also confirmed that "a little over" 30,000 customers have shared in roughly $1 million worth of compensation, with most of the compensated customers receiving a $15 credit, processed typically within three days of lodgement.

For small businesses, the amounts paid have been determined on a case-by-case basis with requirements on some to show proof of business impact, Ms Brady said.

World.title: Sydney Swan Riley Bice ‘not a suspect’ in police sexual assault investigation
World.content:
Exclusive SportAFLCrime Sydney Swan Riley Bice ‘not a suspect’ in police sexual assault investigation Christine Lacy September 2, 2026 — 4:32pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Sydney Swan Riley Bice has been cleared of any criminal conduct in the unfolding police investigation into the alleged sexual assault of exotic dancers at a Melbourne hotel last month. A source with knowledge of the Victoria Police inquiry, but not authorised to speak publicly, also confirmed that detectives have finished a round of voluntary interviews with the four other Swans players but revealed some had not taken part in the process. Swans players (from left) Chad Warner, James Jordon, Isaac Heeney, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey have been suspended for the rest of the season. Artwork: Marija Ercegovac The source said Bice, 25, is now being treated as a potential witness in the case, which is now in its third week. The other Swans stars at the centre of the incident – Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey and James Jordon – all remain part of the police investigation.



The developments follow reporting by this masthead of the appointment by the players of different lawyers to represent their diverging interests, with at least three separate counsels now working for the men. The source connected with the investigation said some in the group had declined to provide voluntary accounts of the fateful night at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne last month, police can seek to interview them again at any time. In a statement on Wednesday, Victoria Police confirmed three women had made a report about the night and detectives had this week travelled to Sydney to speak to four people. “That process has now concluded,” the statement read. “Investigators also spoke to or will speak to three men believed to be in the hotel room at the time of the incident, who are being treated solely as witnesses at this time.



“Police now believe they have now identified all parties who were in the room at the time of the alleged incident and are not looking for anyone further.” Riley Bice’s manager and the Sydney Swans refused to comment. More to come Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: ‘Gaping holes’: North Melbourne give reasons for Clarkson’s sacking
World.content:
North Melbourne have sacked coach Alastair Clarkson after four seasons and with a year remaining on his contract citing “gaping holes” in an inconsistent game plan and muddied messages to players. Players were recalled from leave for an emergency meeting on Wednesday morning to be told the coach had been sacked. Loading Clarkson was told of the club’s decision on Tuesday after a post-season consultation period during which North bosses sought the views of the football department and players, two sources confirmed. In a brutally frank press conference, the club said North’s game plan under Clarkson had “gaping holes” in it, that they failed to implement a modern game style, and that there was muddied messages to players.



North’s football manager, Todd Viney, Clarkson’s long-time friend and ally who came to the club with the coach, said the feedback from players was that the more pressure Clarkson felt, the harder he worked and the more confused the messaging became. Club president Sonja Hood and Viney told the press conference at Arden Street on Wednesday that leadership’s view was that the Kangaroos had made progress under Clarkson, but they needed to extract more from a talented group. When asked what kind of coach North Melbourne needed, Hood said, “One that could coach for the modern game.”



Viney said the game plan was inconsistent, and the club needed a coach who would align the team to modern football.



“I think if there was one thing that Clarko did was he tried too hard in trying to fix that, and then therefore what happens is we get into more meetings, more information, and the players at the end of the day become a little bit confused, and we don’t get the cohesion that we need to win more games,” Viney explained. “There’s still parts of our game plan that we haven’t been able to improve in the four years, and that’s some stuff that we need to get right when we talk to the next coach to bring us in line with where the modern game is right at the moment.”



When asked what the playing group’s reaction was to the news, Hood said they were sad.



“They’re also really excited about what could come in the future,” she said.



In a letter to club members, Hood said it had become clear that “Alastair no longer has the belief from enough people at the club that he is the right coach to take this group forward”. “Once we knew that, it felt disrespectful to him to have him coach into 2027, knowing we would not extend him at the end of that,” Hood wrote. Alastair Clarkson is leaving North Melbourne. Getty Images “Our culture among the players, staff and coaches is undeniably strong, but we need a consistently clear and concise on-field strategy to sit alongside that.” Clarkson issued a statement via his management.



“My time as coach of the North Melbourne Football Club has come to an end,” he said. “We set out to stabilise the club and lay the foundations for a return to playing deep in September. “The challenge was a difficult one that I embraced with my whole being. “My family and I have been privileged to be involved in AFL football for over 40 years, but it is now time for a new chapter.”



Clarkson, who coached Hawthorn to four premierships before departing at the end of the 2020 season, has been with the Kangaroos since his appointment in late 2022. The Roos finished 14th this year with nine wins and 14 losses. They had been in the top 10 with eight wins on June 21 but slumped out of finals contention since. It was their highest result under Clarkson after finishes of 17th in his first two years in charge and 16th in 2025. “We asked Alastair to give our club stability and strength and help return us to the top of the AFL ladder,” Hood said.



Related Article AFL 2026 ‘This is on me, not the club’: Alastair Clarkson opens up on the Roos’ plight “Four years later, we have created an environment where our staff and players want to be at our club. This is a testament to the culture Alastair has helped create and the belief that he has built in this group. “Although we have clearly made progress and won more games, we won’t shy away from our desire to want more from this talented group. “We are incredibly grateful to Alastair for the work he’s done over the last four years and we wish him all the very best for his next chapter.” Viney, Clarkson’s longtime lieutenant and friend, will remain at the club and is expected to be part of the coach search process.



North Melbourne players were spotted emerging from the Roos’ facilities at Arden Street after the meeting but would not comment beyond expressing excitement for next season. As previously reported by this masthead, Clarkson signed a five-year deal worth more than $5 million when he agreed to return to his former club and has a contract that essentially guarantees him the full amount of his 2027 contract, according to sources with knowledge of the deal. North Melbourne, who have received the highest amount of variable funding from the AFL of Victorian clubs over the past two years (surpassing St Kilda who had long held that mantle), have been a relatively frugal club since the 2000s. The Roos wiped off their debt and enjoyed repeated financial benefits from their stint of playing home games in Hobart and now Western Australia. External discussion of Clarkson’s position and future has included the fact that Adam Simpson and John Longmire – both Kangaroos playing greats who went on to coach AFL premierships at other clubs – are not presently employed as senior coaches.



Other potential targets could include Corey Enright and Jaymie Graham, who were contenders for the Carlton and Essendon jobs, respectively, before Josh Fraser and Mark McVeigh were appointed by those clubs. In March, Clarkson told this masthead he was all for someone else taking the top job at North Melbourne if they were better placed for a quicker return to premiership contention. “I came back here to help the footy club. [It’s] nothing to do with ego, nothing to do with anything else except repay to North what they gave to me as a young fellow,” he said. North had not guaranteed Clarkson’s position when pressed on whether he would coach in 2027 as contracted. Western Bulldogs coach Luke Beveridge was shocked when he was told of Clarkson’s fate midway through his press conference on Wednesday.



Related Article AFL 2026 Clarkson’s clause: Frugal Roos would face huge payout if they axed coach early “Really?” Beveridge said. “Jeez.” Beveridge served as an assistant coach under Clarkson at Hawthorn in 2012-14 when the Hawks won two flags and were narrowly beaten by Sydney in a grand final. The Dogs coach said the constant scrutiny on senior coaches right from the start of their tenure was “disconcerting”, even if he accepted it came with the territory. “The difficult thing with what we’re all doing is it’s a different culture now in our code,” Beveridge said.



“We’ve almost become like the EPL where senior coaches’ tenure and your own coaching mortality is speculated about a lot more than it used to be, as opposed to say the NFL, where you can have a winning season and that’s considered a success. “What I’m concerned about is the next generation of senior coaches. Do they actually really want to put them in the situation where, from the start of their tenure, their vocational sustainability is speculated upon? It’s not a nice place to live.” Beveridge paid tribute to Clarkson’s coaching career. “Clarko’s been an amazing coach, amazing custodian of the game, and obviously really outspoken, and someone who’s pushed his own opinions to make the game better,” Beveridge said. Keep up to date with the best AFL coverage in the country.

World.title: Jail time for man who made deepfake images of schoolgirls
World.content:
NationalQueenslandCrime Jail time for man who made deepfake images of schoolgirls Andrew Stafford and Rex Martinich September 2, 2026 — 4:22pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A mother has revealed her anguish over how and when to tell her young daughter she had been targeted by a deepfake image creator who distributed sexualised pictures. A string of women and schoolgirls shared their stories in court, after AI-rendered nudes or sexualised pictures were emailed by former software developer Antonio Rotondo. One took immediate security precautions in their home after discovering the images, while others spoke of the costs of psychological counselling and the stress of the legal process. Rotondo represented himself at trial after pleading not guilty. Dan Peled “What frightens me is knowing that an ordinary photograph can be taken out of my control and transformed into sexual material without my consent,” a victim said.



Rotondo was sentenced to jail on Wednesday after a Brisbane jury found him guilty of 11 counts of stalking. He was also found guilty of five counts of distributing intimate images and one count of distributing child exploitation material involving an image of a 13-year-old girl modified to be sexually “degrading”. The 13-year-old’s mother was among the heartbreaking victim impact statements shared in Brisbane District Court on Wednesday, detailing the toll of being targeted by the 56-year-old. Her teenager has not seen the offensive image. But the mother now feels burdened with keeping that secret and wrestles with how to best tell her about the crime when she was old enough. Rotondo had downloaded public images of female staff and students from a prestigious Queensland school and models who had taken part in a fashion show.



He modified the images to include nudity or sexualised elements using an AI deepfake program, emailing them to the administrators of multiple schools and the fashion event in September 2023. Victims on Wednesday said it impacted not only themselves but also their families. They spoke of feeling humiliated and violated on what were meant to be nights of celebration and personal pride. One said she did not blame the technology, but the people who misused it. “I do not want to be afraid of photography, being photographed or sharing photographs,” she wrote. “Being visible is an important part of my life, my work and the way I express myself.”



Rotondo, who represented himself at trial after pleading not guilty, argued on sentence that he should have faced only two charges, as he only distributed two emails. He also claimed his conduct was not criminal at the time he engaged in it. But Judge John Allen told Rotondo his clear lack of remorse and insight into his offending meant he had to consider other means of deterrence. “It’s a common feature of the victim impact statements that the effects of your offending continue to this day,” he said. Allen, however, found the images fell short of the type of extreme depravity often the subject of such charges.



Rotondo was sentenced to two years in jail. A jury had found Rotondo guilty on Tuesday following a six-day trial. AAP Get alerts on significant breaking news as happens.

World.title: Chalmers backs assault on big tech as Contos sounds alarm on manosphere
World.content:
PoliticsFederalSocial media Chalmers backs assault on big tech as Contos sounds alarm on manosphere Brittany Busch September 2, 2026 — 4:22pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Treasurer Jim Chalmers backs a crackdown on social media algorithms serving “rubbish” to children, as consent advocate Chanel Contos urges the government to better protect young boys from being sucked into the online manosphere. Chalmers became the latest cabinet minister to weigh in on the persistent dangers posed by harmful social media content on Wednesday, after Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek last weekend sounded the alarm on the prevalence of sexual choking in online pornography. Treasurer Jim Chalmers said algorithms were feeding “rubbish” to kids online. Alex Ellinghausen “I find it really disturbing the rubbish that is fed to our kids, and to our population more broadly, with these algorithms,” Chalmers said on Wednesday. “It’s self-evident that social media, and particularly the way these social media algorithms work, are not doing us a lot of good.” Algorithms push content into users’ social media feeds based on their online activity and personal data. Advocates like Contos are calling for default feeds to be algorithm-free.



Labor is strengthening its attack on big tech after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese flagged online safety as a key platform for a third term, with cabinet considering mandating an algorithm opt-out function in its impending digital duty of care reforms. Global momentum to regulate big tech is building after Australia’s teen social media ban, the European Union’s crackdown on algorithms, and Meta’s landmark $25 billion settlement in the United States that also extracted promises from the tech giant to limit its appeal to children. Chanel Contos at the press club on Wednesday afternoon. Alex Ellinghausen But reform has proven difficult. Many Australian teens remain on social media, and in Europe, tech companies complied with an opt-out mandate, but disincentivised uptake by limiting other features, sparking a lawsuit in the Netherlands and an investigation by Ireland’s tech regulator. Nationals leader Matt Canavan agreed online content was toxic, but blamed the “feminisation of our curriculum” for driving young boys towards it.



“They’re sick and tired of getting lectures about how bad men are at school, and so they go to other places,” Canavan told Nine’s Today. “They’re sick and tired of the feminisation of our curriculum and the lack of direction and leadership that they’re given. Maybe we should look at getting more male teachers in,” he said, adding boys felt patronised, not cherished, at school. Nationals leader Matt Canavan. Alex Ellinghausen Contos, who shot to national prominence in 2021 by documenting sexual violence in Sydney schools and successfully campaigned to mandate annual consent education in schools, said the consent curriculum was about promoting healthy intimacy. “It is absolutely not an attack on men or boys at all. It’s to make their sex lives happier and healthier and their relationships better,” the Teach Us Consent chief executive said when asked about Canavan’s comments following a National Press Club address in Canberra on Wednesday.



“But of course, we also need to hold all of that while acknowledging that sexual violence is majority perpetrated by boys and men, and that shouldn’t be shameful for the individual, but it should mean that they’re willing to be part of a system to change that statistic.” Related Article Exclusive

Privacy Albanese attacks algorithm but no ban for ‘pervert glasses’ in privacy overhaul Greens communications spokeswoman Sarah Hanson-Young accused Canavan of stoking a culture war and criticised him for blaming female teachers for boys behaving badly. “Senator Canavan has shown himself to be a fool when talking about these issues,” she told reporters in Canberra. The Greens have backed Contos’ call for the government to go further on reining in social media by requiring algorithms to be opt-in.



In her speech, Contos said algorithms were preying on the insecurities of boys, funnelling them from lifestyle and dating advice into misogynistic content. She said research indicated that it took just 23 minutes for a new male social media profile to be served up misogynistic content, as teen boys overtake men as the most likely to perpetrate child sexual abuse. Related Article Opinion

Cyber bullying If we’re serious about social cohesion, these big tech hate machines must be reined in Chanel Contos Founder of Teach Us Consent “We owe it to our boys and young men to not hand-deliver them to an industry that takes their valid concerns, fuels the fire with unfounded grievance, and then extracts their strong emotions for profit,” she said. Contos is calling for social media feeds to be limited to the pages deliberately followed by users and presented chronologically, with the option to switch on an algorithm to feed them curated suggested content. Contos said social media companies’ business model was to push content that would keep eyes on screens longer, rather than what people would choose to see.



“Our screen time fills big tech’s pockets, and the more outraged we are, the more time we spend on their screens,” she said. Contos conceded people would still choose to use the social media algorithm, but said it was about giving them a choice. “As a society, we put parameters around other addictive substances like gambling, alcohol, and smoking, and people still do those things,” she said. “But we’re trying to make it safer.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: Chalmers admits tax reforms helped drag down house prices
World.content:
Breaking PoliticsFederalAustralian economy Chalmers admits tax reforms helped drag down house prices Shane Wright Updated September 2, 2026 — 4:21pm ,first published 11:58am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Treasurer Jim Chalmers has admitted the government’s budget overhaul of property-tax concessions is contributing to the fall in home values as a new snapshot of the economy shows cash-pressed consumers are splurging on EVs but giving up their overseas holiday plans. As private sector economists forecast property values to continue falling through the rest of this year and well into 2027, Chalmers said higher interest rates and the turmoil facing the economy from the war in Iran were also adding to downward pressure on home prices. The June quarter national accounts, released on Wednesday, showed the economy expanded by 0.4 per cent, taking annual growth down from 2.5 per cent to 2.1 per cent. Half of the growth was due to a lift in household spending with most of that coming through a record purchase of new cars.



The bureau noted that there was a record sale of EVs and hybrids as people sought to avoid the surge in oil prices caused by the US’s war against Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Spending on transport actually fell, due to the lift in pump prices. The surge in EV purchases has continued into the current quarter. Figures from the Electric Vehicle Council covering Tesla and Polestar showed another rise in purchases through August to be 91 per cent up on the same period last year. It said other areas of discretionary spending were “subdued” due to rising cost-of-living pressures. This was most evident with a sharp drop in international tourism, as Australians abandoned their northern-summer plans for travel to Europe and the United States. People buying EVs and hybrids was a major contributor to GDP growth in the June quarter. Bloomberg Essential spending also fell, particularly on electricity and gas caused by the warmer-than-normal winter.



Home construction continues to grow, up by 1.6 per cent in the quarter to be 5.8 per cent stronger over the past year to be at its highest level since early 2019. But there are doubts how much longer the lift in new-home builds can continue given the slowdown in the overall property market, the increase in the cost of construction – which is partly due to the surge in oil prices and strong demand – and the government’s budget tax measures. Chalmers, who noted Australia remained equal with the US as one of the fastest-growing economies in the world, described the overall result as “robust” given the headwinds facing the economy. Pressed on forecasts by the Commonwealth Bank that property prices could fall by as much as 13 per cent in Sydney, Chalmers said the budget changes in areas such as negative gearing and capital gains tax were weighing on the market along with other factors. “We’ve said on a number of occasions that that is not the only factor. It’s a factor but not the only factor, and the evidence of that,” he said.



“What is too frequently ignored, is that house prices and auction clearance rates were softening before the budget, and that’s because of movements in interest rates and developments in the economy more broadly.” Related Article Property prices $40,000 wiped off the value of the average house over winter Shadow treasurer Tim Wilson accused Chalmers of deliberately trying to tank the property market. “This was by design. This is the economy that Labor has designed,” he told News24. The bureau said there was also growth due to public demand and net trade thanks to a lift in exports. It was the first positive contribution to growth from the trade sector since late 2023.



Private investment, which was a key factor in the March quarter, was flat in the June quarter due to a sharp fall in the imports of data processing equipment used in new data centres. But business investment was flat despite firms continuing to construct new buildings for data centres. There was also a lift in engineering construction for new renewable and mining projects. There continued to be concerning signs about the nation’s economic foundations. Productivity was flat in the quarter to be down by 0.2 per cent over the full year. Unit labour costs jumped by 0.9 per cent in the quarter to be 0.5 per cent higher since June last year. The Commonwealth Bank’s head of Australian economics, Belinda Allen, is one who expects the overall economy to slow as investment in new homes ebbs as interest rate increases bite and property prices ease. “But this will not be enough to stop another interest rate hike from the RBA in November given recent inflation data indicating upside risks have materialised,” she said.



Sunny Nguyen, Moody’s Analytics head of Australia economics, said the figures confirmed that higher interest are biting into households’ spending plans. She said while household nominal income grew by 1.5 per cent in the quarter, they had only spent 0.4 per cent of it. “In the March quarter, they drew on savings buffers to cover essentials; now they are rebuilding them,” she said. EY Australia chief economist Cherelle Murphy said the economy’s long-term problems had been exposed by the figures. “Australia’s economy is caught between resilient demand and weak supply-side performance. These national accounts will do little to ease the Reserve Bank’s concerns about the inflation outlook, and we continue to expect that another rate rise will soon be delivered,” she said.
